title: No ASIC's DISC_OUT reaches the FPGA, yet the V3 question to the ASIC designer asks only about the top chips.
what: The bottom chips drive DISC_OUT on pins 3/5, which are no-connect on FPGA-LDO A and the router and have no Frontend line; V3 cut the top chips' DISC_OUT completely. So the system cannot read DISC_OUT from any of the eight chips. The ASIC designer's pin sheet lists DISC_OUT as an output whose termination is undecided. The V3 record asks "is DISC_OUT needed from the top chips?", but the real question is whether it is needed at all, because adding it later means new lines on the Frontend, FPGA-LDO A and the router.
where: ASIC pins 3 (DISC_OUT(2), U01_BCD2) and 5 (DISC_OUT, U01_BCD1) on both V3 boards; top chips' pads on T_DISC_OUT / T_DISC_OUT(2) only; FPGA-LDO A / router J3/J4 pins 3/5 unconnected.
evidence: W/a review working file (not published) "output reaches no FPGA" for DISC_OUT on both ports and both options; V3 dumps: T_DISC_OUT nets have one pad each. ASIC_REFERENCE.md section 2: DISC_OUT appears in E3, E4 leaves its termination undecided. 08 V3 report question list.
source: ASIC designer's Pins sheet; ASIC_REFERENCE.md section 2.
consequence: If DISC_OUT turns out to be a needed status or safety output, the boards to be ordered cannot see it from any chip.
suggested_action: Ask the ASIC designer whether DISC_OUT is needed from any chip, and how it should be terminated if not read, before the Frontend and FPGA-LDO A are ordered.
v2note: With the ASIC boards V4, no chip's DISC_OUT reaches the FPGA, and there is no longer room to add it. All 80 J3/J4 pins now carry nets because V3's spares 2/4/6/8/24/58 carry far-chip lines, so the far chips' bare DISC_OUT pads need a new ASIC pin map unless the ASIC designer allows the shared pins 3/5 he originally drew; and pin map V6 as planned uses 12 of the 15 spare Frontend–FPGA-LDO contacts, leaving 3 (1 with SYS-10) for the near chips' 4 DISC_OUT lines per stack. The designer's DISC_OUT answer is therefore needed before pin map V6 is frozen; if the answer is "needed", V6 must reserve contacts, for example by tying the far boards' SPI_CLK/SPI_LATCH to the near boards' lines, which frees 4. See SYS-63. Second check: the higher severity is upheld. All numbers hold. Both V4 boards use all 80 J3 pins. T_DISC_OUT and T_DISC_OUT(2) are one-pad nets with no copper. The near chips' DISC_OUT reach pins 3/5, which are unconnected on FPGA-LDO A and the router. Each J1/J2 joint has 15 spare contacts. V6 adds 12, leaving 3, or 1 with SYS-10's enable and power-good, for 4 lines. The answer gates the V6 freeze, which is major on the scale. Need is unlikely: the designer calls DISC_OUT a test pin he may ground.

title: Unkeyed DF40 pairs let an ASIC board mate rotated 180 degrees, putting +/-10 V onto ASIC clock and data pins.
what: Hirose states the DF40 connector is not polarized, and no head board has a key, hole, standoff or an orientation mark that stays visible after mating (the Frontend has no silkscreen; the LDO and ASIC boards have only pin-1 triangles, hidden under the mated connector). A rotated Frontend cannot mate in a full stack, because its bottom parts sit over the LDO J3 (Option B: J5) header and it overlaps the ASIC board or router in the same 1.5 mm plane, so it rests at least 1.6 mm high and its contacts never touch. The real exposure is ASIC boards on the LDO underside connector J4 (router J4 on Option B) and ASIC boards stacked on ASIC boards, where nothing stops a rotated fit; on LDO A J4 only about 0.1-0.3 mm of 1206 capacitor height is in the way, less than the 0.45 mm engagement. A partly built stack (a Frontend fitted before the J3 ASIC board, or the Option B LDO board without its router) is also exposed.
where: ASIC board J3/J4 on FPGA-LDO A J4 (bottom), on router J4, and ASIC board on ASIC board; also LDO A J3 and Frontend J1/J2 on LDO J1/J2 in a partly built stack. Nets: LDO /ASIC_VDD10 (U9 LT3042, +10 V), /ASIC_VSS10 (U10 LT3094, -10 V), /ASIC_DVDD; ASIC board /AGND, /DGND.
evidence: Rotation maps 80-pin pin n to 81-n and Frontend Jx pin n to LDO other-J pin 71-n, re-derived from pad coordinates in exports/*/connectors.csv. Rotated ASIC board on LDO A J4 or router J4: LDO 36 ASIC_VDD10 to ASIC pin 45 CLK32MHZ, 54 ASIC_VSS10 to 27 D<4>(2), 34 ASIC_DVDD to 47 SYNC, 38 VDD_DRIVER to 43 D<5>, 1 VDD_CGEN to 80 T_D<1>; ASIC AGND pins 42/44 and DGND pins 46/48 land on LDO J4.39 ASIC1_DATA7, J4.37 ASIC1_DATA8, J4.35 ASIC1_READ and J4.33 ASIC2_DATA1 (LDO J4 mates ASIC J4; ASIC J3 and J4 carry the same nets). Rotated Frontend: FE J2.68-70 VIN_3V3 to LDO J1.3/2/1 (ASIC8_READ, BOARD3_CLK, ASIC6_DATA1); none of the 14 FE GND pins meets a ground. Outlines from pcbnew, LDO A frame: rotated Frontend y 110.93-136.35 against the ASIC board on J3 at y 100.05-117.08 (about 6.2 mm overlap); Option B rotated Frontend y 116.74-142.16 against the router at y 110.31-122.94; rotated ASIC board on J3 y 109.94-126.98 overlaps a fitted Frontend by about 9.3 mm. Rotated Frontend: 13-26 bottom parts (C59, C42, C13, C102, U10 and others) over the LDO A J3 header; C59 1.25 mm + header 1.14 mm = 2.39 mm in a 1.5 mm gap (capacitor heights nominal, from memory). All mated pairs are 1.5 mm DF40C(51). Rotated ASIC on LDO A J4 faces C902, C1002 (CL31A226KAHNNNE 1206), U9 and U10 (heights from memory). Markings: Frontend has 6 gr_text items, all on Cmts.User; JLC_ORDER_NOTES.txt line 12 'no text on the board'. board_stats: NPTH 0 on all head boards.
source: Hirose DF40 Series catalog (Feb. 2024 and earlier editions), receptacle drawing note 4 (p4) and header drawing note 5 (p10): connector not polarized; p1: 0.45 mm effective mating length at 1.5 mm stacking, 0.33 mm self-alignment; p10: header height 1.14 +/-0.15 mm. https://www.hirose.com/product/series/DF40?lang=en (document fetch returned 403; a saved copy was read).
consequence: A rotated ASIC board puts +10 V and -10 V onto ASIC clock and data pins and leaves its grounds on FPGA data lines, which would likely destroy the scarce wire-bonded ASICs at first power-up. On LDO A J4 a forced rotated fit also presses the die area onto the LDO capacitors.
suggested_action: Before ordering, decide on a physical key for the ASIC-board DF40 pairs (an outline tab or standoff that collides when rotated) and add an orientation mark visible after mating on the LDO, router, Frontend and ASIC boards. Add an orientation check to the assembly and bring-up steps.

title: Option B cannot carry pin map V6: J5 would need at least 132 contacts, the DF40 series stops at 120, and the 5.3 mm router/LDO-board overlap has no room for a second connector.
what: V6 adds 6 lines per ASIC port. J5 would then carry 120 signals plus the 9 ASIC rails and 3 returns: 132 contacts against its 120/120. Hirose makes the DF40 only up to 120 positions, and J5 is already that part, so the 'larger DF40' option in SYS-06 does not exist. The router and LDO board overlap only in a 27.9 x 5.3 mm band, and J5 fills it. A second connector therefore needs new outlines on both boards and a new stack fit.
where: Option B router V2: J5 DF40C-120DS (bottom, 99.783, 120.2), outline y 110.315-122.935. LDO board V2: J5 DF40C-120DP (top), outline y 117.634-152.935. Both boards span x 85.833-113.733. As on Option A, router J3/J4 pins 2/4/6/8/24/58 and the 15 LDO board J1/J2 spares are unconnected.
evidence: J5 pin map V4: 108 signals, 9 rails, GND 3/65 and AGND 62, 120 of 120 (the router and LDO board connectors.csv agree). V6: 108 + 12 = 120 signals, so 132 contacts with today's 3 returns, or about 144 at the Frontend J1/J2 ratio of 7 GND per 70 contacts. Overlap = 122.935 - 117.634 = 5.30 mm. The J5 receptacle is 26.6 mm long in the 27.9 mm width (0.65 mm spare at each end) and 3.38 mm deep at y 120.2, leaving 0.88 mm above and 1.05 mm below. Every DF40 receptacle is 3.38 mm deep.
source: Hirose DF40 Series catalog, Feb. 2024 edition (page footer Dec. 1, 2024): p. 6 lists 10-100 and 120 positions; p. 8 gives DF40C-120DS at 26.6 mm long, 3.38 mm deep; p. 14 gives DF40C-120DP at 25.52 mm. Distributor copy read at https://doc.7-el.ru/d/df40.pdf; the Hirose page https://www.hirose.com/en/product/series/DF40 returned 403. Project files: inputs/ldo_b/V2_record/J5_pin_map_V4.csv; exports/ldo_b_router and exports/ldo_b_ldo connectors.csv and board.json.
consequence: Under V6, Option B cannot deliver the far chips' READ and DATA8/7/6/2 (ASIC4 and ASIC8) or DATA6 (ASIC3 and ASIC7). Keeping Option B means redesigning both boards, the J5 interface and the stack fit.
suggested_action: Decide now to drop or freeze Option B and spend the V6 effort on Option A only. If Option B must stay, budget a second board-to-board connector, a larger overlap and a new fit test.

title: High-load stacks reach the 637 mA port current limit on a 1.8 m cable with 30-32 AWG or thinner +5 V wire.
what: Each stack (Frontend, FPGA-LDO board and four ASIC boards) gets all its power through pin 19 of its Micro-HDMI cable, a single +5 V wire. The Frontend buck U16 draws close to constant power, so when the cable voltage drops its current rises. With a perfect cable the high-load case needs about 0.55-0.58 A, below the port switch's 637 mA minimum limit, but once the cable loop resistance passes about 0.9-1.3 ohm (30-32 AWG at 1.8 m) it reaches that limit, and at 34-36 AWG there is no usable operating point. The expected load works on every gauge; the Frontend power has never been estimated with Vivado/XPE and the chosen cable's wire gauge is unknown, so a power estimate and a measured cable loop resistance are needed.
where: HDMI Extension Board U701-U708 (TPS2553DBVR, R711-R718 37.4k) OUT -> PORT1_5V..PORT8_5V -> J610-J617 pin 19; cable +5 V wire; Frontend J3.19 -> VIN_5V -> U16 MPM3833C (IN 13/14, EN 4) -> VIN_3V3 -> every Frontend regulator and J2.68-70 to the FPGA-LDO board (its only supply input). Return on pins 4/7/10/13/16 and the shell.
evidence: TPS2553 limit with 37.4k (eq. 1-3): 636.6 / 696.0 / 763.6 mA min/typ/max (about 630 mA min with a 1 % resistor); rDS(on) DBV 85 mOhm typ, 135 mOhm max over temperature. Load: inputs/hdmi/power_estimate/START_HERE.md section 1 gives 1.2 W / 2.4 W at VIN_3V3, which already include 0.13 / 0.30 A for the LDO/ASIC boards (0.30 A is the DF40 contact rating, not an estimate); a review working file (not published) gives 1.45 W expected and 2.79 W high at 5 V, about 5 % above the record. Perfect cable, high case: 0.55-0.58 A. Re-run models at 1.8 m (a review working file (not published), a review working file (not published), a review working file (not published)), high case: 28 AWG 575-625 mA; 30 AWG 594-654 mA; 32 AWG 631-716 mA; 34 AWG 0.72-0.95 A (past the minimum and typical limits) or no solution; 36 AWG no solution. Loop resistance at which the high case reaches 637 mA: 0.90-1.32 Ohm. Expected case at 36 AWG: 362-394 mA, 3.7-4.0 V at U16, which needs about 3.41 V; a 36 AWG loop delivers at most about 1.9 W, about 30 % over the expected load. The high case is a pessimistic envelope (VCCINT 0.4 A, every stimulator at full current).
source: TI TPS2553 datasheet SLVS841G (rev. Oct 2026), sec. 6.5 p.6-7 and sec. 8.5.1 eq. 1-3 p.16-17, https://www.ti.com/lit/ds/symlink/tps2553.pdf; MPS MPM3833C Rev 1.0, p.4 (UVLO 2.3-2.75 V rising, 400 mV hysteresis, dropout resistance 130 mOhm), https://www.monolithicpower.com/en/mpm3833c.html; copper resistance per AWG from standard tables; engineering judgement. The 0.8 A connector contact rating comes from distributor data and was not checked against the Molex datasheet.
consequence: In the high case the port switch goes into current limit or cycles, VIN_5V falls toward U16's undervoltage lockout, and the Frontend and the LDO/ASIC rails brown out or reset. Slim cables, which the 9.86 mm port pitch pushes toward, make this more likely.
suggested_action: Get a Vivado report_power or XPE estimate for the Frontend and measure the pin-19 plus return loop resistance of the chosen cable; accept only cables below about 0.9 Ohm loop. If the high case is real, cut the stack load rather than raise the limit (30.1k gives 794 mA min but 936 mA max, above the 0.8 A contact rating).

title: The FPGA cannot switch or monitor the ASIC rails or +/-12 V converter; they are on whenever the cable is live.
what: On the FPGA-LDO boards the shared enable for all nine ASIC regulators and the LT3582 +/-12 V converter is only a resistor and capacitor from VIN_3V3, and VIN_3V3 itself is always on once the cable is powered. No enable signal comes from the FPGA and no power-good (a regulator's 'output is in range' signal) goes back, so the FPGA cannot hold off, sequence, watch or shut down the ASIC supplies, and swapping an ASIC board means pulling the cable or hot-plugging. The back-powering at start-up claimed in the original does not happen: the ASIC rails rise about 15-22 ms after VIN_3V3, well after the FPGA's 1.5 V I/O bank (about 3 ms), while the FPGA pins are still undriven. Power-down order is not settled by the files and needs a scope capture; the open point is whether the ASIC designer's still-unknown sequencing and pin limits require FPGA control, which is cheap to add only before ordering.
where: FPGA-LDO A and Option B LDO board: R1 (10k to /VIN_3V3), C3 (4.7 uF), /EN_ASIC_RAILS to U1 (LT3582-12) pin 8 SHDN and U2-U10 EN; R19 (10k, /CHIP_RESET_SHARED J2.58 to /ASIC_DVDD); PG pins of U2, U6, U8, U9, U10 unconnected. Frontend: U16 (VIN_3V3, EN on VIN_5V), U2 PG_CORE_1V0 to U4 EN (VCCO_1V5), U1 ball C9. Spare joint pins J1.29-33, 35-37, 39, 43, 45, 47, 49 and J2.40/42 on Frontend and LDO boards. HDMI board: PORT_ENABLE from U700 pin 13 to U701-U708 EN.
evidence: exports/ldo_a/netlist.xml and exports/ldo_b_ldo/netlist.xml: /EN_ASIC_RAILS = R1.2, C3.1, TP4, U1.8 SHDN, U2-U10 EN or EN/UV; C3 CL10A475KP8NNNC. 'EN_ASIC_RAILS' appears 0 times in every connectors.csv. exports/frontend/netlist.xml: U16 EN = VIN_5V; U2 EN = VIN_3V3; U2 PG = PG_CORE_1V0 to U4 EN; FPGA_PUDC_B tied to VCCO_1V5 through R25 470R, so FPGA I/O stay 3-stated with pull-ups off until configuration. Timing: enable node tau = (10k || 125k, the four TPS7A20 500k pulldowns) x 4.7 uF = 43.5 ms, final 3.06 V; it crosses 0.9 V (TPS7A20 VEN(HI) max) at 15.2 ms and 1.24 V (LT3042 typical) at 22.7 ms; even at VEN(LOW) 0.3 V plus 750 us start-up, DVDD is up about 5 ms after VIN_3V3. VCCO_1V5 is up about 2.7 ms after VIN_3V3 (MPM3833C 1.3 ms soft-start, 100 us PG delay). R19 can inject at most 1.5 V / 10k = 0.15 mA, against the DS181 10 mA clamp-current limit. Capacitance: ASIC_DVDD 2.0 uF on the LDO board (ASIC boards add unvalued C7-C14), VCCO_1V5 about 113 uF. STIM_EN_SHARED (Frontend U1.J6, J2.63) has R2 10k to GND on the LDO board, so stimulation enable defaults low. exports/hdmi/netlist.xml: PORT_ENABLE = U700.13 PG and U701-U708 pin 3.
source: TI TPS7A20 datasheet SBVS338H, electrical characteristics (VEN(HI) 0.9 V, VEN(LOW) 0.3 V, tSTR 750/1150 us) and pin table (500k EN pulldown); ADI LT3042 datasheet, EN/UV rising threshold 1.18/1.24/1.32 V, https://www.analog.com/en/products/lt3042.html; MPS MPM3833C datasheet Rev 1.0 (soft-start 1.3 ms, PG delay 100 us); AMD DS181 Artix-7 data sheet v1.27.1, Tables 1-2 (I/O input voltage to VCCO + 0.55 V, 10 mA clamp current in a powered or unpowered bank, recommended power-on order); inputs/asic/ASIC_Reference/ASIC_REFERENCE.md U02/U03/U05/U07 (sequencing, powered-off pin limits and reset behaviour unresolved); engineering judgement.
consequence: The FPGA cannot sequence the ASICs, keep them off during FPGA bring-up, shut down the +/-12 V converter or react to a failed rail. If the ASIC turns out to need a set power order, adding control after ordering changes the J1/J2 contract on both the Frontend and the LDO board; meanwhile ASIC boards can only be changed with the cable unplugged or by hot-plugging onto live rails.
suggested_action: Get the ASIC power-up and power-down order and powered-off pin limits from the ASIC designer, and decide before ordering whether the FPGA gates the rails; if so, route a Frontend-driven enable on a spare pin (for example J1.29) to EN_ASIC_RAILS with R1 as a pull-down and return a wired-OR power-good. If not, write 'cable unplugged before any DF40 is mated or unmated' into the bring-up procedure and capture the power-down order on a scope.
verification: Upheld after a third independent check
v2note: SYS-10's 2-contact enable/power-good fix has to be reserved during the pin map V6 allocation. V6 as traced takes 12 of the 15 spare Frontend-to-FPGA-LDO contacts (J1.29-33, 35-37, 39, 43, 45, 47, 49, J2.40, J2.42) and leaves 3: enough for enable and power-good, but not for the near chips' 4 DISC_OUT lines, which fit only if the FPGA-LDO board joins the top chips' SPI_CLK/SPI_LATCH (pins 72/70) to the near board's shared ones (63/61); V6 would then need 8 contacts instead of 12. The power-good half also needs regulator changes: PGFB is tied to IN on all five LT3042/LT3094 (U2, U6, U8, U9, U10), which the data sheets say disables power good, and the four TPS7A2015 rails (VDD_ADC, VDD_DRIVER, DVDD, VDD_CGEN) and the LT3582-12 have no PG pin, so a wired PG line reports no rail as built and at most 5 of the 9 rails even after PGFB dividers are added.

title: Each port's 44 chip outputs return through two DGND contacts, and the far chips' outputs return through the REF_VDD and VDD_DRIVER planes, AGND contacts 42/44 and NT1.
what: Each 80-pin port has AGND only on pins 42/44 and DGND only on 46/48. With two real boards stacked, the 44 outputs of four chips return through the two DGND contacts at the FPGA-LDO joint, and the far board's 22 outputs also cross a second joint with the same four returns. On the far (top) board those outputs, including both returned CLK32MHZ clocks, run 4-7.5 mm on In4 between the REF_VDD plane (In3) and the VDD10/VDD_DRIVER plane (In5). Their return current reaches ground mainly through rail capacitors that go to AGND (and plane-to-plane capacitance), then leaves the stack on AGND pins 42/44 and crosses to GND at NT1 on the FPGA-LDO board, through the reference and analog ground of every chip in the port. SYS-41 asked that the second board keep clock lanes on a DGND-referenced layer; V3 does not. The six spare pins 2/4/6/8/24/58 are now nets on both V3 boards but no-connect on FPGA-LDO A and the router, so using them as extra grounds later needs an FPGA-LDO change. The files cannot show how large the effect is.
where: V3 top board In4: T_CLK32MHZ 5.06 mm, T_CLK32MHZ(2) 6.66 mm, T_D<1..8>, T_D<1..8>(2), T_READ, T_SYNC and their (2) copies 3.97-7.47 mm each; In3 /REF_VDD, In4 /REF_VCM, In5 /VDD10 + /VDD_DRIVER. J3/J4 AGND 42/44, DGND 46/48, spares SPARE_P2..P58. FPGA-LDO A and router J3/J4 pins 2/4/6/8/24/58 unconnected; NT1 on FPGA-LDO A at (100.58, 121.0). Option B adds J5 (GND 3/65, AGND 62).
evidence: W/a review working file (not published) on V3_Top: zones In1 AGND, In2 VDD_FE, In3 REF_VDD, In4 REF_VCM, In5 VDD10/VDD_DRIVER, In6 VDD_ADC/VSS10, In7 DVDD, In8 DGND; T_ track lengths as listed. Capacitor nets on both boards: REF_VCM, REF_VDD, VDD_ADC, VDD_DRIVER, VDD_FE to AGND (4 each), DVDD to DGND (4), VDD10/VSS10/VDD_CGEN to AGND on top. W/a review working file (not published) 44 outputs per port; spares open on ldo_a and ldo_b_router. Order of magnitude only (assumed 1.5 ns edges, about 12 pF per line, 0.4 nH for two contacts in parallel; none from a datasheet): 32 data lines switching together give about 0.38 A and about 0.1 V per joint, about 0.2 V for the far chips relative to the FPGA. Option B J5 return count unchanged (SYS-06).
source: Engineering judgement; SYS-23 and SYS-41 suggested actions.
consequence: Digital edge current flows in the ASICs' reference supply and analog ground and through NT1, which can add noise to all eight recordings and disturb the returned clocks; the cheap fix on the spare pins is lost once FPGA-LDO A is ordered.
suggested_action: Before ordering FPGA-LDO A, ask the ASIC designer whether pins 2/4/6/8/24/58 may be DGND on the ASIC pair and, if so, tie them to GND on FPGA-LDO A and the router; on the top board, keep the T_ lanes over DGND or AGND (B.Cu/In8 or F.Cu/In1 side) rather than In4; measure AGND-DGND noise at bring-up.
v2note: On ASIC boards V4, pins 2/4/6/8/24/58 are no longer spare: they carry six outputs from the far (top) chips. Under pin map V6, each 80-pin port therefore routes 65 signals (44 chip outputs and 21 FPGA-driven inputs) over the same four returns (AGND 42/44, DGND 46/48). Pins 2/4/6/8 sit 6.8-8.0 mm from the nearest return, and on the top board In4 carries 28 T_ lines (22 outputs and 6 T_SPI inputs) through the REF_VCM layer, between REF_VDD (In3) and VDD10/VDD_DRIVER (In5). The old fix (tie those pins to DGND/GND) is withdrawn because grounding them on FPGA-LDO A or the router would short top-chip outputs. Before FPGA-LDO A and the ASIC pair are ordered, the owner must choose between extra ground contacts outside the 80-pin joint and accepting the design, then measuring AGND-DGND noise and returned-clock jitter at bring-up. See LDOA-41.

title: Option B J5 carries 108 signals with only three return contacts: GND on pins 3 and 65 and AGND on pin 62.
what: J5, the 120-pin DF40 board-to-board connector between the Option B router and LDO board, uses every contact: 108 single-ended 1.5 V signals, 9 ASIC rails and only three returns. A fast signal's return current flows back along the nearest ground path, and 51 of the 108 signals are more than 5 mm from a GND contact, so about 80 lines switching together at 32 MHz can cause crosstalk and ground bounce. The AGND planes on both boards also act as reference planes for signal layers, and AGND joins GND at NT1 about 6.6 mm from J5, so pin 62 carries switching digital return current as well as the analog return of eight ASICs; that mixing is the main analog risk, while the DC drop (about 1-4.4 mV) is negligible. ASIC output edge rates are not documented, so the files cannot show whether three returns are enough; a decision on more returns, or measured edge rates, would settle it.
where: Option B router J5 (DF40C-120DS) and LDO board J5 (DF40C-120DP): GND pins 3 and 65, AGND pin 62; the four MP pads on the LDO-board header have no net. Router: GND plane L3, AGND plane L4 (next to 25 signals on L5); J3/J4 AGND 42/44 and GND 46/48 (8 returns) narrow to 3 at J5. LDO board: AGND plane L2 (also carries signal tracks), net tie NT1 at (100.58, 126.81), J5 centre (99.783, 120.2).
evidence: exports/ldo_b_router/connectors.csv (120 J5 rows): 108 signals, 9 rails, GND 3/65, AGND 62; exports/ldo_b_ldo/connectors.csv matches net for net. Nearest GND contact, router: max 11.2 mm, mean 5.1 mm, 51 signals > 5 mm; LDO board: max 11.6 mm, 50 > 5 mm; counting AGND, 45 > 5 mm; counting AGND and decoupled rail pins, max 9.3 mm and 26 > 5 mm. Frontend_V46_pins_V2.xdc: signals LVCMOS15, no SLEW or DRIVE set. exports/ldo_b_router/zones.csv: GND L3, AGND L4; exports/ldo_b_ldo/zones.csv: AGND L2, GND L3/L4. inputs/asic/J3_pinout__Power_Pins.csv: AGND 6.156 mA per pin, 12.3 mA per board including the 2 mA VDD10 stimulation figure; 4 boards = 49 mA; x 90 mOhm max = 4.4 mV, x about 19 mOhm typical = about 0.9 mV. The ASIC designer's own 80-pin connector uses 4 returns for about 61 signal and pass-through pins (inputs/asic/J3_pinout__J3_Pinout.csv). inputs/ldo_b/V2_record/START_HERE.md line 53 lists J5 returns as open.
source: Hirose DF40 Series catalog (2013.11), p.2 Product Specifications (0.3 A rated current, 90 mOhm max contact resistance), https://www.hirose.com/en/product/document?clcode=CL0684-4016-5-51&documentid=en_DF40_CAT&documenttype=Catalog&lang=en&productname=DF40C-70DS-0.4V%2851%29&series=DF40 - not read directly (hirose.com returned 403); values from the project's parts review and search results quoting the catalog, so not checked against the datasheet. Engineering judgement for the return ratio.
consequence: Possible data errors on the 32 MHz returned clocks and data lanes, and digital switching noise on the recording reference through the shared AGND contact. A fix after ordering needs a new J5 pinout on both Option B boards.
suggested_action: Before making Option B order files, decide on more GND/AGND returns at J5 (for example a larger DF40 or a second small connector), or obtain the ASIC output edge rates and show that three returns are enough.

title: If all eight stacks share one head ground electrode, as SYS-11 advises, every J1 lead becomes a supply-return path through ASIC AGND (where REF_1-4 are bonded) and NT1, carrying about 4-27 mA in a typical lead and 9-62 mA (up to 89 mA) in the most-loaded one, so load steps put up to about 13 mV on the recording reference.
what: Each stack returns its whole supply current (0.15-0.55 A) through its own HDMI cable ground. The eight stack grounds therefore sit tens of mV apart, and the offsets move with each stack's load. On both V4 ASIC boards the chips' REF_1-4 pads and the one-pin J1 are on AGND, so whatever ties the animal to a stack also sets that stack's recording reference. One shared ground electrode is the usual rule for low-power headstages and is what SYS-11 proposes. Here it makes the head leads a parallel return path: part of every stack's supply current flows through J1, the ASIC AGND plane, the DF40 AGND contacts and NT1, and the voltage drop along the lead appears on every channel. Separate electrodes instead drive DC current through the tissue.
where: ASIC boards V4 (both): J1 (PinHeader 1x01 at 144.875, 68.28) and U01_BCD1/2 REF_1-REF_4, LREF_GND1-4, RREF_GND1-4 on /AGND; no part ties AGND to DGND. FPGA-LDO A: NT1 (100.58, 121.0) is the only AGND-GND tie, with only 1.0 mm test pads TP5 (GND, 92.5, 144.4) and TP6 (AGND). Option B: the router, which stays on the head, has no ground pad, and its AGND reaches NT1 (LDO board, 100.58, 126.81) only through J5.62. Cable ground: J610-J617 and Frontend J3 pins 4/7/10/13/16 and shell.
evidence: Netlists: exports/asic_top and asic_bottom netlist.xml put J1.1 and all eight REF_n pins on /AGND; only J3, J4 and the dies touch both /AGND and /DGND. exports/ldo_a and ldo_b_ldo netlist.xml: NT1 is the only part on both AGND and GND. Load per port 0.15/0.27/0.55 A at 5 V (inputs/hdmi/power_estimate/START_HERE.md sec. 1). Model: W2/a review working file (not published) (output groundloop_out.txt), eight stacks. Cable ground 0.07-0.35 ohm (assumed, as in SYS-11). Head lead 0.06-0.5 ohm: NT1 14.6 mOhm (LDOA-11), two DF40 contacts at 90 mOhm maximum, J1, and 5-30 cm of 30-36 AWG wire. No head tie: stack grounds 15-193 mV above the base board, 6-98 mV apart. One common electrode: largest lead current median 9-62 mA, 95th percentile 13-89 mA (loads ±15 %, cables ±25 %). One stack starting full stimulation (+0.08 A, FE-02) shifts its lead current by 9-60 mA. 13-77 % of one stack's stimulation return comes back through the other stacks' leads and cables. A cable with an open ground sends 0.27 A (expected load) through the leads. Mid case (cable 0.2 ohm, lead 0.15 ohm of which 0.1 ohm is wire): 40 mA x 0.1 ohm = 4 mV step on the stimulating stack's reference, about 0.6 mV on each other stack. Separate electrodes (lead plus tissue 0.5-10 kOhm): 1-28 uA DC per electrode.
source: TDT Headstage Connection Guide, sections 'Overview' and 'A Common Error to Avoid' (all headstage grounds on one common ground), https://www.tdt.com/docs/hardware/headstage-connection-guide/ . Hirose DF40 Series catalog 2013.11, p.2 (0.3 A; contact resistance 90 mOhm max), distributor copy https://cdn-shop.adafruit.com/product-files/2227/ed_DF40_20140305-337786.pdf . IEC 60601-1 Table 3, patient auxiliary current d.c. 10 uA normal condition, from a secondary summary https://lac.us/medical-standards/iec-60601-electrical-safety (standard not read; used only as a yardstick). known/system.json SYS-11; known/ldo_a.json LDOA-11; known/ldo_b.json LDOB-29 (J5 rated 0.25 A). Typical headstage supply currents of tens of mA are from memory, not re-read. Engineering judgement.
consequence: Load changes on any stack (stimulation, FPGA activity, link start) put steps of up to several mV on the reference of every channel; neural signals are tens to hundreds of uV. Part of one stack's stimulation current returns through the other stacks. An open cable ground pushes a stack's full return through the AGND contacts; in Option B that means J5.62, rated 0.25 A. Separate electrodes put 1-28 uA of DC through the animal.
suggested_action: Before ordering FPGA-LDO A or the router, add a GND (not AGND) strap pad at the edge of each head-mounted board, so the stacks' GND can be joined at the head by a short thick link, and tie the animal to AGND at one point only. Measure the lead current and the recorded step on two powered stacks in saline before building eight.

title: Each cable's one GT lane must carry eight ASICs, but the only recorded line rate (1.25 Gb/s) counts one ASIC.
what: Each Frontend sends all its recording data over one GT (multi-gigabit transceiver) lane, U1 TX0, through its HDMI cable. That lane must carry all eight ASICs on the Frontend: 64 data lines, 2.048 Gb/s raw or 1.536 Gb/s once the 12-bit words are packed. The only recorded line rate, about 1.25 Gb/s with an 800 ps bit, was worked out from one ASIC per port; after 8b/10b coding (a line code that sends 10 bits for every 8 data bits) it leaves only 1.0 Gb/s. A workable lane is 2.5 Gb/s (packed data) or 3.125 Gb/s (raw frames), and no line rate, framing, cable grade or loss budget has been set or checked at that rate.
where: Frontend U1 (XC7A35T-2CSG325I) GTP TX0 balls H2 (P) / H1 (N); TX1-TX3 unconnected, RX balls on GND. J3 pin 5 = GTP_TX0_P, pin 3 = GTP_TX0_N (swap intended, TXPOLARITY=1). Micro-HDMI cable, about 1.8 m. HDMI Extension Board J610-J617 pins 3/5 -> ESD U801-U808 -> AC capacitors C745-C760 -> MC3 GTY RX quads 224/226 (rec_rx[0..7]).
evidence: inputs/hdmi/design_inputs/START_HERE.md line 17: 256 Mbit/s per port, about 1.25 Gb/s (assumed), 800 ps; line 34: skew and spacing items to be reopened if the rates are higher; line 36: cable about 1.8 m. inputs/hdmi/power_estimate/START_HERE.md line 31: one GTP TX lane at about 1.25 Gb/s (its line 28 lists 64 DATA lines). inputs/frontend/V2_review_fixes/Frontend_V46_pins_V2.xdc and exports/frontend/nets.csv: 64 nets ASIC1-8_DATA1-8, J1/J2 to U1. ASIC_REFERENCE.md section 3, line 51: 256 Mbit/s raw, 192 Mbit/s payload per ASIC; x 8 = 2.048 Gb/s raw, 1.536 Gb/s payload. Reference clocks are 125 MHz on both ends (Frontend Y1 AX3DAF1-125.0000T3; the XEM's on-module oscillator for rec_refclk). With UG482 dividers the reachable lane rates are 1.875, 2.0, 2.5, 3.125 and 3.75 Gb/s. 8b/10b payload: 1.25 -> 1.0 Gb/s (too low); 2.0 -> 1.6 Gb/s (96 % load with packed data, too tight); 2.5 -> 2.0 Gb/s (77 % packed); 3.125 -> 2.5 Gb/s (82 % raw). Nyquist frequency rises from 0.625 GHz to 1.25-1.56 GHz. The Frontend schematic note lists 'GT link rate/protocol, cable SI' as unverified; no later lane-rate decision was found in inputs/ or the 3-11 Nov dated folders.
source: ASIC reference V1 (inputs/asic/ASIC_Reference/ASIC_REFERENCE.md) section 3, line 51; AMD DS181 v1.27.1 Table 52 (GTP maximum 6.25 Gb/s for -2 in CS/CP packages; PLL range 1.6-3.3 GHz; line rate 3.2-6.6 Gb/s at output divider 1), https://www.amd.com/content/dam/xilinx/support/documents/data_sheets/ds181_Artix_7_Data_Sheet.pdf; AMD UG482 7 Series GTP Transceivers, PLL dividers; engineering judgement. The HDMI cable-category limit was quoted from memory and not re-read.
consequence: If cables or firmware are planned around 1.25 Gb/s, the link cannot carry eight ASICs. At 2.5-3.125 Gb/s a thin 1.8 m Micro-HDMI cable with its ESD parts and connectors may not give an open eye, which shows up as bit errors and lost recording frames on some ports.
suggested_action: Record the lane rate and framing (2.5 Gb/s with packed 12-bit data, or 3.125 Gb/s with raw frames) and reopen the HDMI-board items tied to the rate. Run an IBERT eye and loss check over one real cable at 1.25-1.56 GHz Nyquist before buying eight sets.

title: On FPGA-LDO A V12 at most about 3-4 of the 12 new V6 lines get short routes through the existing copper; the rest need long multi-via detours, more L2 AGND cuts or moved lanes, so V6 needs a re-planned lane field, not 12 extra routes.
what: The known plan treats V6 on FPGA-LDO A as 12 added routes plus 4 swaps. The 13 J1 spares lie south of the 11 ASIC8 lanes that fill L1 between J1 and J3. Below them, L5 carries the ASIC1-4 lane bundle, L6 carries the J4 staircase lanes and rail pours, and L2 is the AGND plane, already cut by the lane hops. A rule-based search on the saved copper finds short paths in only two places: one 0.57 mm strip of L2 AGND west of J1's outer row (2-3 tracks wide), and one path from J3.58 to J2.40. J4.58 has no exit at all. Every other line is either unroutable or a 43-56 mm detour around J2.
where: FPGA-LDO A V12. Spares: J1.29-49 (x 92.61 inner / 89.90 outer, y 125.8-129.8, L1) and J2.40/42 (107.40, 127.8/128.2). Targets: J3 pins 2/4/6/8/24/58 (x 91.983-93.183, 96.383, 103.183; y 114.868; L1) and the same J4 pins (y 115.058, L6). The free strip on L2 is x 89.03-89.60. J4.58 is boxed in by the /ASIC_VSS10 via (102.383, 114.8), the /ASIC_VDD_ADC via (102.783, 115.1) and its 0.2 mm track, the /ASIC3_READ lane (x 103.583), the /ASIC1_READ lane (y 114.36), and J3.58's pad 0.19 mm above it on L1.
evidence: Grid search at 0.02 mm with the V12 rules: 0.1 mm track and clearance, 0.2 mm hole clearance, 0.3 mm edge, the V12 via types (micro 1-2, buried 2-5, micro 5-6, through 1-6), no stacked vias (V12 has none). Results: (a) L1/L5/L6 only, pours intact: 1 of 12 (J3.58 to J2.40, 16.2 mm). (b) With V12-style L2 hops, in either port order: 3-4 short paths (J3.2 to J1.30 12.1 mm, J3.4 to J1.32 12.0 mm, J3.6 to J1.36 13.7 mm, J3.58 to J2.40 15.9 mm); 2-4 detours of 43.7-55.6 mm with 5-9 vias; the rest no path. (c) Each line alone: 11 of 12 reach a spare, 10 of them through the same L2 strip; J4.58 none, even with all L1/L6 pours treated as removable. Exact geometry: above J4.58 the track-centre window is 114.560-114.578 mm, and it closes at the VSS10 via. For comparison, the V5 lanes are 6.3-31.6 mm.
source: Project files: boards/ldo_a/FPGA_LDO_A_Layout_V12.kicad_pcb, .kicad_dru (JLC 0.2 mm hole clearance, 0.3 mm edge), .kicad_pro (0.1 mm); exports/ldo_a/connectors.csv and board.json; known/pinmap_v6_trace.csv; inputs/ldo_a/pin_map_V5_schematic_V30/START_HERE.md. Method and logs: a review working file (not published), route_ldoa.py, out/ldoa_*.log. Engineering judgement for the search method.
consequence: V6 will not close on FPGA-LDO A as an incremental edit. Forcing the lines through the L2 AGND plane, or as 45-55 mm detours, adds more cuts to the analog ground. Either way the V12 order files, JLC checks and DRC become void, so a new layout revision has to be scheduled.
suggested_action: Run the lane planner (plan_v11.py) on pin map V6 as one full plan for all 120 signals, freeing J4.58 by moving /ASIC1_READ or the VSS10/VDD_ADC vias. Budget this as layout V13 before any other FPGA-LDO A edit.

title: In Option A the Frontend's south edge, where its order asks for break-off tabs, sits only 0.567 mm from the near ASIC board beside it.
what: In Option A the Frontend (on FPGA-LDO A J1/J2) and the near ASIC board (on J3) both sit one 1.5 mm DF40 height above FPGA-LDO A, so they stand side by side at the same level. The Frontend's south edge faces the ASIC board's connector-side edge across 0.567 mm over their whole 22 mm width. The Frontend order asks JLC to put break-off tabs on exactly that edge, and FE-07's proposed fix keeps tabs there. SYS-39 says Option A is not affected, but a tab nub, normal outline tolerance, or tilting the Frontend out by its cable end can push the removable Frontend against the board that carries the implanted probes.
where: Frontend south edge: y 121.92 in its own file = y 117.650 in the FPGA-LDO A frame, x 88.70-111.29, z 3.084-4.658. Near ASIC board (same outline on both V4 boards): connector-side edge y 67.44 = y 117.083, x 89.02-110.98, z 3.084-4.684. Frontend J1/J2 sit on LDO A J1/J2 at (91.255, 127.0) and (108.755, 127.0); ASIC J3 sits on LDO A J3 at (99.783, 113.513).
evidence: Edge.Cuts read from the board files: Frontend lines at y 96.5 / 121.92 and x 102.21 / 124.8; ASIC V4 gr_poly at y 67.44-84.4724 and x 124.34-146.31. Both mappings were checked pad by pad: Frontend 70/70 and ASIC 80/80 within 0.185 mm. Gap = 117.650 - 117.083 = 0.567 mm. LDO A is 1.584 mm thick, so both boards start at z 3.084; inputs/system/README_2026-11-11.md also lists Frontend 3.08-4.62 and ASIC board 1 3.08-3.88. inputs/frontend/V3_order/JLC_ORDER_NOTES.txt line 13 asks for tabs 'on the south and east edges only'. Tolerance (a review working file (not published)): ±0.2 mm routing on both boards plus four connector placements and two matings at an assumed ±0.05 mm gives worst case -0.13 mm and RSS +0.26 mm. With ±0.1 mm precision routing the worst case is +0.07 mm. Tilting the Frontend about the south end of J1/J2 moves its south top corner 0.13 / 0.26 / 0.37 mm toward the ASIC board at 5 / 10 / 15 degrees. No other Frontend edge is free: the east and west edges are flush with LDO A (0.02-0.03 mm) with J1/J2 pads 0.645-0.665 mm in (FE-07), and J3 overhangs the north edge by 0.62 mm.
source: JLCPCB PCB capabilities (routed outline ±0.2 mm regular, ±0.1 mm precision), https://jlcpcb.com/capabilities/pcb-capabilities. JLCPCB blog 'Mouse Bites in PCBs: Easy Solutions for Clean Separation and Professional Results', 20 Mar 2026 (1.5 mm keep-out from a tab edge; sand off the nubs that remain), https://jlcpcb.com/blog/pcb-mouse-bites. Hirose DF40 Series catalog, Jun 1 2024: p2 (0.45 mm effective mating length) and p23 (pull out in parallel; otherwise tilt only along the pitch direction), LCSC copy https://datasheet.lcsc.com/datasheet/pdf/145ab5d527b34eafa7a47375cb561c6a.pdf?productCode=C3640153, series page https://www.hirose.com/en/product/series/DF40. Placement and mating play: engineering judgement.
consequence: A nub or a tolerance stack-up can stop the Frontend or the ASIC pair from seating within the 0.45 mm DF40 engagement. In Option A the Frontend is the routine disconnect, so every swap can rub or push the implanted near ASIC board.
suggested_action: Change the Frontend order so the south edge gets no tabs (route the board out fully, or have that edge sanded flush), and order ±0.1 mm precision routing. Keep the ASIC boards' connector-side edge tab-free too. Give the head housing (SYS-07) a feature that lifts the Frontend straight off.

title: The only complete V6 grid route found for FPGA-LDO A fails KiCad DRC, has 37 laser vias too close to same-net buried vias for JLC and cuts L2 AGND by 62 mm², so a re-route under V12's rules is still unproven.
what: This is the first test of whether a re-planned FPGA-LDO A can carry the V6 pin map. With all signal copper removed and the LDOA-05 GND vias and ASIC-14 strips added, no straight cut is close to full: every horizontal cut from y 115.6 to 125 and every connector face has at least 1.5 times its demand on L1, L5 and L6 alone. A negotiated grid router then routed all 121 nets with legal clearances, but only by running L2 tracks outside today's AGND pockets and by putting about 45 laser vias on, or within 0.3 mm of, a buried via of the same net, which V12 never does. Held to today's pockets, the best route left 12 of 121 nets unrouted, and the same router misses 6-10 of V12's own 109 nets on the case V12 proves routable, so the strict case is still undecided.
where: FPGA-LDO A V12. J3 (L1) and J4 (L6) at x 91.98-107.58, y 111.98-115.06 connect to J1 (x 89.90/92.61) and J2 (x 107.40/110.11) at y 120.2-133.8, on layers L1, L2 (AGND), L5 and L6. New L2 copper in the complete strip-clean route: 35.6 mm in the J1 wing and 41.5 mm in the J2 wing. By band: 13.1 mm under J3/J4, 22.5 mm at y 115.6-120, 41.5 mm along the J1/J2 rows.
evidence: Demand (demand.json): 121 nets, 120 of which cross to J1/J2 (60 to each). The re-plan removes 644 signal tracks and 223 signal vias. Capacity in 0.1 mm tracks at V12 rules (0.10 clearance, 0.20 hole clearance, 0.30 edge, 0.10 to kept pours), as L1/L5/L6/L2 pockets/L2 open vs demand: y115.6 77/110/84/46/108 vs 120; y117.5 79/110/76/46/108 vs 120; y119.5 65/109/77/46/107 vs 120; y120.4 68/107/7/62/108 vs 116; y121.6 68/110/4/75/108 vs 104; y122.8 68/99/19/17/98 vs 94; y125.0 66/110/22/78/108 vs 72; J1 faces 107/105/26/38/117 vs 60; J2 faces 92/82/27/49/119 vs 60; J3/J4 field 98/136/101/46/134 vs 121. The limiting cut is none. The tightest is y 120.4-121.6, with L1+L5+L6 at 182 vs 104-116, where L6 drops to 4-7 tracks under the regulator pours (178 with 0.2 mm pour clearance). V12 already uses 108 tracks at y 117.5. Router model: 0.1 mm grid, tracks at 0.2 mm pitch, via spacing 0.40-0.60 mm, no via copper in the J4 strips. Complete route V_H40s2: 121/121 nets; an independent check (verify_route.py) finds 0 clearance violations and every net connected. It uses 516 vias: 203 laser L1-L2, 159 buried, 115 laser L5-L6, 39 through. It puts 77.1 mm of L2 track outside today's pockets in 85 pieces, 66 of them under 1 mm, removing about 44 mm2 of AGND. It has 45 same-net laser/buried pairs closer than 0.3 mm; V12 has none, and its closest such pair is 0.43 mm. Three earlier complete routes, which let 1-6 vias touch the strip band, used 46.9, 62.8 and 85.7 mm of new L2. Inside today's pockets: 109, 109 and 106 of 121 nets over 3 seeds, even with about 20 close pairs. Allowing explicit stacked vias gave 108/121. Calibration on V12's own nets: 100, 99 and 103 of 109. Files: a review working file (not published) (cuts_h_z0.10.log, facecuts.log, route_V_H40s2.log, route_R3_pocket*.log, route_CAL_pocket*.log, l2_open_detail_V_H40s2.log) and img/route_V_H40s2_L*.png.
source: Project files: boards/ldo_a/FPGA_LDO_A_Layout_V12.kicad_pcb, .kicad_dru and .kicad_pro (track 0.1, clearance 0.1, hole clearance 0.2, hole-to-hole 0.25, edge 0.3); exports/ldo_a/board_stats.txt for via types (laser 0.10/0.26, buried 0.20/0.40, through 0.15/0.35); known/pinmap_v6_trace.csv; a review working file (not published); known/ldo_a.json LDOA-05; known/asic.json ASIC-14. The strip limits are taken from ASIC-14, which cites the Hirose DF40 catalogue p.8 note 3 and drawing EDC3-311352-00 note 2, https://www.hirose.com/product/download?distributor=all&type=catalogue&lang=en&series=DF40; I did not re-read those. JLCPCB HDI PCB capabilities FAQ, https://jlcpcb.com/help/article/hdi-pcb-capabilities-faq, read 12 Nov 2026. It defines stacked vias as blind and buried vias at the same position. It says buried vias are resin plugged and capped. It sets a 0.13 mm minimum from a blind-via edge to a same-net hole. It does not say stacked vias are offered for this stack.
consequence: Option A is the only board left for the 'keep V4, fix the rest' plan, and the change is not a patch. Every signal track and via must be re-routed, and the V12 order files become obsolete. Without stacked vias and new AGND pockets, nothing yet shows that the re-route closes. Ordering on the assumption that it does risks another spin, and the earlier 3-4 of 12 limit only applies to a patch.
suggested_action: Ask JLC whether a laser via may sit on a capped buried via in stack JLCH061611Y1-1078. Decide whether 50-80 mm of new L2 signal pockets in the connector wings are acceptable for AGND. Then re-route the board in one pass with the V6 map, the LDOA-05 vias and the ASIC-14 strips, or first try a pocket-only route by hand, and check DRC and parity before ordering.

title: The V3 boards are 1.6 mm, so each head stack is about 17.0 mm tall, not 13.8 mm, and the four probe rows are 3.1 / 6.2 / 3.1 mm apart, not 2.3 / 5.4 / 2.3 mm.
what: Both V3 board files are ten-layer, 1.6 mm. The project record says the ASIC board will be 0.8 mm (6 Nov), and the print models, the deck's head view on the sheep and the Option A fit use 0.8 mm. With four 1.6 mm ASIC boards each stack grows by about 3.1-3.2 mm and 2.3-2.9 g. Each board's dies sit on its top face and its probes leave the same edge (y 100.0 in the FPGA-LDO frame), so the four probe rows of a stack spread over 12.4 mm instead of 10.0 mm. The V3 record lists thickness as needing input; until it is decided, the models used to judge fit on the animal and the probe plan do not match the board files.
where: V3 Top_board and Bottom_board PCB.kicad_pcb (thickness 1.6, 10 copper layers); inputs/system/README_2026-11-11.md (print models V2); inputs/notes/fpga-ldo-v14.md lines 108-110; inputs/system/weekly_deck/START_HERE.md 11 Nov 08:24 head view.
evidence: W/a review working file (not published) Option A (z = 0 at LDO A bottom, LDO 1.58 mm): board top faces with 0.8 mm boards -3.80, -1.50, 3.88, 6.18 (pitch 2.3 / 5.38 / 2.3, span 9.98 mm); with 1.6 mm -4.60, -1.50, 4.68, 7.78 (3.1 / 6.18 / 3.1, span 12.38 mm). Option B (z = 0 at LDO board bottom): 0.8 mm -0.70, 1.60, 7.00, 9.30 (2.3 / 5.4 / 2.3, span 10.0); 1.6 mm -1.50, 1.60, 7.80, 10.90 (3.1 / 6.2 / 3.1, span 12.4). Envelope without plug, record conventions (receptacle box 1.44 mm from 0.09 mm off the board, header box up to 1.44 mm): Option A 13.82 -> 16.95 mm, Option B 13.77 -> 16.97 mm; both ends are now ASIC boards. Mass: outline 21.97 x 17.03 mm, +0.8 mm at 1.9-2.4 g/cm3 = 0.57-0.72 g per board, 2.3-2.9 g per stack, 18-23 g for eight stacks, against the record's 10-12 g on-head estimate (fpga-ldo-v14.md line 110). Side pin: at 1.6 mm the near board's J1 tail clears the LDO A / router top by 0.55 mm; at 0.8 mm it reaches 0.25 mm into it.
source: Engineering judgement; project records listed.
consequence: The printed heads and the head view are about 3 mm short and show the wrong probe-row spacing, so an animal fit judged on them can fail; switching to 0.8 mm later changes via aspect ratio, impedance and the side-pin result on both ASIC boards.
suggested_action: Decide 1.6 mm or a fabricator-quoted thin ten-layer stack before the ASIC pair is ordered, then rebuild the fit and print models and the head view with that thickness and the V3 capacitor placement.

title: No record estimates or limits head-stack heat; about 1.45 W per stack gives a 19-34 K still-air surface rise.
what: Nearly all power that enters a stack becomes heat in it: the FPGA, the 5 V-to-3.3 V buck and the other bucks, the linear regulators and the ASIC boost converter. The Option A stack is small (24.12 x 47.05 x 13.82 mm), so in still air its average surface rises about 19-34 K at the expected 1.45 W, with hot spots over U1 and the bucks running higher. Eight stacks stand side by side on the animal's skull with probe shanks in the brain, so they heat each other and the head, about 11.6 W in total at the expected load. No record sets a temperature limit, and only a measurement of one powered stack running the real bitstream will give the real rise.
where: Frontend U1 (XC7A35T), U16 and U2/U3/U4/U13 (MPM3833C), U5/U6 (TPS74801), U10 (MP5077); FPGA-LDO A U1 (LT3582-12), U2/U6/U8/U9 (LT3042), U10 (LT3094), U3/U4/U5/U7 (TPS7A2015); four ASIC boards per stack; whole Option A stack (Option B is larger and similar).
evidence: a review working file (not published) 1.45 W expected, 2.79 W high at VIN_5V; rail currents match inputs/hdmi/power_estimate/START_HERE.md section 1 and inputs/asic/J3_pinout__Power_Budget.csv. A low case of about 1.1 W follows from the record's low column plus the boost. Envelope 24.12 x 47.05 x 13.82 mm (inputs/system/README_2026-11-11.md; matches Option_A_Head_Stack_V12.stl without the plug) -> 4,237 mm2. h = 10-15 W/m2K -> 15.7-23.6 K/W -> 23-34 K at 1.45 W, 17-26 K at 1.1 W, 44-66 K at 2.8 W. A convection plus radiation estimate gives h about 13-16 W/m2K, so about 19-23 K expected. The 2.8 W case assumes all 1,024 stimulators at 22.5 uA on both rails continuously and VCCINT 0.4 A; with 1 ms pulses under 200 Hz and one rail per phase it falls to about 2.1 W (about 33 K). Option B (27.90 x 52.88 x 13.77 mm, 5,175 mm2) rises about 20 % less. Eight stacks: 9-22 W, 11.6 W expected. inputs/system/weekly_deck/START_HERE.md (11 Nov 08:24 entry): eight stacks on a sheep skull, shanks in the brain. A search of inputs/ found no head-stack thermal estimate or limit.
source: Engineering judgement (lumped surface model). The IEC 60601-1 applied-part surface limit of about 43 C for long contact is from secondary sources and was not read; tissue-heating limits (usually about 1-2 K brain temperature rise) are stricter. Efficiency curves of the LT3582-12, MPM3833C and TPS74801 were not checked against the datasheets.
consequence: Stack surfaces above body-contact limits, heat conducted down the shanks into the brain, and hot FPGA and ASIC junctions; the planned commercial-grade U1 (XC7A35T-2CSG325C, 0-85 C) leaves less junction margin. This may force a heat sink, duty cycling or a head-mount change after eight stacks are built.
suggested_action: Set a head-surface and tissue-heating limit, then measure one powered stack (thermocouple or IR) in still air with the real bitstream before ordering eight.

title: No head board has a fixing feature, so the stack and the HDMI cable load hang on unlocked DF40 connectors.
what: None of the five head boards (Frontend, FPGA-LDO Option A, Option B router, Option B LDO board, ASIC board) has a mounting hole, slot, notch or standoff. The 70-, 80- and 120-position DF40 parts used here have no latch, and Hirose says a board must not be held by these connectors alone but secured with a housing or cushioning. The Micro-HDMI cable plugs into the Frontend, so every plug-in, pull-out, tug or twist of the cable is carried by the 140 contacts of Frontend J1/J2, which engage by only 0.45 mm. No record says how the stack is held on the animal or where the cable is anchored; the weekly deck says the head cap is not drawn.
where: All five head boards. Frontend J1/J2 (DF40C-70DS-0.4V(51), bottom) on FPGA-LDO J1/J2 (DF40C-70DP-0.4V(51)) of Option A and of the Option B LDO board; Frontend J3 Micro-HDMI (Molex 467651001) at (112.5, 98.28), top, plug entering from the north edge; LDO A J3/J4, router J3/J4 and J5, ASIC board J3/J4.
evidence: exports/*/board_stats.txt: NPTH 0 on frontend, ldo_a, ldo_b_router, ldo_b_ldo and asic. Through-hole pads: Frontend 4 (the J3 shield slots, 0.65 x 1.7 mm, GND), the three LDO boards 0, ASIC board 1 (J1 pin, 0.5 mm, /AGND). No mounting-hole or standoff part in any parts.csv and no cut-outs inside any outline; outlines are plain rectangles, the Option B boards with side tabs. inputs/frontend/V3_order/JLC_ORDER_NOTES.txt line 6: four plated slots only. Rigid-pivot estimate, not measured: J3 mouth at y 95.88, J1/J2 bodies y 104.215-120.925; an upward pull F at the end of a 20 mm overmold acts 45.05 mm from the far end of J1/J2 against an average retention arm of 8.355 mm, so J1+J2 see about 5.4 x F of peel (1 N on the cable gives about 5.4 N). Molex Micro-HDMI forces from secondary copies of the Type D spec, not molex.com: insertion up to 44.1 N, initial withdrawal 5-25 N. Hirose gives no DF40 withdrawal force; mating durability 30 cycles. inputs/frontend/V3_record/START_HERE.md line 69: Frontend parts within 1 mm of the edge almost all the way round. inputs/system/weekly_deck/START_HERE.md line 67: head cap not drawn; the Frontend (Option A) and the LDO board (Option B) are meant to be unplugged.
source: Hirose DF40 Series catalog, Feb. 2024 edition (printed Jun. 1 2024), read from the LCSC copy https://datasheet.lcsc.com/datasheet/pdf/145ab5d527b34eafa7a47375cb561c6a.pdf?productCode=C3640153 because hirose.com returned 403: p2 (lock on 10-50 positions only; 0.45 mm effective mating length), p6/p8 (C = no retention tab), p21 Precautions (do not support the PCB only with the connectors; secure mated connectors with housings and cushioning), p23 (pull out parallel). 2014 edition p16 item 6 (connector not designed as the main support). Series page https://www.hirose.com/en/product/series/DF40. Molex Micro-HDMI 46765 forces from secondary copies only.
consequence: Plugging or pulling the cable can tilt or peel the Frontend off the FPGA-LDO board. On a moving animal the stack can unseat, giving intermittent power, clock and data contact, and repeated peeling can crack the 0.4 mm-pitch joints.
suggested_action: Before ordering, decide how the stack is held: a housing or edge clamp around the Frontend (its edges have no room for holes) with the cable anchored to it, plus holes or notches on the board that stays on the head (Option A board or Option B router) if wanted. Then measure the unplug force of a built Frontend-LDO pair.

title: Three 0805 capacitors under the Frontend can be 1.45 mm tall in the 1.5 mm gap, leaving 0.05 mm worst case.
what: The mated DF40C-70DS / DF40C-70DP pair sets a 1.5 mm gap between the Frontend and the FPGA-LDO board. C4, C42 and C59 sit on the Frontend underside inside that gap and can be up to 1.45 mm thick, which leaves 0.25 mm nominal and 0.05 mm worst case before solder standoff, solder mask and board bow. The LDO top under them has no parts, but the silkscreen text 'PRE-' runs under C42 and C59 on Option A and under C42 on Option B, so the worst case can reach zero or slight interference. Contact is unlikely with typical part thickness, but the margin is gone and the parts are still in the V3 order.
where: Frontend bottom: C4 at (122.8, 101.08), 100 uF Murata GRM21BR60J107ME15L on VCCINT_1V0; C42 at (104.16, 97.725) on VCCO_1V5 and C59 at (107.03, 98.45) on VCCAUX_1V8, both 47 uF Yageo CC0805MKX5R5BB476. They land over the LDO A top at about (90.70, 138.49), (109.34, 141.85) and (106.47, 141.12); on the Option B LDO board at the same x with y +5.81 mm. C89 (DNP, same part as C4) would be the same if fitted.
evidence: exports/frontend/parts.csv: C4, C42, C59 bottom and fitted; C89 DNP. inputs/frontend/V3_order: BOM_JLC.csv orders C4 as C141660 and C15, C42, C59 as C109461 (C15 is on top); CPL_JLC.csv places C4, C42, C59 on the bottom. Thickness: Murata reference sheet T = 1.25 +/-0.2 mm (1.45 mm max); Yageo part 1.45 mm max per DigiKey and a third-party listing. Gap: 1.5 - 1.45 = 0.05 mm worst case; 1.5 - 1.25 = 0.25 mm nominal (a review working file (not published) rows A1, B1). Next tallest Frontend bottom parts U5, U6, Y1 at 1.0 mm leave 0.50 mm (heights not re-checked). Board mapping LDO = (213.5 - x, 239.57 - y), plus 5.81 mm in y for Option B, matches the J1/J2 pad nets. Under the capacitors on both LDO boards: no top parts, one via each. pcbnew silkscreen scan: 'PRE-' at x 106.55-110.94, y 141.84-143.54 on ldo_a (overlaps C42 and C59) and x 107.75-110.99, y 146.23-147.61 on ldo_b_ldo (overlaps C42). frontend/schematic_V45_record/START_HERE.md line 30: proposed GRM219R60J476ME44D (0.95 mm max), not applied.
source: Hirose DF40 catalog, 2014 copy: 1.5 mm stacking table listing DF40C-70DS-0.4V(51), standard header height 1.14 +/-0.15 mm for DF40C-70DP-0.4V(51), effective mating length 0.45 mm at 1.5 mm (p1, p4, p10); Feb. 2024 edition (LCSC copy) p8; https://www.hirose.com/en/product/series/DF40. Murata GRM21BR60J107ME15 reference sheet (specifications as of Jun. 25 2026), dimensions, T = 1.25 +/-0.2 mm. Yageo CC0805MKX5R5BB476 thickness not checked against the Yageo datasheet.
consequence: The connectors may not seat fully within their 0.45 mm engagement, or a 100 uF or 47 uF capacitor on VCCINT, VCCO or VCCAUX takes the mating force and cracks, which can short the rail.
suggested_action: Before the Frontend is ordered, fit parts of about 1.1 mm maximum thickness at C4, C42 and C59 (for example the proposed 0.95 mm-max GRM219R60J476ME44D; at C4 this halves VCCINT bulk unless C89 is fitted, which the record ties to an MPM3833C output-capacitance limit) or move them to the top, and clear the 'PRE-' silkscreen under them on both LDO boards.

title: No file records the height of the ASIC dies and bond loops, which sit 1.5 mm under the next ASIC board.
what: Each ASIC board carries two bare dies on its top side, joined to the board by fine bond wires that arch above the die (the bond loops). When ASIC boards stack, the next board's bare underside sits 1.5 mm above those dies, which is the mated height of the DF40 connector pair. No file records the die thickness, the bond-loop height or the height of any protective encapsulation (glob-top), and the fit models only use 0.5 mm boxes. The files cannot settle whether 1.5 mm is enough; die, loop and encapsulation heights from the ASIC designer or the bonding house would.
where: ASIC board, top side: U01_BCD1 and U01_BCD2 pad area x 124.98-145.63, y 75.36-83.96. J4 (DF40C-80DP header) on top, J3 (DF40C-80DS receptacle) on the bottom. Affects two of the four ASIC boards in each option; in Option A, ASIC1 (under ASIC2) and ASIC4 (under ASIC3). The top board's dies are exposed.
evidence: exports/asic/pads.csv: all 176 pads of U01_BCD1/U01_BCD2 on copper layer 1 (top); the only bottom-side part is J3 at y 69.47-72.55, so nothing hangs over the dies. Edge.Cuts in boards/asic/PCB.kicad_pcb: x 124.34-146.31, y 67.44-84.47. Hirose DF40 catalog text (a review working file (not published)): 1.5 mm stacking height for DS receptacle with DP header. inputs/system/README_2026-11-11.md line 51: 'two dies are 0.5 mm boxes'; its Option A levels give 1.5 mm between ASIC1 and ASIC2 and between ASIC4 and ASIC3. ASIC3's dies have 4.58 mm up to ASIC1's underside because they lie past the LDO-A edge (y 110.34). inputs/asic/ASIC_Reference has no die thickness, loop height or glob-top value; U01 die and bonding revision listed as unknown.
source: Hirose DF40 Series catalog, stacking height table, https://www.hirose.com/en/product/series/DF40; Engineering judgement for the clearance need.
consequence: If die, loops and encapsulation together exceed about 1.4 mm, mating the next ASIC board can crush the bond wires of an irreplaceable ASIC.
suggested_action: Get die thickness, loop height and encapsulation height from the ASIC designer or bonding house and record a maximum allowed height (for example 1.2 mm) in the ASIC board notes.
v2note: On the ASIC boards V4, both board types carry the same 24 0201 capacitors on B.Cu inside the 8.58 mm die openings. ASIC boards mate J4 into J3 with no rotation, so at each ASIC-to-ASIC joint the upper board's capacitors hang over the lower board's dies (four ASICs per stack), leaving about 1.15 mm (1.5 mm DF40 − 0.33 mm 0201 − about 0.02 mm solder), not 1.5 mm, for die, attach, bond loops and any glob-top; no file records those heights, so this is the same major item as A-1 / R2S-02 and SYS-31 should be merged into it. Second check: the higher severity is upheld. Confirmed on V4: both boards have 24 0201 caps on B.Cu at identical XY (x 129.55-141.00, y 79.90-83.35), 12 inside each bond-finger ring (side rows 8.585 mm apart). J3/J4 share XY (pin n within 0.19 mm, nets 80/80), so each upper ASIC board's caps sit over the lower board's dies. Gap is about 1.5 (DF40C-80DS/DP) - 0.33 (0201 T 0.30±0.03) - 0.02 = 1.15 mm. No die, loop or glob-top height on file. Major matches A-1/R2S-02; blocker unproven.

title: Enclosure V3 has no recorded room for the XEM8310's fansink, so the 10-15 W module has no heat sink in a box without a fan and may exceed its 0-70 C rating.
what: The project power estimate puts 10-15 W (20 W high) on the XEM8310 and assumes it runs under its own fansink. The enclosure V2 record says the box relies on that fansink plus vent slots. But the fansink is an optional add-on, the V2/V3 enclosure model has none, and over the FPGA the lid ceiling is only about 14.35 mm above the XEM board top. The only fansink height in the workspace (21 mm) would not fit. Opal Kelly rates the module 0 to +70 C and warns that heat sinks may be needed, especially in an enclosure; HDMI-41's box-air estimate reaches 40-74 C in a 25 C room.
where: HDMI Extension Board V37 with the XEM8310 on MC1-MC3 (FPGA at x 159.8-186.8, y 87.8-114.8). Enclosure V3, heights above the HDMI board bottom: deck z 20.9-22.4 with a window at x 147-222, y 77-123; lid ceiling z 22.4; lid top z 25.4; 13 vent slots of 2.5 x 40 mm in the lid and floor.
evidence: inputs/hdmi/power_estimate/START_HERE.md section 2: XEM8310 10-15 W expected (fan included), 20 W high; 'most of the 22-44 W is dissipated on the XEM, under its fansink'. enclosure_V2/deliver/START_HERE.md lines 32, 79 and 92: the XEM model has no fansink; heat 'relies on the XEM's own fansink and the slots'; 'measure the real fansink before making parts'. enclosure_V3/deliver/review/enclosure_meta.json and enclosure3.py lines 36-56 give the deck, ceiling, top, window and vents. XEM board top = 1.594 (board) + 5.00 (MC mated height) + 1.46 (XEM PCB) = about 8.05 mm, using the stack figures in inputs/hdmi/V35_prefab_review/ALL_FINDINGS.md line 752. That leaves 12.85 mm to the deck, 14.35 mm to the lid ceiling and 17.35 mm to the lid top. The same review line names a '21 mm Radian FI27 fansink' (no source given): 8.05 + 21 = 29.05 mm before adding the FPGA package, above the 25.4 mm lid top. inputs/hdmi/enclosure_V3/START_HERE.md lines 7 and 62: thermal not verified, no fan. HDMI-41: box air 15-49 K above the room.
source: Opal Kelly XEM8310 Specifications (operating temperature 0 to +70 C; optional fansink Radian FI27/1.3+Y+T725, 12 V nominal, 10.8-13.2 V), https://docs.opalkelly.com/xem8310/specifications/. Opal Kelly 'Powering the XEM8310' (heat sinks may be required, primary focus the FPGA U1 and SDRAM U4/U5; consider heat dissipation in an enclosure; example VCCINT 9,916 mW at about 80 % utilization), https://docs.opalkelly.com/xem8310/powering-the-xem8310/. Opal Kelly FANSINK-05 product page (no dimensions given), https://www.opalkelly.com/products/accessories/FANSINK-05/. Known HDMI-41 and HDMI-17.
consequence: Without the fansink, the FPGA module has no heat sink in a closed box with no fan. With the fansink fitted, the lid as drawn cannot close. At the high end of the box-air estimate the module exceeds its 70 C rating before its own heating, and the board's Micro-HDMI pin-19 contacts reach the 55 C condition where HDMI-17's 0.3 A rating applies.
suggested_action: Decide whether FANSINK-05 is fitted, measure its height on a real part, and cut the lid (or add a fan opening) to suit before printing. Then run HDMI-41's closed-box test with the real XEM bitstream and log box air and FPGA temperature (system monitor) against the 0-70 C rating.

title: If the Frontend is unplugged between sessions, as the records assume for Option A, FPGA-LDO A's two DF40C-70DP plugs sit bare on the head with 108 contacts wired straight to ASIC die pads and no ESD protection.
what: LDOB-08 records that Option B's router J5 leaves unprotected ASIC lines open to static discharge (ESD) while the module is off. Option A has the same exposure. In the recorded Option A split, the Frontend unplugs and FPGA-LDO A stays on the head, so its J1/J2 plugs (contacts proud of the housing) stay bare. 108 of their contacts run to J3/J4 and the die pads with no series part, clamp or make-first ground. In both options each stack's far ASIC board also leaves one 80-contact DF40 permanently open, and on the V4 boards every one of the 80 contacts lands on a die pad of one board or the other.
where: FPGA-LDO A V12: J1 (91.255, 127.0) and J2 (108.755, 127.0), DF40C-70DP on the top face, routed to J3/J4 at (99.783, 113.51). ASIC V4 near and far boards: J3 (DS, B.Cu) and J4 (DP, F.Cu) at (135.54, 71.01). Free end of each stack: the far board's J4 on the top-side port and its J3 on the underside port (R2S-10).
evidence: exports/ldo_a/parts.csv: J1/J2 are DF40C-70DP-0.4V(51) on the top face. exports/ldo_a/pads.csv and nets.csv: all 108 J1/J2 signal contacts reach J3/J4 with no series part; 8 of them carry only a 10k pull (R2-R5, R16-R19). exports/asic_top/parts.csv and asic_bottom/parts.csv: the only parts are J1, J3, J4, U01_BCD1/2 and 30 rail capacitors. pads.csv: 52 (near board) and 50 (far board) of the 80 contacts go straight to that board's own die pads; the rest pass through to the other board's dies; 80/80 reach a die pad, 22 on both boards. inputs/system/weekly_deck/START_HERE.md line 67: 'the Option A split (Frontend unplugs, FPGA-LDO stays) is assumed'. With the Frontend off, the head's only reference is the animal, through ASIC J1 (/AGND).
source: known/ldo_b.json LDOB-08, which cites the Hirose DF40 catalogue 2013.11 p.1 (no make-first contacts on DF40C). Hirose DF40 series page https://www.hirose.com/product/series/DF40?lang=en (not re-read; hirose.com returned 403 to earlier reviewers). inputs/asic/ASIC_Reference/ASIC_REFERENCE.md open item U03 (no ESD or absolute ratings). JEDEC JS-001 human-body model, 100 pF / 1.5 kOhm (from memory, not re-read). Engineering judgement.
consequence: Any handling of an Option A head between sessions, and any touch on a stack's free connector, can discharge into ASIC pads and through the implanted electrodes. Choosing Option A to avoid LDOB-08 does not remove this exposure.
suggested_action: Make LDOB-08's handling rule (handler and module bonded to the head's ground before any DF40 touches) and a cover for every exposed DF40 a system rule for both options. Get the ASIC pad ESD rating from the ASIC designer.

title: Frontend JTAG uses HDMI pin 2 for TMS, a wire that cables without Ethernet may leave out.
what: The Frontend's JTAG runs as single wires in the roughly 1.8 m HDMI cable: TMS on pin 2 (Utility/HEAC+), TDI on 15 (CEC), TCK on 17 (SCL) and TDO on 18 (SDA). Pin 2 is only sure to be wired in 'with Ethernet' cables. Cable JTAG is the Frontend's only JTAG path, so a cable without pin 2 means the Frontend cannot be configured and its flash cannot be programmed. Crosstalk from TCK onto TDO is plausible but the files cannot settle it: neighbouring connector pins do not show how the wires lie inside a given cable, and only the cable's construction or a measurement would.
where: HDMI Extension Board J610-J617 pins 2 (HDMIn_JTAG_TMS), 15 (TDI), 17 (TCK), 18 (TDO), 16 (GND); TCK path J610.17 -> R640 100 ohm -> U611 TS3A27518E -> R601 -> U602 TXU0304. Frontend J3 pins 2, 15, 17, 18 direct to U1.
evidence: exports/hdmi/pads.csv J610: 2 = HDMI1_JTAG_TMS, 15 = TDI, 17 = TCK, 18 = TDO, 16 = GND; exports/frontend/pads.csv J3 the same. exports/frontend/netlist.xml: FPGA_JTAG_* connect only J3 and U1. Cable length about 1.8 m: inputs/hdmi/design_inputs/START_HERE.md line 36. Pin-2 item: inputs/hdmi/V35_prefab_review/ALL_FINDINGS.md lines 243-246. No cable construction data in the workspace.
source: HDMI Type D pinout, https://www.electronics-notes.com/articles/audio-video/hdmi/hdmi-pinouts-connections.php (pin 2 Utility/HEAC+); engineering judgement for crosstalk.
consequence: A cable that lacks the pin-2 wire leaves that Frontend unprogrammable; TDO errors at high TCK are possible but unproven.
suggested_action: Buy passive 'High Speed with Ethernet' cables, ring out pins 1, 2, 15, 17, 18 and 19 on each, and start JTAG at 1 MHz or less.

title: After V6 only 3 of the 15 Frontend-LDO spare contacts remain, too few for the rail enable/power-good pair plus the bottom chips' four DISC_OUT lines.
what: R2S-07 left open whether DISC_OUT must be read. V6 uses 12 of the 15 Frontend-to-FPGA-LDO spare contacts, including both J2 spares, and also K5/K6, the last free balls in bank 34. That leaves 3 contacts, all on J1, or only 1 if the proposed ASIC rail enable/power-good pair (SYS-10, LDOA-15) is added, while bringing the bottom chips' DISC_OUT (J3/J4 pins 3 and 5, open on FPGA-LDO A today) to the FPGA needs 4. The top chips' DISC_OUT has no connector pin at all on the V4 boards: all 80 J3/J4 pins are assigned, including pins 4 and 6, which R2E-04 proposed for it and which now carry T_D<8>(2) and T_D<7>(2). Option B's J5 has no spare.
where: Frontend and FPGA-LDO A spares J1.29-33, 35-37, 39, 43, 45, 47, 49 (10 used by V6) and J2.40, 42 (both used). FPGA-LDO A J3.3, J3.5, J4.3, J4.5 unconnected. ASIC V4 J3/J4 pins 4/6 (T_D<8>(2), T_D<7>(2)); on the top board, /T_DISC_OUT and /T_DISC_OUT(2) reach only their chips.
evidence: exports/ldo_a and exports/frontend connectors.csv: 15 unconnected J1/J2 contacts; FPGA-LDO A J3/J4 unconnected pins are 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 8, 24 and 58. known/pinmap_v6_trace.csv: 12 'NEW ROUTE' rows (pins 2/4/6/8/24/58 on each port), so 15 - 12 = 3. exports/asic_bottom/nets.csv: /DISC_OUT = J3.5, J4.5, U01_BCD1; /DISC_OUT(2) = J3.3, J4.3, U01_BCD2. exports/asic_top/nets.csv and netlist.xml: /T_DISC_OUT = U01_BCD1 only and /T_DISC_OUT(2) = U01_BCD2 only, with no J3/J4 pad. exports/asic_top/connectors.csv and exports/asic_bottom/connectors.csv: all 80 J3/J4 pins are on nets; only the mounting pads are unassigned. Bank 34 becomes 50 of 50. known/fix_plans_11nov_evening_on_V3.json critic: 'V6 needs 12 of them plus 2 for EN/PG, which leaves 1'. known/asic_r2.json R2E-04 suggested action (pins 4 and 6).
source: ASIC designer's Pins.xlsx (inputs/asic/Pins__Sheet1.csv: DISC_OUT termination undecided); known/system.json R2S-07 and SYS-10; known/ldo_a.json LDOA-15; known/fix_plans_11nov_evening_on_V3.json (pin choices for SYS-10 and LDOA-15); project files as listed; engineering judgement.
consequence: If DISC_OUT or rail control is wanted after the V6 boards are ordered, no contact is left for it: the bottom chips' copy then needs larger joint connectors and another spin of the Frontend and FPGA-LDO A, and the top chips' copy needs a new ASIC board.
suggested_action: Before V6 routing starts, settle DISC_OUT use with the ASIC designer and decide the enable/power-good option and any per-port STIM_EN split (see the finding on shared STIM lines) together, then record the remaining spares in the pin map. If any DISC_OUT must be read, reserve four joint contacts now (drop the power-good line, or use larger DF40s for J1/J2) and tell the ASIC designer that the top chips need a connector pin for it.

title: The four V6 clock swaps belong on the Frontend: there each pair routes in 2-13 mm, while on FPGA-LDO A they need the same scarce space as the new lines and the ASIC3 swap has no path.
what: In V6 the top chips' returned clocks arrive on lanes that end at non-clock-capable balls (U16, L4, B17, R7). The known plan swaps four lane pairs on FPGA-LDO A. On V12, 7 of the 8 crossed lanes route on their own, but the ASIC8 and ASIC4 swaps use the inter-row pocket at x about 92.9 that J3/J4 pins 2-8 need, and J4.62 to J2.35 (the ASIC3 clock) has no path. On the Frontend every crossed pair routes on its own using the existing 7-via stack. After the swap the four clocks sit on P-side clock-capable balls.
where: Frontend 8L V3 pairs: J1.5/J1.13 with U16/P15 (ASIC8), J2.36/J2.26 with L4/N3 (ASIC7), J1.64/J1.56 with B17/E16 (ASIC4), J2.25/J2.35 with R7/P4 (ASIC3). Matching FPGA-LDO A lanes: J3.12/20, J3.62/70, J4.12/20, J4.62/70.
evidence: Frontend search with its rules (0.09 mm track and clearance, 0.15 mm hole clearance, 0.24 mm hole-to-hole, 0.5 mm edge; JLC spans 1-2/2-3/3-4/4-11/11-12/12-13/13-14; ASIC lanes on L1/L8/L10/L12/L14): J1.5 to P15 2.04 mm, J1.13 to U16 2.18, J2.36 to N3 6.43, J2.26 to L4 5.82, J1.64 to E16 3.01, J1.56 to B17 1.96, J2.25 to P4 9.46, J2.35 to R7 13.07, each with 7-8 vias. FPGA-LDO A: J3.12 to J1.13 11.2 mm, J3.20 to J1.5 12.5, J4.12 to J1.56 19.6 and J4.20 to J1.64 23.0, with vias at (92.82-92.86, 113.8-114.5); J3.62 to J2.26 12.0, J3.70 to J2.36 19.1, J4.70 to J2.25 17.1; J4.62 to J2.35 no path. Ball types from the AMD package file: P15 IO_L11P_T1_SRCC_14, N3 IO_L11P_T1_SRCC_34, E16 IO_L14P_T2_SRCC_15, P4 IO_L12P_T1_MRCC_34.
source: AMD xc7a35tcsg325 package file (12/3/2013): https://download.amd.com/adaptive-socs-and-fpgas/developer/adaptive-socs-and-fpgas/package-pinout-files/a7packages/xc7a35tcsg325pkg.txt. AMD UG472, 7 Series FPGAs Clocking Resources v1.14, single-ended clock on the P side of a clock-capable pair: from memory, not re-read (https://docs.amd.com/v/u/en-US/ug472_7Series_Clocking did not load). Project files: boards/frontend/Artix_Frontend_8L_V3.kicad_pcb, .kicad_dru, .kicad_pro; boards/ldo_a/FPGA_LDO_A_Layout_V12.kicad_pcb. Logs: a review working file (not published) and out/ldoa_swaps.log.
consequence: Doing the swaps on FPGA-LDO A uses up its little free routing space and leaves the ASIC3 clock on R7, a non-clock-capable ball.
suggested_action: Make all 4 swaps on the Frontend V6 copy and leave FPGA-LDO A lanes 12/20/62/70 as they are. Route the swaps together with the 12 new Frontend lines, then run KiCad DRC.

title: An open or wrong SET resistor drives an ASIC rail to about 3.2 V or +/-11.7 V, and nothing clamps it.
what: The LT3042 and LT3094 regulators set their output as 100 uA times one SET resistor to AGND. If that 0402 resistor is open or the wrong value, the output ramps toward the input minus dropout, and every rail goes to all eight ASICs on a head with no clamp. The unused power-good (PG) pins are left the way the data sheet allows, and PG only flags a low output, so wiring it would not catch this fault; the inherited LDO Board A had the same exposure on nine rails. The ASIC's absolute voltage limits are not known, so the files cannot say whether this damages the ASICs; only limits from the ASIC designer would settle it.
where: LDO A and LDO B LDO board: U2/R201 (ASIC_VDD_FE), U6/R601 (ASIC_REF_VDD), U8/R801 (ASIC_REF_VCM), U9/R901 (ASIC_VDD10), U10/R1001 (ASIC_VSS10); rails reach J3/J4 pins 50, 52, 40, 36, 54 directly.
evidence: exports/ldo_a/pads.csv and parts.csv (ldo_b_ldo identical): R201 15k, R601 15k, R801 7.5k, R901 100k, R1001 100k, 1% 0402, from Net-(Ux-SET) to AGND, giving 1.5, 1.5, 0.75, +10 and -10 V; each SET net also has 1 uF (C203, C603, C803 0402; C903, C1003 0603), so an open SET ramps at about 100 uA / 1 uF = 0.1 V/ms. Inputs: U2, U6, U8 on VIN_3V3 (3.32 V from Frontend U16, R59 200k / R60 44.2k, 0.6 V feedback from memory); U9, U10 on STIM_PRE_POS/NEG from LT3582-12 +/-12 V through bridged JP1/JP2. Open-SET output about 3.1-3.2 V or +/-11.7 V. PG pins unconnected, PGFB tied to IN. Only diodes on these boards: D11, D12 B0540WS Schottky; no TVS, zener or clamp. inputs/system/reference_LDO_Board_A/PCB_BOM.csv: nine LT3042 with SET resistors R1-R9, no clamps. ASIC_Nine_Rail_Design_Intent.csv: every voltage window UNKNOWN.
source: ADI LT3042 data sheet (copy footer 3042fa), p.12 Pin Functions (SET, PG, PGFB), p.14 Output Voltage (0 V to VIN minus dropout), p.18 Programmable Power Good, https://www.analog.com/media/en/technical-documentation/data-sheets/lt3042.pdf (direct download timed out; text from the copy in the review scratch folder); LT3094 data sheet, same PG/PGFB guidance; inputs/asic/ASIC_Reference/ASIC_REFERENCE.md items U02/U03.
consequence: One open or swapped 0402 resistor could put an overvoltage at power-up on a rail shared by all eight ASICs of a head; whether they survive is unknown.
suggested_action: Make it a bring-up rule to measure every rail at J3/J4 with no ASIC board mated, after assembly and after any rework. An overvoltage supervisor or clamp is optional and needs the ASIC limits first.

title: Each stack's power crosses one Micro-HDMI contact and one cable wire of unrecorded gauge, with little margin.
what: Each stack gets all its power through one contact, Micro-HDMI pin 19, and one wire in the cable. The Molex receptacle contact is listed at 0.8 A at 25 C; the project estimates 0.27 A expected and 0.55 A high per port, and a constant-power load (regulators that draw more current as their input voltage falls) can reach about 0.65 A on a thin 1 m cable, 81 % of the rating. The port switch passes its full 764 mA only while it is limiting current, which is a fault state. The gauge of the cable's +5 V wire is not recorded, so the files cannot settle the wire and contact heating; naming the cable and measuring loop resistance and temperature at full load would.
where: HDMI Extension Board J610-J617 pin 19 (Molex 467651001, nets PORTn_5V); Frontend J3 pin 19 (net VIN_5V); the cable's +5 V conductor. No other pin carries 5 V (pins 4/7/10/13/16 and the shell are DGND).
evidence: exports/hdmi/connectors.csv and exports/frontend/connectors.csv: pin 19 is the only power pin. exports/hdmi/parts.csv: U701-U708 TPS2553DBVR with R711-R718 37.4k, giving current limits of 637/696/764 mA (min/typ/max, SLVS841G eq. 1-3, p.16-17). inputs/hdmi/power_estimate/START_HERE.md: 0.15/0.27/0.55 A at the 5 V pin. Contact load at the estimates: 34-81 % of 0.8 A (0.65 A case from the V35 cable-drop analysis). Wire heating at 0.55 A: about 0.26 W/m for 34 AWG to 0.41 W/m for 36 AWG. inputs/hdmi/V35_prefab_review/ALL_FINDINGS.md lines 209, 231 and 316-320 already record the 0.8 A rating, the 34 AWG assumption, the 0.65 A at 1 m case and a should-fix cable-drop item.
source: Molex 46765-1001 listing, 0.8 A per contact at 25 C, https://www.molex.com/en-us/products/part-detail/467651001 (page timed out; value from Molex and distributor summaries; Molex specification PS-46765 not read). TI TPS2553 datasheet SLVS841G, eq. 1-3, p.16-17, https://www.ti.com/lit/ds/symlink/tps2553.pdf.
consequence: The contact and cable run warm at high load in a head-mounted, warm setting; contact wear over mating cycles raises resistance and adds to the known cable-drop problem.
suggested_action: Name the cable, including the gauge of its +5 V wire, in the build record, and measure pin-19-to-ground loop resistance and cable temperature at full load (about 0.65 A) before ordering eight.

title: A port in current limit leaves the Frontend browned out, not shut down, and the XEM cannot see the fault.
what: Frontend buck module U16 (MPM3833C) has its enable pin tied straight to VIN_5V, so it keeps running down to its own input lockout of 2.3-2.75 V. If a port's TPS2553 switch limits current, VIN_5V sags and U16 can sit in dropout (input too low to regulate) with VIN_3V3 partly up, while the TPS2553 stays in current limit and cycles on its 135 C thermal shutdown. Each FAULT output drives only an LED, so the XEM8310 cannot see or clear a port fault. A resistor divider on U16 EN would not fix this: EN is a logic input (on above 1.2 V, off only below 0.3 V, internal 1 MOhm pull-down), not a precise threshold.
where: Frontend: U16 pin 4 EN (and pins 13/14) on VIN_5V; U16 pin 12 PG unconnected. HDMI Extension Board: U701-U708 pin 4 FAULT to D701-D708 cathodes only; PORT_ENABLE driven only by U700 PG; R711-R718 37.4k.
evidence: exports/frontend/netlist.xml: VIN_5V (8 nodes) = J3.19, U16.4/13/14, C206/C207/C209, TP14; U16.12 PG unconnected. exports/hdmi/netlist.xml: each Net-(D70x-K) has 2 nodes (U70x.4 FAULT and the LED cathode); PORT_ENABLE has 10 nodes (U700.13 PG, R703, eight EN pins), no XEM pin. MPM3833C Rev 1.0 p.4: UVLO rising 2.3/2.5/2.75 V, 400 mV hysteresis, EN logic low 0.3 V, logic high 1.2 V; p.12: internal 1 MOhm EN pull-down. TPS2553 with 37.4k: limit 637-764 mA; constant-current limiting and thermal turn-off at 135 C minimum while in current limit (sec. 8.3.1, 8.3.6). inputs/hdmi/V35_prefab_review/ALL_FINDINGS.md lines 192-194 and 328-335 already record that FAULT is not seen by the XEM, the cable-drop collapse and EN tied to VIN_5V.
source: MPS MPM3833C datasheet Rev 1.0, p.4 (UVLO, EN thresholds) and p.12 (Enable), https://www.monolithicpower.com/en/mpm3833c.html; TI TPS2553 datasheet SLVS841G, sec. 8.3.1, 8.3.3 and 8.3.6, https://www.ti.com/lit/ds/symlink/tps2553.pdf.
consequence: Partial-power states on the FPGA and ASIC rails, repeated TPS2553 thermal cycling, and data loss that firmware cannot diagnose.
