suggested_action: On the next Frontend spin, put a supervisor or a load switch with a precise UVLO ahead of U16 (not an EN divider), or record that the existing U12/PG reset chain is accepted; on any HDMI board spin, route the eight FAULT outputs (or a wired-OR) to an XEM input.

title: ASIC rail regulators have no set current limit, so a fault shared by eight ASICs can draw 160-730 mA.
what: All five LT3042/LT3094 regulators have their current-limit pin (ILIM) tied to ground, so only their internal limit applies (about 220-320 mA at low input voltage). The four TPS7A2015 regulators have no limit pin; their internal limit is 360-730 mA, folding back to about 160 mA into a hard short. Each regulator feeds all eight ASICs, which normally draw only 1.4-18 mA per rail in total. One resistor on ILIM would cap an LT3042 rail at about 50 mA, but that limit would still be shared by eight ASICs, and no file or datasheet shows that the present limits would fuse bond wires.
where: FPGA-LDO Option A and Option B LDO board: U2, U6, U8, U9 pin 5 ILIM and U10 pin 6 ILIM on AGND (VDD_FE, REF_VDD, REF_VCM, VDD10, VSS10); U3, U4, U5, U7 TPS7A2015 (VDD_ADC, VDD_DRIVER, DVDD, VDD_CGEN).
evidence: exports/ldo_a/pads.csv and exports/ldo_b_ldo/pads.csv: U2.5, U6.5, U8.5, U9.5 and U10.6 ILIM = AGND on both boards. LT3042 data sheet text (a review working file (not published)): internal limit 220/300/320 mA min/typ/max at VIN 2 V, 130/180/250 mA at VIN 20 V; RILIM scale 125 mA*kohm; 45/50/55 mA at RILIM 2.5 kohm. TPS7A20: ICL (DQN) 360/520/730 mA, ISC 160 mA typical at VOUT 0 V. inputs/asic/J3_pinout__Power_Budget.csv: 11.6 mA per board, VDD_FE 4.5 mA per board, VDD10/VSS10 at most 2 mA each per board, REF rails TBD.
source: ADI LT3042 data sheet, ILIM pin function and electrical table (saved copy; revision not confirmed), https://www.analog.com/media/en/technical-documentation/data-sheets/lt3042.pdf; TI TPS7A20 SBVS338H p.7 (ICL, ISC) and section 6.3.4 (foldback); ASIC designer's power budget spreadsheet.
consequence: A latch-up or misplaced probe on one ASIC can draw hundreds of mA from a shared rail instead of tripping a low limit; whether that damages the ASIC is not established.
suggested_action: Decide per LT3042/LT3094 rail whether to fit an ILIM resistor (2.5 kohm gives about 50 mA) after checking ASIC start-up current and, on the stimulation rails, the stimulation current; keep ILIM to AGND where the current is unknown.

title: One open feedback resistor (R700) lets the HDMI board's shared 5 V rail run up to about 12 V, with no overvoltage stop or clamp.
what: R700 is the 40.2 kOhm resistor from the 5 V output to the U700 module's feedback pin. If it is missing, tombstoned or cracked, or if R701 is shorted, the feedback pin sees 0 V and the module drives its output to just below its 12 V input. The module has no overvoltage stop of its own, its power-good output reads the same feedback pin, and nothing clamps FE_5V. Power-good does keep the eight port switches off, but each switch then holds about 12 V on its input against a 7 V absolute maximum, with no stated behaviour. This settles the 'TPS2553 with about 12 V if R700 opens' item in the system not-checked list.
where: HDMI Extension Board V37: U700 TPSM63606 pin 10 (FB). R700 40.2k 0603 at (129.4, 60.9), about 3 mm from the module, from FE_5V to FB. R701 10k from FB to DGND; C708 22 pF across R700. FE_5V feeds U701-U708 (TPS2553) IN; PORT_ENABLE = U700.13 PG; TP700 (FE_5V) at (134.25, 65.5). Downstream: Frontend U16 MPM3833C on VIN_5V.
evidence: exports/hdmi/netlist.xml: Net-(U700-FB) = U700.10, R700.1, R701.2, C708.2. FE_5V = U700.5/8/9, C704-C707 (47 uF), C708, C711-C718, R700, R703, R721-R728, TP700 and U701-U708 IN. No diode, TVS or clamp on FE_5V; the only diodes on the board are D500 (USBLC6-2SC6) and the LEDs D701-D708. Setpoint 1 V x (1 + 40.2k/10k) = 5.02 V. With R700 open, FB sits at 0 V and the output rises toward the input; estimated 11.5-11.9 V at 12 V in. PG is derived from FB (94-107 % window, 120 us filter), so PG stays low and holds PORT_ENABLE low. Hiccup only acts when FB < 40 % during an overload and not during the 3.5-7 ms soft start, so it does not stop the rise at power-up. TPS2553: 7 V absolute maximum on IN and IN-to-OUT.
source: TI TPSM63606 data sheet SLVSGB4B (Oct 2021, revised Apr 2022), read from a local copy: p.1 features (overcurrent and thermal shutdown are the only protections), p.5 absolute maximums (VOUT 16 V), p.7 (hiccup at 40 % FB, not during soft start; soft start 3.5-7 ms), sec. 8.3.2 p.15 (1 V reference; output up to slightly less than VIN), sec. 8.3.9 p.19 (PG from FB, 94-107 %, 120 us). https://www.ti.com/lit/ds/symlink/tpsm63606.pdf . TI TPS2553 SLVS841G sec. 6.1 p.5 (IN, OUT, EN and IN-to-OUT 7 V absolute maximum) and sec. 6.3 (VIN 6.5 V maximum), https://www.ti.com/lit/ds/symlink/tps2553.pdf . MPS MPM3833C Rev 1.0 p.3 (6.5 V absolute maximum, as recorded in FE-19), https://www.monolithicpower.com/en/mpm3833c.html .
consequence: A single bad 0603 puts all eight port switches beyond their rating. If one fails short, about 12 V reaches a Frontend's U16 (6.5 V absolute maximum, 10 V input capacitors), and from there VIN_3V3 and the ASIC regulators. A failure while running also lets FE_5V rise for up to the 120 us PG filter before the ports switch off.
suggested_action: Make 'HDMI board alone: FE_5V at TP700 = 5.0 V and PORT_ENABLE high' the first power-up step of every HDMI board. Before ordering, decide whether to add an FE_5V clamp (for example a TVS that fails short, so U700's hiccup takes over) or to accept and record the single-resistor risk.

title: No record sets a grounding rule for eight stacks on one animal, each tied to base ground by its own cable.
what: On every stack the ASIC analogue ground (AGND, which also carries the ASIC board's one-pin ground pin J1) joins digital ground at the net tie NT1, and that ground runs through the cable shell and ground pins to the HDMI Extension Board ground and on to the PC. All stacks meet at that one point, which is the normal arrangement for multi-headstage recording rigs, so there is no ground loop unless stacks are also joined at the head end, for example through separate ground electrodes in the same animal, a shared frame or another earthed instrument. Each stack's 0.15-0.55 A supply return flows in its own cable, so each stack's ground sits roughly 15-190 mV from the base board ground; the differences between stacks are probably smaller but are not known. No record says how the eight stacks on one animal are to be grounded.
where: ASIC board J1 pin 1 (/AGND; also ASIC REF_1..4 and J3/J4 pins 42/44); FPGA-LDO A NT1 and Option B LDO board NT1 (AGND to GND, the only tie); Frontend J3 pins 4/7/10/13/16 and shell to GND (layers 1-14); HDMI Extension Board J610-J617 pins 4/7/10/13/16 and shells to DGND (layers 1-6), J6 card edge (37 DGND pins).
evidence: exports/asic/pads.csv: J1 (PinHeader_1x01_P1.00mm) pad 1 = /AGND; no part bridges /AGND and /DGND on the ASIC board. exports/ldo_a and ldo_b_ldo pads.csv: NT1.1 = GND, NT1.2 = AGND, the only tie; ldo_b_router has none. exports/frontend/connectors.csv: J3 pins 4/7/10/13/16 and four SH pads = GND. exports/hdmi/connectors.csv: J610-J617 ground pins and SH = DGND; J6 has 37 DGND pins. inputs/hdmi/power_estimate/START_HERE.md: 0.15 / 0.27 / 0.55 A per port at 5 V (low / expected / high). Cable about 1.8-2 m (inputs/hdmi/design_inputs/START_HERE.md; V35_prefab_review/ALL_FINDINGS.md lines 317-327, 34 AWG at 0.86 ohm/m); ground return resistance assumed 0.05-0.35 ohm, braid unknown, not measured, giving about 15-190 mV per stack. U16 MPM3833C switches at 1150 kHz (MPS product page), so the return also carries ripple current. inputs/system/weekly_deck/START_HERE.md: eight stacks on one head. inputs/hdmi/enclosure_V3/START_HERE.md: board in a Thunderbolt adapter on a 12 V supply with one USB-C to the host, so whether the system is earthed depends on the host and adapter.
source: TDT headstage connection guide, sections Overview, Multiple Headstage Configurations and Common Error to Avoid (all headstages on one subject share one ground; separate grounds add noise), https://www.tdt.com/docs/hardware/headstage-connection-guide/ ; engineering judgement.
consequence: If stacks on one animal are given separate ground electrodes, the stack-to-stack offsets drive current through tissue and show up as hum, offset and common-mode noise, with possible electrode corrosion. With a shared ground wire, any offset drives current through that wire and ASIC J1/AGND.
suggested_action: Write a rig grounding rule: one common ground electrode (for example a skull screw) for all stacks on an animal, never separate grounds. With the first two powered stacks, measure the stack-to-stack ground offset, hum, and the current in the shared ground wire and ASIC J1.

title: Each J3/J4 joint has only four ground contacts, all near the middle, for about 60 signals.
what: The inherited ASIC pinout puts AGND on pins 42/44 and GND/DGND on 46/48 and nothing else, so signals near the connector ends are up to 7-8 mm from a return path (the ground contact that carries each signal's return current back). On the FPGA-LDO side 21 (J3) and 23 (J4) of 60 used signals are more than 5 mm from a ground. The files cannot show whether this causes crosstalk; that depends on the ASIC output edge rate and needs a measurement at bring-up. The FPGA-LDO cannot add grounds here without the ASIC designer's agreement.
where: FPGA-LDO A and router (identical) J3/J4, and ASIC board J3/J4: grounds pins 42, 44, 46, 48; spare on both sides pins 2, 4, 6, 8, 24, 58; the FPGA-LDO also leaves pins 3 and 5 open.
evidence: Minimum pin-to-ground distance from exports/ldo_a, exports/ldo_b_router and exports/asic connectors.csv. LDO A J3: 60 signals, max 7.32 mm (pin 7, BOARD3_CLK), 21 over 5 mm; LDO A J4: max 7.47 mm, 23 over 5 mm; router identical. ASIC J3: 62 signals, max 8.2 mm (pin 3, DISC_OUT(2), open on the FPGA-LDO), 25 over 5 mm; ASIC J4: max 8.07 mm, 23 over 5 mm. inputs/asic/J3_pinout__J3_Pinout.csv: 39 Signal, 22 Pass-through, 9 Power, 6 NC, 4 Ground rows.
source: Engineering judgement; inputs/asic/J3_pinout__J3_Pinout.csv (ground assignment).
consequence: Margin on the 32 MHz, 1.5 V CMOS clocks and data depends on the unknown ASIC edge rate; bring-up may show crosstalk on the far lanes.
suggested_action: Ask the ASIC designer whether the six spare pins can be grounded on the ASIC board; if agreed, tie the same pins to GND on the FPGA-LDO.
v2note: Each J3/J4 joint still has only four ground contacts (AGND on pins 42/44, DGND on 46/48), but on both V4 ASIC boards they now serve 67 assigned signal pins, up from 61 on the old board (SYS-23's figures of 62 and 60 counted VDD_CGEN as a signal). Pin map V6 takes FPGA-LDO A and the router from 59 to 65 signals, so 25 (J3) and 27 (J4) are more than 5 mm from a return (worst 8.0 mm, at pin 2), against 29/27 on the ASIC side (worst 8.20 mm). The fix of grounding the six spare pins is gone, because V4 uses pins 2/4/6/8/24/58 for the far chips' READ/DATA outputs. Only pins 3/5 (DISC_OUT, open on the FPGA-LDO) could still become returns, and only if the ASIC designer's DISC_OUT answer (R2S-07) allows it; that would cut J3's count over 5 mm from 29 to 11. Otherwise, measure crosstalk at bring-up. Merge this item with ASIC-20 under R2S-05. See SYS-75.

title: On the ASIC board the clock and strobe lanes switch between the AGND and DGND planes with no tie between them.
what: A fast signal's return current flows in the ground plane right under its trace. On the ASIC board the top-layer clock lanes run over the AGND (analog ground) plane and the bottom-layer lanes over the DGND (digital ground) plane, so at each through via the return current must jump between the two grounds. No capacitor or tie joins AGND and DGND on the board, so the return goes either through the rail decoupling capacitors and the capacitance between the stacked rail planes, or out through the J3/J4 ground contacts to the net tie NT1 on the LDO board. Either way, clock-edge current passes through the analog rails and AGND of a recording chip. How much noise this causes can only be judged by measurement.
where: ASIC board: /CLKH vias at (142.14, 71.25) and (135.76, 84.11); 4 vias each on /STIM_CLK, /SPI_CLK, /SPI_LATCH and 6 on CHIP_RESET, all layers 1-10. F.Cu over In1 /AGND (L2), B.Cu over In8 /DGND (L9). LDO A: NT1 at (100.58, 121.0), 7.53 mm from J3/J4 at (99.78, 113.51).
evidence: Reference-plane scan (a review working file (not published) on a copy of boards/asic/PCB.kicad_pcb), top over AGND / bottom over DGND: CLKH 11.66/27.18 mm; STIM_CLK 4.85/11.52 mm; SPI_CLK 4.06/14.80 mm; SPI_LATCH 4.63/14.10 mm; CHIP_RESET 7.66/35.14 mm. 14 through vias on the four clock/strobe nets (18 with CHIP_RESET). AGND and DGND vias are separate nets. exports/asic/zones.csv: L2 /AGND 325.59 mm2, L3 VDD_FE, L4 REF_VDD, L5 REF_VCM, L6 VDD_DRIVER/VDD10, L7 VDD_ADC/VSS10, L8 DVDD, L9 /DGND 332.88 mm2. exports/asic/pads.csv: 16 placed capacitors go rail to AGND, only C7/C14 go DVDD to DGND; exports/asic/netlist.xml: none of the 50 schematic capacitors joins AGND and DGND. Estimated plane path: about 100 pF between VDD_ADC (L7) and DVDD (L8) across 0.1 mm (er 4.3, 263 mm2), then C7/C14 to DGND. NT1 exists only on ldo_a and ldo_b_ldo.
source: Engineering judgement (return current follows the nearest reference plane; a change of reference plane needs a stitching path close to the via).
consequence: Clock-edge noise in the ASIC analog ground and reference planes, and extra ringing on the clocks; this is outside the edge model of the other signal-integrity findings and only a measurement will show its size.
suggested_action: When the second, not yet drawn ASIC board is laid out, keep clock lanes on the DGND-referenced layer end to end; on the existing board, measure AGND-DGND noise at J3/J4 while CLKH runs, before relying on it for recording.
v2note: SYS-41 is broader and stays minor. On both V4 boards, CLKH, STIM_CLK, CHIP_RESET and each board's own SPI clock and latch switch between AGND-referenced F.Cu and DGND-referenced B.Cu through 2-6 through vias, and no part joins AGND and DGND (26 capacitors go to AGND; only C7/C14/C61/C62 go DVDD to DGND). The V4 0.25 mm plane pull-back also leaves CLKH's 9.84 mm F.Cu run along the bottom edge (y 84.23) straddling the In1 AGND edge on both boards; PCB-5 covered it fully. The far board's In4 segments belong to A-6/R2E-01 (major). Laying out the second board differently is now moot, but three actions remain: get the ASIC designer's answer on the AGND/DGND bond (ASIC_REFERENCE U04), consider a few AGND-DGND capacitors near the layer-change vias or J3/J4, and do the bring-up noise measurement.

title: Even with 20 full ground stacks around J2, 11 west-side J2 lanes keep a 1.06-1.50 mm return path, so the 1.0 mm aim is not reachable there.
what: Only J2.15 and J2.41 accept a full stack directly on the pin's own microvia. The stacks for J2.50, J2.27, J2.66, J2.14 and J2.34 had to move 0.23, 0.27, 0.37, 0.69 and 1.06 mm, because neighbouring lane vias and L8/L10/L12 lanes block the spot beside the pin. Thirteen more stacks fit in the via rows, and all 20 V6 nets still route with every stack in place, so none had to be dropped. West-row positions (x about 102.9-103.0) mostly fail. The ground planes there are thin pockets between the 0.5 mm edge setback and the odd-row anti-pads, so a stack ends up joined to nothing. All 20 placed stacks reach the main fill on L2, L7, L9, L11 and L13.
evidence: Same metric as FE-10, after all changes: 56 J2 transitions, max 1.499 mm, 45 within 1.0 mm, 11 at 1.06-1.50 mm, median 0.80 mm. Before: 58 transitions, all > 1.0 mm, 48 > 3 mm, max 6.84 mm, median 3.96 mm. Remaining lanes over 1.0 mm: ASIC1_READ 1.50, ASIC1_DATA8 1.49, STIM_EN_SHARED 1.49, ASIC1_CLK32MHz_Out 1.26, ASIC1_SYNC 1.23, STIM_CLK_SHARED 1.20, ASIC5_DATA2 1.20, ASIC3_DATA1 1.19, ASIC5_DATA6 1.17, ASIC1_DATA6 1.13, ASIC7_DATA4 1.06. A trial stack at (102.885, 118.595) gave 2 via_dangling warnings and 1 unconnected item in KiCad (out/drc_westrow_trial.json). The stacks alone cost about 4 mm2 (3%) of VIN_3V3 on L4 (out/post_stacks_only.json).
source: Project routing ground rules V1, rule G05, inputs/frontend/routing_rules/ROUTING_GROUND_RULES_V1.md. The 1.0-1.5 mm target comes from FE-10 (engineering judgement). Metric script and data: a review working file (not published), out/stage1_stacks.json, out/stage2_extra.json, out/post_v6_esc12_swapsfirst.json.
consequence: The return detours fall from 3-7 mm to at most 1.5 mm, which mostly removes FE-10's risk. The ASIC1 and STIM lanes that change layer in the west row stay above the 1.0 mm aim.
suggested_action: Use this 7 + 13 stack set (positions in out/r_esc12_swapsfirst.json) in the V6 layout, and record that 1.0-1.5 mm is accepted for the west row. The alternative is to move those lanes' layer changes about 0.3-0.5 mm east to make room.

title: Eight stacks need PCIe Gen3 x4 to the host, but no record states Gen3 or packed samples as a requirement.
what: Eight stacks of eight ASICs produce 12.3 Gb/s (1.54 GB/s) of packed 12-bit samples, or 16.4 Gb/s (2.05 GB/s) if each sample is sent as a 16-bit word, before framing. The only host path that can carry this is the HDMI Extension Board's PCIe x4 link; at Gen2 it cannot carry 16-bit words and has almost no margin for packed data, while Gen3 carries either, and the XEM8310 USB 3 interface is several times too slow. Every part of the chain already supports Gen3 x4 (the FPGA's PCIe block, the Thunderbolt adapter and the board layout), so the open generation is a firmware IP setting plus a bring-up test, not a copper change. The project record states the system rate (about 2 GB/s) but does not tie it to the host-link generation or record a fallback.
where: HDMI Extension Board: J6 card edge lanes 0-3 to MC3 pins 21-36 (XEM8310 GTY quad 225), lanes 4-7 unconnected; XEM8310 PCIe IP and USB 3 host interface; Thunderbolt 3 adapter DFR1169 (enclosure V3).

title: The ASICs are powered about 7 s before the Frontend is configured, with their clock and SPI inputs floating.
what: On both FPGA-LDO A and the Option B LDO board, one RC (R1/C3) enables every ASIC regulator 15-22 ms after VIN_3V3 rises, whatever the FPGA is doing. The Frontend has PUDC_B strapped high, which turns off the FPGA's internal pull-ups during configuration, so the FPGA-driven ASIC clock (CLKH), SPI clock and SPI data lines float at the powered ASICs until configuration ends about 7 s later. Floating CMOS inputs can draw extra current and toggle at random. The files cannot settle whether this is safe, because the ASIC reset polarity and safe input states are unknown; an answer from the ASIC designer would settle it.
where: FPGA-LDO A and Option B LDO board: R1 10k / C3 4.7 uF on /EN_ASIC_RAILS (U1 LT3582 SHDN, U2/U6/U8 LT3042, U9/U10 LT3094, U3/U4/U5/U7 TPS7A2015 EN); R2-R5, R16, R17, R18 10k pull-downs; R19 10k CHIP_RESET_SHARED pull-up to ASIC_DVDD. No pull on any board: BOARD1_CLK, BOARD3_CLK, BOARD1_SPI_CLK, BOARD3_SPI_CLK, STIM_CHIP1..4_SPI_DL/DR (Frontend U1 balls G16, V17, D10, V8, C11, G14, C14, C16, V7, V6, N17, N18; ASIC board CLKH, SPI_CLK, SPI_DINL/DINR). Frontend R25 470R PUDC_B to VCCO_1V5.
evidence: exports/ldo_a/netlist.xml and exports/ldo_b_ldo/netlist.xml: /EN_ASIC_RAILS has 13 nodes (R1, C3, TP4, U1.8, U2-U10). The clock and SPI nets are 2-node nets on every LDO and router board, go straight to U1 balls on the Frontend and reach the ASIC pins with no resistor (exports/asic/netlist.xml). Enable delay t = 47 ms x ln(3.3/(3.3-V)): 15 ms at 0.9 V (TPS7A20 VEN(HI) max) and 22 ms at 1.24 V (LT3042 EN/UV rising, 1.18/1.24/1.32 V). Configuration: U12 hold 1.07 s (TPS3890 1.07 s per uF, C84 1 uF) plus 17,536,096 bits / 3 MHz = 5.85 s, about 7 s in total. inputs/asic/ASIC_Reference/ASIC_REFERENCE.md rows U03/U05 and line 76: reset polarity and pad limits unknown.
source: AMD UG470, 7 Series FPGAs Configuration User Guide: PUDC_B high disables I/O pull-ups during configuration (not opened, docs.amd.com returned 404; from memory). ASIC reference V1, rows U03/U05. Analog Devices LT3042 datasheet, EN/UV threshold row; TI TPS7A20 datasheet, VEN(HI) row; TI TPS3890 datasheet SLVSD65A, p.3.
consequence: Powered ASICs with floating inputs may draw extra current and may clock random data into the configuration shift register, and whether CHIP_RESET held high and FE_RESET held low is a safe state is unknown. Boot also takes about 7 s unless the bitstream raises the configuration clock.
suggested_action: Ask the ASIC designer for the reset polarity and the safe idle state of CLKH and SPI, then add pull-downs on the LDO board for the floating lines rather than setting PUDC_B low, whose weak pull-ups would fight the 10k pull-downs on STIM_EN, STIM_START and FE_RESET. Set BITSTREAM.CONFIG.CONFIGRATE as high as the U8 translator timing allows.
v2note: With the ASIC boards V4, SYS-28 is broader. The far (top) chips have their own SPI clock (pin 72), latch (pin 70) and two data lines per chip (66/68 and 16/18), so pin map V6 adds 6 FPGA-driven lines per port. That is 12 per head stack, or 24 unpulled FPGA-to-ASIC lines with the existing 12, and all of them float for about 7 s while PUDC_B is high. The two new latch lines (T_SPI_LATCH) also lack the 10k pull-down that R18 gives SPI_LATCH_SHARED on FPGA-LDO A and the Option B LDO board. During the V6 re-route, add a pull-down on each far latch (or tie it to SPI_LATCH_SHARED if the ASIC designer confirms the latch may be shared), and decide whether the far SPI clock and data lines need pulls. On today's V5-based files these far-chip inputs sit on FPGA input balls and float permanently, which is part of blocker A-P. See SYS-62.

title: Clock and strobe edges may overshoot the 1.5 V ASIC rail by up to 0.4 V, and the ASIC pad limits are unknown.
what: The FPGA drives the shared clock and strobe lanes with no series resistor, and the ASIC dies at the far ends are light loads, so the edges ring above the 1.5 V rail and below ground. A simple lossless model (no clamp diodes) puts the peak up to about 0.4 V over the rail at a 1.0 ns edge; about 0.6 V is reached only with a pessimistic 5 nH connector loop. That much overshoot is ordinary for unterminated CMOS, and at 0.4 V or less a silicon clamp diode conducts only a little, so current through the input protection on every edge is not shown. The real gap is that the ASIC's input absolute-maximum and clamp limits are not published; only the ASIC designer can say whether the pads tolerate this.
where: U01_BCD1/U01_BCD2 CLKH, SPI_CLK, FPGA_CLK (STIM_CLK), SPI_LATCH, RRST_DIGITAL/RST_DRIVER pads on all four ASIC boards; nets BOARD1/3_CLK, BOARD1/3_SPI_CLK, STIM_CLK_SHARED, SPI_LATCH_SHARED, CHIP_RESET_SHARED.
evidence: a review working file (not published) at 1.0 ns rise, 20-30 ohm source and 0.8 nH contacts, peaks across all seven nets are 1.51 V (SPI_LATCH/STIM_CLK, eight dies, 30 ohm) to 1.93 V (B_BOARD1_CLK, 20 ohm, 2 pF). Re-run (a review working file (not published)): BOARD1_CLK at 1.0 ns/20 ohm gives 1.88 V at 0.8 nH, 2.13 V at 5 nH, 2.20 V at 8 nH; 1.62 V at 30 ohm/0.8 nH; 1.51-1.56 V at 1.5 ns/45 ohm. Undershoot below 0 V is the same size only in this linear model. exports/frontend/nets.csv and exports/ldo_a/nets.csv: no series resistors; LDO A has only 10k resistors to a rail or GND (R5/R18/R19). exports/asic/nets.csv: nets touch only J3/J4/U01_BCD1/U01_BCD2. ASIC_REFERENCE.md line 130: DVDD 1.5 V; line 175 (U03): VIH/VIL, absolute-maximum and clamp limits absent. The 45 ohm for DRIVE 8 is the DS181 worst-case bound (VOL 25 % of VCCO at 8 mA), not a typical value; the SLOW-slew edge rate is not verified (no IBIS model).
source: inputs/asic/ASIC_Reference/ASIC_REFERENCE.md item U03; AMD DS181 Artix-7 Data Sheet v1.27.1, Table 4 (HR I/O overshoot VCCO + 0.55 V and undershoot -0.40 V for 100 % of the unit interval) and Table 8 (LVCMOS15 VOL), engineering judgement.
consequence: If the ASIC pads tolerate only about 0.3 V outside their rail, the upper end of this overshoot could stress the input protection of dies that cannot be replaced, and the damage would be hard to trace.
suggested_action: Ask the ASIC designer for the pad absolute-maximum and clamp ratings. Meanwhile use DRIVE 8 SLEW SLOW and probe CLKH at the far die's bond finger at first power-up with a probe of 1 GHz or more.

title: Pin map V6 gives the top chips their own SPI latch line with no pull-down, so it floats for about 7 s at every power-up while the bottom chips' latch is held low by R18.
what: Under pin map V6 the top (far) chips get their own SPI latch on J3/J4 pin 70, SPI clock on pin 72 and SPI data on pins 16/18/66/68. All six per port are existing two-pin lanes that today carry ASIC outputs and have no resistor, and the V6 change list adds no parts, while the bottom chips keep SPI_LATCH_SHARED on pin 61 with R18 (10k to GND). The ASIC rails are up 15-22 ms after power, but the FPGA leaves its pins undriven with pull-ups off (PUDC_B high) until configuration ends about 7 s later (SYS-28), and again at every reconfiguration, so the top chips' latch and clock float in those windows; V6 adds 12 such floating FPGA outputs per stack to the 12 in SYS-28. Because the assembler does not program the boot flash, a new Frontend (or one with a bad image) never configures, and these lines then float until a bitstream arrives over JTAG.
where: FPGA-LDO A (and the Option B router and LDO board if kept): J3/J4 pins 16, 18, 66, 68 (top SPI data), 70 (T_SPI_LATCH; today /ASIC3_CLK32MHz_Out on the J2.35-J4.70 lane and /ASIC7_CLK32MHz_Out on J2.26-J3.70) and 72 (T_SPI_CLK; today /ASIC3_SYNC and /ASIC7_SYNC). If the four planned clock swaps are made on FPGA-LDO A, the latch moves to the lanes that today carry /ASIC3_DATA8 (J2.25-J4.62) and /ASIC7_DATA8 (J2.36-J3.62). Pin 61: /SPI_LATCH_SHARED with R18 10k (J2.48, J3.61, J4.61). Frontend: balls P4/N3 (R7/L4 after the swaps); U7 W25Q128JWYIQ boot flash; PUDC_B pulled high through R25.
evidence: exports/ldo_a/netlist.xml and nets.csv: /SPI_LATCH_SHARED = J2.48, J3.61, J4.61, R18.1 (R18 10k to GND), which reaches the near board's /SPI_LATCH (exports/asic_bottom/connectors.csv). Two-node lanes with no other part: /ASIC3_CLK32MHz_Out = J2.35, J4.70; /ASIC3_SYNC = J2.37, J4.72; /ASIC7_CLK32MHz_Out = J2.26, J3.70; /ASIC7_SYNC = J2.24, J3.72; /ASIC3_DATA8 = J2.25, J4.62; /ASIC7_DATA8 = J2.36, J3.62; the ASIC3/4/7/8 DATA5/6 lanes are the same. known/pinmap_v6_trace.csv: these 12 rows (A/J3/70, A/J3/72, A/J4/70, A/J4/72 and the SPI data rows) become ASIC3_4 and ASIC7_8 TOP_SPI_LATCH and TOP_SPI_CLK and ASIC3/4/7/8 SPI_DR/SPI_DL, dir out, status 'rename (existing line)'. exports/asic_top/netlist.xml and pads.csv: both top chips' SPI_LATCH are on /T_SPI_LATCH (J3.70/J4.70), and pins 70 and 72 reach both far dies. The V6 change list in known/asic_open.json A-P (12 new routes plus 4 clock swaps) adds no resistor. Frontend_V46_pins_V2.xdc sets no PULLUP or PULLDOWN; Frontend R25 470R ties PUDC_B to VCCO_1V5 (SYS-28). inputs/frontend/V3_order/JLC_ORDER_NOTES.txt: the assembly remark asks for no flash programming, and U7 is still to be sourced. ASIC_REFERENCE.md section 4: SPI_LATCH is a positive pulse, so it idles low. Per stack in V6: 12 existing floating FPGA outputs (SYS-28) plus 12 new = 24.
source: AMD UG470 v1.17, 7 Series FPGAs Configuration User Guide, Table 2-4 p.22 ('When PUDC_B is High, internal pull-up resistors are disabled'), https://docs.amd.com/v/u/en-US/ug470_7Series_Config . inputs/asic/ASIC_Reference/ASIC_REFERENCE.md section 4; boards/asic_bottom/CHANGES.md (SPI_CLK 63 and SPI_LATCH 61 serve the near board's chips only); known/pinmap_v6_trace.csv; exports/ldo_a/netlist.xml; known/system.json SYS-28 (about 7 s unconfigured); engineering judgement.
consequence: Noise on the floating latch can copy random shift-register contents into the four top ASICs' configuration at every boot and reconfiguration. Stimulation stays off only while the ASIC honours STIM_EN held low by R2; after that, because the stimulation lines are shared (see the finding on shared STIM lines), such a chip can stimulate when another chip does unless firmware first rewrites every top chip's configuration. A first bring-up with a blank flash leaves all eight ASICs powered with floating clock and SPI inputs for as long as the head is on.
suggested_action: In the V6 FPGA-LDO A change, add a 10k pull-down to GND beside R18 on each of the two new top-latch nets (J3.70, J4.70), and on the Option B board that carries R18 if Option B is kept; add the two top SPI clock nets (pin 72) to SYS-28's pull-down list. Program each Frontend's flash before any bonded ASIC board is mated.

title: Under pin map V6 as traced, ASIC3 and ASIC7 each bring READ, DATA7 and DATA8 into a different FPGA bank from their returned clock, breaking the Frontend's one-bank-per-ASIC rule.
what: The Frontend was laid out so each ASIC's returned clock sits on a clock-capable ball in the same bank as its other ten lines, so each chip can be captured on its own I/O clock buffer, which reaches only its own bank (BUFIO) or its own clock region (BUFR). In V6 the far chips' READ, DATA8 and DATA7 come in on J3/J4 pins 28/30/32, whose lanes end on Frontend J1, so even after the four clock swaps ASIC3's clock is on P4 (bank 34) while its T_READ, T_D<8> and T_D<7> arrive on F18, F17 and G17 (bank 15), and ASIC7's clock is on N3 (bank 34) while the same three lines arrive on M16, L14 and K15 (bank 14). Bank 34 has only K5 and K6 free, the nearest balls for the two new DATA6 lines, and restoring one bank per group would mean moving 6 outputs and 6 inputs across the BGA; ASIC8 and ASIC4 can stay whole in banks 14 and 15. Capture still works at 32 MHz on a global clock buffer with timing constraints, so this constrains the firmware and the V6 routing choice; it is not a failure.
where: Frontend U1 banks 14, 15 and 34. ASIC7: READ/DATA8/DATA7 on M16, L14, K15 (bank 14); the rest on K3, N3, M5, P6, P5, R6, R1 and K5 (bank 34). ASIC3: READ/DATA8/DATA7 on F18, F17, G17 (bank 15); the rest on T2, P4, T3, N6, N2, M6, L5 and K6 (bank 34). Returned clocks after the swaps: P4 (IO_L12P_T1_MRCC_34) and N3 (IO_L11P_T1_SRCC_34). FPGA-LDO A: J4 pins 28/30/32 go to J1.48/46/44, and J3 pins 28/30/32 go to J1.21/23/25. Spare joint contacts J2.40/J2.42; free bank-34 balls K5/K6. The rule is stated in inputs/frontend/V2_review_fixes/Frontend_V46_pins_V2.xdc line 2 and in the schematic V46 J1/J2 note.
evidence: a review working file (not published) over exports/{asic_top,asic_bottom,ldo_a,frontend}/netlist.xml and known/pinmap_v6_trace.csv, with ball names from AMD's package file: ASIC3's bank-15 balls F18 (IO_L19N_T3_A21_VREF_15), F17 (IO_L24P_T3_RS1_15) and G17 (IO_L19P_T3_A22_15); ASIC7's bank-14 balls M16 (IO_L7P_T1_D09_14), L14 (IO_0_14) and K15 (IO_L5N_T0_D07_14). The trace keeps rows A,J3,28/30/32 on J1.21/23/25 and A,J4,28/30/32 on J1.48/46/44. Free user I/O counted from exports/frontend/pads.csv: bank 14 has 14, bank 15 has 14, bank 34 has 2 (K5, K6). Frontend J2 spares are only 40 and 42; J1 has 13. In the Frontend search, ASIC8's 5 new lines reach J14/K17/T12/T13/U12 (1.1-7.7 mm) and ASIC4's reach F15/G15/H16/F14/H14 (0-1.2 mm). XDC line 2 reads 'CLK32 returns sit on P-side MRCC/SRCC balls in their group bank'; the schematic V46 J1/J2 note says each ASIC group (CLK32 + SYNC + READ + 8 data) sits in one FPGA bank with its clock on a P-side MRCC/SRCC ball. Global-buffer timing: DS181 Table 44 gives 2.65 ns setup / -0.29 ns hold at the pins (XC7A35T, -2) against a 15.6 ns half period.
source: AMD xc7a35tcsg325 package file (12/3/2013), https://download.amd.com/adaptive-socs-and-fpgas/developer/adaptive-socs-and-fpgas/package-pinout-files/a7packages/xc7a35tcsg325pkg.txt . AMD UG953 7 Series Libraries Guide, BUFIO (drives only I/O in its own bank) and BUFR (drives I/O and logic in its own clock region), read from AMD page text in search results because the pages did not load directly: https://docs.amd.com/r/2022.2-English/ug953-vivado-7series-libraries/BUFIO and https://docs.amd.com/r/2023.2-English/ug953-vivado-7series-libraries/BUFR . AMD UG472 v1.14 (BUFMR only vertically adjacent regions): from memory, not re-read (https://docs.amd.com/v/u/en-US/ug472_7Series_Clocking did not load). AMD DS181 v1.27.1 Table 44 p.45, https://docs.amd.com/v/u/en-US/ds181_Artix_7_Data_Sheet . Project files: known/pinmap_v6_trace.csv; inputs/frontend/V2_review_fixes/Frontend_V46_pins_V2.xdc; boards/frontend/Artix_Frontend_8L_V3.kicad_sch (V46 J1/J2 note); exports/frontend/pads.csv.
consequence: Firmware written to the recorded V5 rule (each chip on its own regional I/O clock with IOB flip-flops, R2S-09) will not place for ASIC3 and ASIC7, which have to be captured differently. Without clock and input-delay constraints the 32 MHz capture margin is not checked. If the two new DATA6 lines are routed through J1 spares, they also land outside bank 34.
suggested_action: In the V6 plan, route the two new DATA6 lines through J2.40/J2.42 to K5/K6 (J4.58 first needs an exit on FPGA-LDO A; see the finding on the V6 lane field). Then either swap LDO A pins 28/30/32 with three of the bank-34 lanes V6 gives to the top SPI outputs (J2.31/33/37 for ASIC3, J2.24/28/30 for ASIC7), or record that ASIC3 and ASIC7 are captured on a global clock buffer (BUFG or MMCM). In the V6 pin file, correct the header, add create_clock and input-delay constraints for all eight returned clocks, set DRIVE/SLEW on the 12 new outputs (SYS-51), and replace R2S-09's firmware map with the V6 one: separate SPI for every chip (8 data streams, four SPI clocks, three latches), SPI_LATCH_SHARED and BOARD1/3_SPI_CLK loading only the bottom chips, and STIM_CHIP3/STIM_CHIP4 driving ASIC5/ASIC6.

title: Paste openings on every DF40 land pattern equal the pad, where Hirose recommends an 80 % opening.
what: The solder paste openings in the stencil (the metal sheet that prints paste onto the pads) are the same size as the copper pads on every DF40 connector in the stack. Hirose recommends a 0.12 mm stencil with an 80 % opening on both the receptacle (DS) and header (DP) halves, and warns that excess solder and flux can wick into the contacts. No pad, footprint or board paste margin or ratio is set anywhere, and the order notes give no stencil instruction.
where: Frontend J1/J2 (bottom); LDO A J1/J2/J3 (top) and J4 (bottom); LDO B board J1/J2/J5 (top); router J3 (top) and J4/J5 (bottom); ASIC board J3 (bottom) and J4 (top).
evidence: pcbnew (KiCad 10.0.6) on every board: board paste margin 0 and ratio 0; every DF40 footprint and pad margin and ratio None, so paste = pad. DS pads 0.20 x 0.70 mm; DP pads 0.23 x 0.66 mm plus 0.35 x 0.66 mm hold-downs. Gerbers: inputs/frontend/V3_order/gerber_files B_Paste ADD26 R,0.200X0.700 and ADD25 R,0.700X0.200; LDO A V12 F_Paste ADD10 RoundRect (outer 0.23 x 0.66) and ADD11 R 0.35 x 0.66. JLC_Remarks_paste.txt and JLC_ORDER_NOTES.txt give no stencil or aperture instruction.
source: Hirose DF40 Series catalog (2014 copy), p16, Operating Precautions item 3 (stencil 0.12 mm, opening ratio DS 80 %, DP 80 %) and item 6 (excess flux, solder and flux wicking), https://www.hirose.com/en/product/series/DF40 (hirose.com returned 403; read from a re-hosted copy of the Hirose catalog).
consequence: Higher chance of bridged or wicked contacts at 0.4 mm pitch, on joints that are hard to inspect once mated.
suggested_action: Set a -20 % paste ratio on the DF40 pads, or tell the assembler in the order notes to use 80 % apertures on every DF40.

title: In Option B the Frontend sits 0.525 mm from the router, on the edge where its order notes put break-off tabs.
what: In Option B the router and the Frontend both plug into the top of the LDO board through 1.5 mm DF40 pairs, so they sit side by side at the same height. Their facing edges are 0.525 mm apart. The Frontend order notes ask the factory to put break-off tabs (small strips that hold a board in its panel and are snapped off after assembly) on exactly that edge, so a tab remnant could close most of the gap. Option A is not affected.
where: Option B: router y-max edge at y 122.935 (its own file); Frontend south edge at y 121.92 in its own file, y 123.46 in the LDO-board frame; overlap x 88.70-111.29.
evidence: exports/ldo_b_router/board.json: edge y 122.935 from x 85.833 to 113.733. exports/frontend/board.json: outline x 102.21-124.8, y 96.5-121.92. Mapping (x, y) -> (213.5 - x, 245.38 - y) checked on J1 (122.245, 112.57) -> (91.255, 132.81) and J2 (104.745, 112.57) -> (108.755, 132.81), matching ldo_b_ldo J1/J2; the Frontend spans y 123.46-148.88, so the gap is 123.46 - 122.935 = 0.525 mm. inputs/ldo_b/V2_fit/fit_b.json: router z 1.5-3.1, Frontend z 1.5-3.032. inputs/ldo_b/V2_record/START_HERE.md line 31 already records a 0.50 mm router-to-Frontend edge gap at the same height. inputs/frontend/V3_order/JLC_ORDER_NOTES.txt line 13 asks for break-off tabs on the south and east edges only.

consequence: If Option B is built with the current Frontend order notes, a tab remnant, edge burr or small connector placement error could make the two boards touch and stop the Frontend from seating.
suggested_action: If Option B is used, move the Frontend break-off tabs to the north or east edge, or ask for the south edge to be routed and sanded clean.

title: Neither the Frontend nor the FPGA-LDO A order asks for the 0.02 mm board flatness Hirose requires under each DF40, although both boards carry unbalanced copper.
what: Hirose allows at most 0.02 mm of board warpage at the centre of each DF40, measured against the connector's ends. Over these 16.6-18.6 mm connectors that is about four to six times tighter than a common 0.75 % bow allowance. Every head joint has only 0.45 mm of effective engagement, and the Frontend-to-LDO joint uses two parallel 70-pin pairs. The Frontend has more plane copper above its centre core than below it, FPGA-LDO A pairs a 71 % plane with a 13 % signal layer, and the ASIC boards carry 63 % top against about 20 % bottom outer copper. No order note states a flatness or bow/twist limit, and JLC publishes none.
where: Frontend J1/J2 (DF40C-70DS, bottom; 16.6 mm bodies, 17.5 mm apart). FPGA-LDO A J1/J2 (70DP, top), J3 (80DP, top) and J4 (80DS, bottom). ASIC V4 J3/J4 (18.6 mm). Order notes: inputs/frontend/V3_order/JLC_ORDER_NOTES.txt and inputs/ldo_a/V12_order/JLC_Remarks_paste.txt.
evidence: Per-layer copper = pours (exports/<board>/zones.csv) plus track area (board.json), outer pads excluded. Frontend L1-L14: 8, 81, 78, 71, 3, 2, 78, 3, 78, 5, 78, 5, 81, 4 %. Mirror pairs are unbalanced at L3/L12 (78/5), L6/L9 (2/78) and L7/L8 (78/3, across the centre core); planes sit on L2/L3/L4/L7 above the core against L9/L11/L13 below; the dielectric stack is symmetric (exports/frontend/stackup.txt). LDO A L1-L6: 39, 71, 89, 89, 13, 51 %. ASIC V4: L2-L9 75-85 %; F.Cu 237 mm2 (63 %) against B.Cu 67 / 79 mm2 (18 / 21 %) (board_stats.txt). Bow arithmetic (a review working file (not published)): a 0.75 % bow sags 0.081 mm over a 16.6 mm DF40 on the 25.42 mm Frontend and 0.118 mm over 18.6 mm on the 22 mm ASIC board; Hirose's 0.02 mm equals about a 0.13-0.27 % bow. The order notes only ask that via-in-pad pads be 'flat and solderable'. The JLC capabilities page gives thickness ±10 % and outline ±0.1 / 0.2 mm, but no warpage figure.
source: Hirose DF40 Series catalog, Jun 1 2024: p21 (board warpage 0.02 mm max at the centre relative to both connector ends; 2 reflows max) and p8 (A = 16.6 mm for 70 positions, 18.6 mm for 80), LCSC copy https://datasheet.lcsc.com/datasheet/pdf/145ab5d527b34eafa7a47375cb561c6a.pdf?productCode=C3640153. JLCPCB PCB capabilities, https://jlcpcb.com/capabilities/pcb-capabilities. The 0.75 % IPC-6012 SMT bow/twist figure is from memory, not re-read (paid standard).
consequence: A board bowed beyond 0.02 mm across a DF40 can leave centre joints open after reflow. Two bowed boards also mate J1 and J2 unevenly inside the 0.45 mm engagement. Either fault would show only at bring-up as intermittent lines.
suggested_action: Add to both order notes: 'flatness 0.02 mm max across each DF40 footprint (Hirose DF40 p21); please state your bow/twist limit'. Ask JLC whether it will add balancing copper on Frontend L8/L12 and LDO A L5, kept away from controlled lanes. Check the first bare boards on a surface plate before assembly.

title: The FPGA-LDO A order leaves break-off tab positions to JLC, although J1/J2 sit 0.88 mm from both long edges and only short edge stretches meet JLC's own tab keep-out.
what: At 22.64 x 36.76 mm, FPGA-LDO A must be assembled in a JLC panel. The order remark asks JLC to add rails, fiducials and tooling holes but does not say where the break-off tabs go. Both long edges carry a 70-pin, 0.4 mm-pitch DF40 header only 0.88-0.89 mm in along 14.9 mm, J3/J4 sit 1.29-1.49 mm from the short edge, and 0402 parts sit 0.31-0.34 mm from three edges. JLC's own guidance asks for 1.5 mm between a tab and any pad and no tabs at connectors, so leaving the choice to JLC risks the problem FE-07 found on the Frontend.
where: FPGA-LDO A V12 outline x 88.68-111.32, y 110.34-147.10. J1 pads x 89.57-92.94 and J2 pads x 107.07-110.44, both over y 119.55-134.45. J4 pads from y 111.63 and J3 pads from y 111.83. C301/C302 0.31 mm from the east edge; R6 0.33 mm from the south edge; C16 0.34 mm from the north edge.
evidence: a review working file (not published) run on pcbnew pads and courtyards (fps_all.json). Clear stretches at a 1.5 mm courtyard keep-off: west y 115.95-118.69 (2.7 mm), 137.9-139.5 and 144.9-147.1; east y 112.42-115.53 (3.1 mm) and 135.31-139.78 (4.5 mm); north x 88.68-91.70 (3.0 mm) and 94.89-98.00 (3.1 mm); south only x 88.68-89.94. inputs/ldo_a/V12_order/JLC_Remarks_paste.txt lines 6-7 and 20-21: panel by JLC, 'for example 3 x 2 boards with 5 mm rails on the two short sides', 'please add rails, fiducials and tooling holes', closest courtyard 0.14 mm from the edge; no tab positions are given.
source: JLCPCB blog 'Mouse Bites in PCBs: Easy Solutions for Clean Separation and Professional Results', 20 Mar 2026 (1.5 mm keep-out between tab edge and nearest pad; keep tabs away from connectors, at least 2 mm if unavoidable), https://jlcpcb.com/blog/pcb-mouse-bites. Hirose DF40 catalog Jun 1 2024, p21 (0.02 mm board warpage at the connector), LCSC copy https://datasheet.lcsc.com/datasheet/pdf/145ab5d527b34eafa7a47375cb561c6a.pdf?productCode=C3640153. Known FE-07 (same issue on the Frontend).
consequence: Snapping a tab beside J1/J2 bends the board at a 0.4 mm-pitch joint that the Frontend re-mates every session. It can crack those joints or the edge 0402 capacitors, and the damage may show only as an intermittent ASIC line.
suggested_action: Name the tab positions in the order, for example the east stretch y 135.3-139.8 and the north stretches x 88.7-91.7 / 94.9-98.0, or draw the panel. Ask JLC not to place any tab within 2 mm of J1-J4.

title: ASIC board J3/J4 have no part number, and their land pattern also fits taller DF40 parts that alter the stack.
what: Every gap in the head stack assumes the ASIC board uses the 1.5 mm mated-height Hirose DF40 pair, but J3 and J4 are generic Conn_02x40_Odd_Even symbols with no manufacturer part number and an empty Datasheet field; no ASIC board part has one. Only the footprint names and the ASIC designer's spreadsheet point to the 1.5 mm part. Hirose uses the same receptacle land pattern (the copper pad layout on the board) for 80-pin parts at 1.5 mm, 2.0 mm and 3.0-4.0 mm, so the board files alone do not fix the mated height.
where: ASIC board J3 (bottom, footprint Hirose_DF40C-80DS-0.4V_2x40_P0.4mm, at 135.54, 71.01) and J4 (top, footprint Hirose_DF40C-80DP-0.4V_2x40-1MP_P0.4mm, at 135.54, 71.005); J3/J4 symbols in PCB.kicad_sch.
evidence: exports/asic/parts.csv: J3/J4 value Conn_02x40_Odd_Even, Datasheet empty, no MPN column for any part. boards/asic/PCB.kicad_sch near line 19153: J4 has only Reference, Value, Footprint and an empty Datasheet. inputs/asic/J3_pinout__Summary.csv lines 2-3: 'J3 - Hirose DF40C-80DS-0.4V receptacle' (not part of the board BOM). Hirose DF40 catalog: receptacle pattern 3.78 +0.05 / 2.38 mm on p.8 (1.5 mm, DF40C-80DS), p.9 (2.0 mm, DF40C(2.0)-80DS) and p.10 (3.0-4.0 mm, DF40HC(x.x)-80DS); no 80-pin receptacle at 2.5 mm (pp.10-11).
source: Hirose DF40 Series catalog, Feb. 2024, pp.8-11 (recommended PCB patterns and part tables), https://www.hirose.com/en/product/series/DF40.
consequence: An assembler or buyer can fit a 2.0 mm or taller receptacle; all stack clearances and the side-by-side fit with the Frontend then change.
suggested_action: Put DF40C-80DS-0.4V(51) on J3 and DF40C-80DP-0.4V(51) on J4 in the ASIC board's schematic fields, BOM and assembly notes.

title: No HDMI cable is specified, yet its plug must be under about 9.2 mm thick at the head and about 13 mm wide.
what: No record names an HDMI cable model. At the head, the Micro-HDMI plug hangs over a 4.0 mm strip of the FPGA-LDO board that sticks out past the Frontend's edge; a plug moulding thicker than about 9.2 mm rests on that strip. On the HDMI Extension Board the eight ports sit on a 13.1 mm pitch, so plug mouldings wider than about 13 mm cannot sit side by side.
where: Frontend J3 (Molex 46765-1001, top side, rotation 180). FPGA-LDO strip past the Frontend edge: Option A y 143.07-147.10, Option B y 148.88-152.94; the strip's top side carries test points TP1-TP9. HDMI Extension Board J610-J617 at x 67.08, y 145.3 down to 53.6.
evidence: Molex SD-46765-001 sheet 1 (a review working file (not published)): interface point 1.53 mm above the PCB, height 2.90 mm (3.05 max at the latch). Frontend thickness 1.574 mm (stack-up 1.594 mm). Clearance plug-to-strip = 1.5 + 1.574 + 1.53 - T/2 = 4.60 - T/2 mm, zero at T about 9.2 mm (9.25 mm with 1.594). Frontend edge maps to LDO-A y 143.07 (edge 147.10) and LDO-B y 148.88 (edge 152.935). exports/hdmi/parts.csv: J610-J617 in 13.1 mm steps. Enclosure V3 fitcheck.json checked a '12x8 overmold'. inputs/hdmi/power_estimate/START_HERE.md plans a cable fit test but names no cable.
source: Molex SD-46765-001, sheet 1; Engineering judgement.
consequence: A bulky cable rests on the FPGA-LDO test-point strip and adds leverage on the DF40 connectors, or will not fit side by side on the HDMI Extension Board.
suggested_action: Write a cable spec (Micro-HDMI both ends, plug moulding at most about 12.5 mm wide and 8.5 mm thick, length and power-wire size from the power review) and check samples against a printed stack.

title: Each stacked ASIC board's J1 pin tail lands on the J1 below and holds two DF40 joints about 0.24 mm open.
what: J1 on the ASIC board is a single 1.00 mm right-angle pin on AGND whose tail goes through the board. All four ASIC boards put J1 at the same x/y, so in KiCad's generic 3D model each upper board's tail comes down onto the bent lead of the J1 below. That holds the DF40 board-to-board joint between those two boards about 0.24 mm short of fully mated, about half of its 0.45 mm effective mating length (the travel over which the contacts touch). Both pins are AGND, so this is a seating problem, not a short; the pin has no part number, so the real tail length is unknown and only the chosen pin's drawing can settle the true overlap.
where: ASIC board J1 (PinHeader_1x01_P1.00mm_Horizontal, /AGND, 0.85 mm pad, 0.5 mm drill), top side at (144.875, 68.28); at (90.448, 116.243) in the LDO A / router frame. Affects the ASIC1-ASIC2 and ASIC3-ASIC4 joints in both Option A and Option B.
evidence: Stock KiCad model PinHeader_1x01_P1.00mm_Horizontal.step (parsed): vertical pin z -2.55 to +0.785 mm, horizontal lead z 0.485 to 0.785 mm out to x +3.3 mm, body z 0 to 1.27 mm. Board thickness 1.6 mm (boards/asic/PCB.kicad_pcb, exports/asic/board_stats.txt, inputs/asic/pcbway_fab/PCB-job.gbrjob BoardThickness 1.6); DF40 stack gap 1.5 mm. Upper tail end above lower board top = 1.5 + 1.6 - 2.55 = 0.55 mm; lower lead top 0.785 mm, so overlap = 0.235 mm. inputs/ldo_b/V2_fit/fit_b_v2.json lists the same 0.24 mm for both ASIC pairs. Body to board above = 1.5 - 1.27 = 0.23 mm (nominal, generic model). The lowest ASIC tail clears the LDO A / router top by 0.55 mm. The 0.8 mm thickness appears only in the weekly deck's display profile, not in any fab file; at 0.8 mm the pin-on-pin overlap would be about 1.04 mm, and only then would ASIC1's tail reach LDO A L1, where the nearest foreign track (/ASIC6_DATA1) is 0.65 mm from the tail centre. exports/asic/parts.csv: J1 has no MPN.
source: Hirose DF40 Series catalog, Feb. 2024, p2 (effective mating length 0.45 mm at 1.5 mm stacking height), p8 and p14 (heights), read from the LCSC copy https://datasheet.lcsc.com/datasheet/pdf/145ab5d527b34eafa7a47375cb561c6a.pdf?productCode=C3640153 (series page https://www.hirose.com/en/product/series/DF40); engineering judgement for the pin.
consequence: If assembled with an uncut long-tail pin, the ASIC1-ASIC2 and ASIC3-ASIC4 DF40 joints sit about half their effective mating length short, and contacts may be intermittent.
suggested_action: Add an assembly rule to trim J1's tail to about 0.5 mm below the board, or fit a short-tail or SMT pin (or J1 on one board only), then check the 0.23 mm body clearance against the chosen pin's drawing. No PCB change is needed.

title: DF40 joints are rated for 30 mating cycles, and no record says how often each stack will be unplugged.
what: Hirose rates every DF40 for 30 mate/unmate cycles, with contact resistance at most 90 mOhm after them; nothing is specified beyond 30. The removable joints are the Frontend on the LDO A in Option A and the plug-in LDO board on the router in Option B, and the half that stays on the head wears with every swap. Several records state the 30-cycle rating, but none says how many unplugs are expected or keeps a mate count. This is a usage decision, not a board defect.
where: Option A: Frontend J1/J2 mated to LDO A J1/J2 (70 positions). Option B: LDO board J5 mated to router J5 (120 positions).
evidence: Hirose DF40 catalog, 2014 copy, p2: rated current 0.3 A; item 7 Durability, 90 mOhm max, 30 mating cycles. Hirose DF40 catalog, Jun. 1, 2024 copy, p5: mating durability 90 mOhm max, 30 times; rated current 0.3 A, 0.25 A for 120 positions. The 30-cycle rating is recorded in inputs/asic/sandwich_hub_options/START_HERE.md line 16, inputs/ldo_b/history/17_FPGA_LDO_B_Floorplan_V1_and_J5_Pin_Map_V2/START_HERE.md line 44, inputs/ldo_a/parts_review_V21/index.html (J5 row) and inputs/notes/fpga-ldo-v14.md line 52. inputs/system/weekly_deck/START_HERE.md assumes the Option A split (Frontend unplugs). No record gives an expected unplug count.
source: Hirose DF40 Series catalog, 2014 copy, p2 item 7; Hirose DF40 Series catalog, Jun. 1, 2024, p5, https://www.hirose.com/en/product/series/DF40 (read from an LCSC-hosted copy).
consequence: Past 30 cycles the contact resistance is no longer guaranteed, so the head-permanent board may need replacing after repeated swaps.
suggested_action: Decide the expected number of unplugs per stack and keep a mate count per board at bring-up; if it exceeds the budget, plan to disconnect at the HDMI cable instead.

title: ASIC boards cannot be unplugged as Hirose requires, and Option A traps the FPGA-LDO board between ASIC pairs.
what: Each ASIC board's DF40 connector sits near one long edge, with about 11.8 mm of board, dies and probes beyond it across the connector's width. With other boards 1.5 mm above and below, and only about 2.5-2.9 mm of board past each end of the connector, lifting a board evenly needs a thin tool; lifting the far end rocks the connector across its width, which Hirose prohibits. In Option A, replacing the FPGA-LDO board means unplugging the Frontend and both ASIC pairs, though each pair can come off as a mated unit.
where: ASIC board: Edge.Cuts y 67.44-84.47; J3/J4 body about y 69.3-72.7 (J3 pads x 127.74-143.34, J4 pads x 127.27-143.82). FPGA-LDO Option A: J3 (DF40C-80DP, top) and J4 (DF40C-80DS, bottom) at (99.783, 113.51); J1/J2 take the Frontend.
evidence: boards/asic/PCB.kicad_pcb Edge.Cuts x 124.34-146.31, y 67.44-84.47; exports/asic/pads.csv J3 pads y 69.47-72.55; 84.47 - 72.7 = 11.8 mm beyond the connector. exports/ldo_a/parts.csv: J3 and J4 both at (99.783, 113.51). Hirose DF40 unmating precautions (a review working file (not published)): lift evenly with both sides parallel; one-side lifting only on a very rigid board; do not pull on one side or a corner or from the width direction; connector is not meant as the main support.
source: Hirose DF40 Series catalog, Feb. 2024 (LCSC copy), pp. 21 and 23, unmating precautions; same content re-checked in a 2014 catalog text, pp. 17-18 of that copy; https://www.hirose.com/en/product/series/DF40.
consequence: Prying from the probe end can crack the DF40 housing or lift pads and puts tools next to bond wires and probe shanks. Option A service means handling the Frontend and two mated ASIC pairs.
suggested_action: Before stacking boards with ASICs, define a spreader tool that separates boards evenly along the connector's long side and a written mate/unmate order, and weigh this in the Option A/B choice.

title: Enclosure V3 sets the HDMI Extension Board's height twice, by base posts and by the adapter's PCIe slot.
what: In enclosure V3 the board is clamped between nine base posts and lid pins, and its card edge is also seated in the DFR1169 adapter's x16 slot, which is screwed to the back wall. So two separate chains of printed-part and vendor-part tolerances both fix the board's height (it is over-constrained). In plane, the board is also located twice, by a pin in one mounting hole and by the slot. Each Micro-HDMI insertion can push up to 44.1 N in plane, a load the record has not checked; holes MH2/MH3 exist on V37 but are not used.
where: Enclosure V3: nine base posts (board underside z 0) and lid pins; adapter slot centre plane z 0.8 mm on 6 mm pillars, slot mouth y 154.454, nominal seating 7.6 mm; card fingers x 109.68-160.98; locating pin in the 3.5 mm hole at (164.68, 100.05); HDMI Extension Board V37 MH2/MH3.
evidence: Desktop record 14_HDMI_Extension_Board_Enclosure_V3/review/enclosure_meta.json: nine posts; adapter zmid 0.8, pcb_t 1.6, mouth y 154.454, pillar 6.0, four screw holes. Its START_HERE.md: 'Seating depth is nominal (7.6 mm)'; adapter size from the vendor drawing only; MH2/MH3 'could take screws in a later revision'. V2 START_HERE line 93: clamped between posts and lid pins, 'Not tested against cable pull.' Molex 46765 product specification section 5.2 item 9 (a review working file (not published)): insertion force 44.1 N max.
source: Molex 46765 product specification, section 5.2 item 9 (insertion force); Engineering judgement.
consequence: The card edge can be bent or only partly seated, giving intermittent PCIe contact, and the board may shift when a cable is plugged in.
suggested_action: Pick one height datum (the posts, with slotted adapter holes or shims), use MH2/MH3 for screws, and measure a real DFR1169 before printing the base.

title: In Option A the FPGA-LDO A connectors J1/J2 stay open on the animal's head whenever the Frontend is unplugged, with no cover and no cleaning method.
what: The project assumes an Option A split in which the Frontend unplugs and FPGA-LDO A stays on the head with the four ASIC boards. Between sessions, LDO A's two 70-contact DF40 headers then face hair, bedding, blood and saline. Hirose protects the contacts only when mated, does not recommend cleaning, and lists no cover, and no cover has been chosen. LDOB-22 records the same problem for Option B's J5 only.
where: FPGA-LDO A J1 and J2 (DF40C-70DP-0.4V(51), top) at (91.255, 127.0) and (108.755, 127.0). They carry 108 ASIC and control signals, 14 GND and VIN_3V3 (J2.68-70), which is live again as soon as the Frontend is re-mated.
evidence: inputs/system/weekly_deck/START_HERE.md line 67: 'the Option A split (Frontend unplugs, FPGA-LDO stays) is assumed'. exports/ldo_a/parts.csv: J1/J2 on the top side. known/system.json checked_ok: the 140 J1/J2 pins are 108 signals, 14 GND, 3 VIN_3V3 and 15 spares. No cover or dummy-plug part appears in any parts.csv or record.
source: Hirose DF40 Series catalog, Jun 1 2024: p3 feature 8 (contact walls protect the contacts when mated), p5 (mating durability 30 times) and p21 (cleaning not recommended), LCSC copy https://datasheet.lcsc.com/datasheet/pdf/145ab5d527b34eafa7a47375cb561c6a.pdf?productCode=C3640153. Known LDOB-22 (Option B).
consequence: Residue in the open headers can bridge 0.4 mm neighbours, including VIN_3V3 and signal contacts, when the Frontend is plugged back in. A dummy cover plug would use the same 30-cycle rating.
suggested_action: Choose an Option A cover (blank DF40C-70DS dummy receptacles or a sealed cap in the head housing) and count its insertions in the SYS-22 mate log, or disconnect at the HDMI cable instead.

title: The +10 V and -10 V connector pins sit 0.4 mm from 1.5 V rail pins, and on LDO B J5 beside an ASIC data line.
what: On every 80-pin DF40 connector J3/J4, the +10 V pin (VDD10) and the -10 V pin (VSS10) each have a 1.5 V rail pin on both sides, 0.4 mm apart. A solder bridge between neighbours would put 8.5 V or 11.5 V on 1.5 V rails shared by all eight ASICs on a head and on regulator outputs rated far below that. This pin order comes from the ASIC designer's pin table and is fixed by the ASIC board; nothing fails as drawn, so it is a bring-up and assembly hazard. The not-yet-ordered LDO B J5 repeats the pattern and puts VSS10 next to ASIC1_DATA4, which runs straight to an FPGA pin.
where: LDO A, router and ASIC board J3/J4: pins 34 DVDD, 36 VDD10, 38 VDD_DRIVER, 52 REF_VDD, 54 VSS10, 56 VDD_ADC. LDO B J5 (router and LDO board): pins 53 DVDD, 55 VDD10, 57 VDD_DRIVER, 71 ASIC1_DATA4, 73 VSS10, 75 VDD_ADC. ASIC1_DATA4 path: J5.71 to LDO board J2.60 to Frontend J2.60 to U1.K1, no series part.
evidence: exports/ldo_a/pads.csv: J3.34/36/38/52/54/56 at x 98.383/98.783/99.183/101.983/102.383/102.783, y 114.868; J3 pads 0.23 x 0.66 mm (0.17 mm gap), J4 pads 0.20 x 0.70 mm (0.20 mm gap). Router and ASIC board J3/J4 use the same pin numbers; LDO B J5 at y 118.845 (LDO board) and 118.66 (router), 0.4 mm pitch. Rail voltages from the netlist: R901 and R1001 100k on the SET pins of U9 LT3042 and U10 LT3094 give +/-10 V; R601 15k on U6 LT3042 gives REF_VDD 1.5 V; U3, U4, U5 TPS7A2015 (fixed 1.5 V) drive VDD_ADC, VDD_DRIVER, DVDD. Differences 8.5 V and 11.5 V. inputs/asic/J3_pinout__Power_Pins.csv has the same order; inputs/ldo_b/V2_record/J5_pin_map_V4.csv confirms J5. On the ASIC board J4.73 /D<4> is a U01_BCD1 data output. Script: a review working file (not published)
source: TI TPS7A20 data sheet SBVS338H (rev. July 2024), section 5.1 Absolute Maximum Ratings: VOUT -0.3 V to 6.5 V or VIN + 0.3 V, whichever is lower, https://www.ti.com/lit/ds/symlink/tps7a20.pdf. Hirose DF40 contact voltage rating not checked against the datasheet. Engineering judgement on pin adjacency.
consequence: One bridge or bent contact at these pairs could damage every ASIC on the head and the regulator on that rail, and on J5 the FPGA input U1.K1.
suggested_action: Before the first mate, measure resistance VDD10 to DVDD/VDD_DRIVER and VSS10 to REF_VDD/VDD_ADC on every assembled board (for example C902 to C502/C402 and C1002 to C602/C302). On LDO B J5, optionally move ASIC1_DATA4 off pin 71 and put a ground or a free pin beside pins 55 and 73.

title: No board has a test pad on any of the nine ASIC rails, so rails must be probed on small capacitor pads.
what: Each of the nine ASIC rails should be measured before the first ASIC board is plugged in, but no board has a test point on any of them. The rails can still be reached on bottom-side regulator output capacitor pads on LDO A and the LDO B LDO board, and these stay reachable with the full stack mated, because the ASIC boards cover only up to about y 118.8 and the nearest rail capacitor is at y 121.9. Probing 0402 pads, or the 0.4 mm pitch DF40 contacts where DVDD pin 34 sits next to VDD10 pin 36, is slow and a probe slip can short neighbours. This is a bring-up convenience item, not a likely failure.
where: LDO A and LDO B LDO board: rails ASIC_VDD_FE, ASIC_VDD_ADC, ASIC_VDD_DRIVER, ASIC_DVDD, ASIC_REF_VDD, ASIC_VDD_CGEN, ASIC_REF_VCM, ASIC_VDD10, ASIC_VSS10; output capacitors on the bottom (layer 6). Router (Option B): TP7 only. ASIC board: J1 (/AGND) only.
evidence: exports/ldo_a/pads.csv: TP1-TP9 on VIN_3V3, STIM_POS_12V, STIM_NEG_12V, EN_ASIC_RAILS, GND, AGND, ASIC_AC_IN, STIM_PRE_POS, STIM_PRE_NEG; TP8 is on the bottom at (92.6, 129.3). ldo_b_ldo has the same set without TP7; ldo_b_router has TP7 only; asic has no TP parts. LDO A rail pads, all bottom: C202, C602, C802 0603 (0.9 x 0.95 mm pads); C902, C1002 1206 (1.15 x 1.8 mm); C51, C53-C57, C302, C402, C502, C702 0402 (0.56 x 0.62 mm). Router top-side 0402s on six rails (C51, C53-C57); none on VDD10, VDD_ADC or VSS10. ASIC board footprint on LDO A is y about 100 to 118.8 (inputs/ldo_b/V2_fit/fit_b_v2.json slabs; stack fit test V10 lists only R2, R3, R6 under it); nearest rail capacitor C1004 at y 121.9. Vias are tented on all three LDO/router boards. Free top strip y 143.1-147.1 beside TP1-TP9, but fit_b_v2.json shows the Micro-HDMI plug overhangs 3.16 mm of it at 1.78 mm clearance when the cable is in.
source: Engineering judgement; inputs/asic/ASIC_Reference/ASIC_REFERENCE.md item U02 lists per-rail voltage windows as unknown, so measurement before mating is the main safeguard.
consequence: Rail checks before mating are slow and risky, so they may be skipped, and a wrong rail is then found by the ASICs.
suggested_action: Add nine 1 mm rail pads on LDO A and the LDO B LDO board, preferably on the bottom beside the output capacitors since the cable plug overhangs the top strip; or build a DF40-80 breakout that brings every J3/J4 contact to pads for first power-up.

title: The Frontend cable connector has no ESD protection on the GT pair, JTAG pins, sense pin or 5 V input.
what: The head end of the cable is the one plugged and unplugged most, so it is where a static discharge from the cable is most likely. On the Frontend only the clock, command and SYNC LVDS pairs pass through an ESD array (U17, U18 TPD4E02B04). The transceiver (GT) transmit pair, the four JTAG lines, the sense line and the 5 V input go to the FPGA or the power input with no protection part. The HDMI Extension Board's ESD parts protect only that board, and on it the JTAG and sense lines pass only through 100 ohm resistors and an analog switch.
where: Frontend: J3.3/5 GTP_TX0_N/P to U1 H1/H2 (no ESD, no AC capacitor on this board); J3.2/15/17/18 FPGA_JTAG_TMS/TDI/TCK/TDO to U1 R8/T9/F8/T8 (bank 0); J3.1 CABLE_TARGET_SENSE to R27 only; J3.19 VIN_5V with no TVS; U18 IO3/IO4 spare, tied to GND. HDMI Extension Board: J61x.1/2/15/17/18 to R640-R671 (100R) and U611-U617 (TS3A27518E); GT and LVDS pairs there have U801-U816.
evidence: exports/frontend/netlist.xml: FPGA_JTAG_TCK = J3.17 + U1.F8 only; TDI = J3.15 + U1.T9; TDO = J3.18 + U1.T8; TMS = J3.2 + U1.R8; GTP_TX0_P/N = J3.5/3 + U1.H2/H1 only; CABLE_TARGET_SENSE = J3.1 + R27.2; VIN_5V = J3.19, C206/C207/C209, TP14, U16 (no TVS); U17 on CABLE_CLK/CMDSYNC, U18 on CABLE_SYNC, U18 pins 4-7 on GND. exports/hdmi/netlist.xml: HDMI1_JTAG_TCK = J610.17 + R640 only (R640-R643 100R per parts.csv), then U611; HDMI1_VREF = J610.1 + U611.13; GT nets carry U801-U808.
