title: The XEM can drive LVDS pairs into an unpowered Frontend, back-feeding its 1.5 V bank through clamp diodes.
what: The XEM drives the clock, command and SYNC pairs on every port whenever its bitstream runs, but it cannot tell whether a port's Frontend is powered. On a live plug, or when a port is in fault or current limit, the Frontend's VCCO_1V5 rail is at or near 0 V, so up to 4 LVDS legs (6 on ports 3-6) push current through the Artix-7 clamp diodes (protection diodes from each pin to its bank supply) and can partly lift the dead rail. This does not happen on a normal cold start, because the ports power up about 10 ms after 12 V, before the XEM is configured. The files cannot settle how much current flows; the LVDS driver current is expected to stay below the 10 mA clamp limit, and a measurement of VCCO_1V5 during a live plug would settle it.
where: HDMI Extension Board MC1 bank 64 (B64_L6P/N clock, B64_L5P/N command/SYNC, plus SYNC on ports 3-6) to J610-J617 pins 6/8, 9/11, 12/14, with ESD U801/U809; Frontend J3 to U1 P14/R15 (CABLE_CLK), M14/N14 (CMDSYNC), B9/A9 (SYNC) on VCCO_1V5, each with a 100 ohm resistor R61/R62/R64; PORT_ENABLE from U700.13 (PG) to U701-U708 EN; FAULT outputs to D701-D708 only.
evidence: exports/hdmi/netlist.xml: PORT_ENABLE = R703, U700.13 (PG), U701-U708 EN, so all eight ports switch together; Net-(D701-K) = U701.4 FAULT and D701 only; J610.6/9 go to MC1 B64_L6P/L5P. HDMIn_VREF goes only to the U611 mux and the U603 window / U605 / U602 OE path, which gates the JTAG buffer only. exports/frontend/netlist.xml: all user banks on VCCO_1V5, supplied by U3/U4 enabled by PG_CORE_1V0. inputs/hdmi/V35_prefab_review/ALL_FINDINGS.md line 193: ports turn on about 10 ms after 12 V, before XEM configuration. DS181 Table 2: IIN 10 mA max through any pin of a powered or unpowered bank when the clamp diode is forward-biased.
source: AMD DS181 Artix-7 FPGAs Data Sheet: DC and AC Switching Characteristics, v1.27, Table 2 (IIN clamp current), https://docs.amd.com/v/u/en-US/ds181_Artix_7_Data_Sheet (the AMD URL returned 404 on re-check; the 10 mA value was read from third-party copies of v1.27); engineering judgement.
consequence: A Frontend can be partly powered through its I/O pins during a live plug or port fault, which risks a stuck or out-of-order power-up; damage is unlikely.
suggested_action: Make 'plug with the HDMI board off' the bring-up rule, and measure VCCO_1V5 on a Frontend during a live plug once boards exist.

title: The Frontend FPGA can be configured only through the HDMI cable from a working HDMI Extension Board.
what: JTAG is the four-wire test and programming port of the FPGA. On the Frontend, each JTAG net has just two pads, the FPGA ball and a contact on the Micro-HDMI connector, and the SPI flash can only be written through the FPGA. A first Frontend therefore needs a working HDMI Extension Board (USB-JTAG chip, switches set correctly, cable voltage check met) and a good cable; if any of these fails there is no fallback. A blank FT232H EEPROM mainly affects whether AMD's Vivado recognises the cable; open tools may still drive it (judgement, not checked).
where: Frontend: U1 TCK F8, TMS R8, TDI T9, TDO T8; nets FPGA_JTAG_TCK/TMS/TDI/TDO to J3 pins 17/2/15/18; flash U7 via U8; FPGA_PROGRAM_B (no test pad); INIT_B on TP11. HDMI Extension Board: U501, U602, U603 (TPS3700DDCR), U610-U618, SW600.
evidence: exports/frontend/nets.csv: FPGA_JTAG_* pad_count 2 (J3 and U1); FPGA_PROGRAM_B 3 pads (R17, U1.P10, U11.6); flash nets only to U7, U8 and pull resistors. exports/frontend/pads.csv: no TP on any JTAG net; R27 from VCCAUX_1V8 to CABLE_TARGET_SENSE (J3.1). exports/hdmi: R605 301k/R606 100k give 0.4 V x 401/100 = 1.604 V; R607 402k/R608 100k give 0.4 V x 502/100 = 2.008 V on U603. The HDMI board has no standalone JTAG header (J4, J500, J900-J911, J920 carry no JTAG net).
source: AMD UG470 (7 Series FPGAs Configuration User Guide), JTAG and master SPI configuration; TI TPS3700 data sheet SBVS187 (0.4 V threshold not re-read); Engineering judgement.
consequence: Bring-up of the first Frontend stalls on any HDMI Extension Board or cable problem, with no independent way to tell which side is at fault.
suggested_action: Add four small JTAG pads plus GND and VCCAUX_1V8 on a Frontend edge before ordering, or document a Micro-HDMI breakout to a standard AMD 2 mm JTAG header.

title: Once the head is stacked, FPGA configuration and the power-good/reset chain cannot be seen or probed.
what: No board in the head (Frontend, LDO A, Option B router and LDO board, ASIC board) has an LED. The Frontend's only DONE pad, TP12 (DONE is the FPGA pin that goes high when configuration has loaded), is on the bottom side between J1 and J2, under the board that mates there. The power-good and reset nets, and a few internal supply nets, have no test pad at all. Most output rails and INIT_B can be probed on top, so the real gaps are DONE and the power-good/reset chain.
where: Frontend: TP12 FPGA_DONE at (117.52, 110.2), bottom (layer 14); nets PG_CORE_1V0, PG_GTP_1V4, BOOT_RESET_N, 1V4_GTP_IN, VCCADC_1V8, OSC125_3V3, /CLK25_VDD (no pads). HDMI Extension Board: fault LEDs D701-D708, bottom side.
evidence: exports/frontend/pads.csv: TP12 FPGA_DONE at (117.52, 110.2), copper layer 14 (bottom); J1/J2 on the bottom at x 122.245 / 104.745. Top pads exist for VIN_5V, VIN_3V3, SWITCHED_3V3, VCCINT_1V0, VCCAUX_1V8, VCCO_1V5, MGTAVCC_1V0, MGTAVTT_1V2, BOOT_RAILS_PG_3V3 and INIT_B (TP2-TP11, TP14, y 101.45-121.12). exports/frontend/nets.csv: the seven listed nets have no TP pad; 1V4_GTP_IN is only the input to U5/U6, whose outputs are on TP7/TP8. parts.csv: no LED on frontend, ldo_b_router or asic; ldo_a and ldo_b_ldo have only the B0540WS Schottky diodes D11/D12. hdmi: D701-D708 RED 0603 on the bottom, R721-R728 3.3k from FE_5V, cathode to TPS2553 FAULT (U701.4); (5 - about 1.9 V)/3.3k is about 0.9 mA. No port-on or target-present light.
source: Engineering judgement.
consequence: On a stacked head, whether the FPGA configured and which supply failed to come up can only be learned over JTAG, which itself depends on the cable working.
suggested_action: Move TP12 to the Frontend top side and add top pads on PG_CORE_1V0 and PG_GTP_1V4 (or BOOT_RESET_N); optionally add one DONE LED on the Frontend top.

title: No board in the head has a test pad on any ASIC clock, sync, read, data or SPI line.
what: The ASIC clock, sync, read, data and SPI lines pass between boards only through DF40 connector contacts inside the stack. No board offers a pad where an oscilloscope probe can touch them. If the first ASIC does not answer, nobody can look at CLKH, CLK32MHz_Out or SYNC without taking the head apart. LDO A has a free strip on its top side, outside the area covered by the Frontend, where small pads would fit.
where: LDO A and Option B router: nets /BOARD1_CLK, /BOARD1_SPI_CLK, /ASIC1_CLK32MHz_Out, /ASIC1_SYNC, /ASIC1_READ, /ASIC1_DATA1, /STIM_CHIP1_SPI_DL, /SPI_LATCH_SHARED. ASIC board: no TP footprints. Frontend: no pads on BOARD1_CLK, BOARD1_SPI_CLK or SPI_LATCH_SHARED. Free LDO A top strip about y 143-147.
evidence: exports/ldo_a/nets.csv: /ASIC1_CLK32MHz_Out J2.59 J4.45; /ASIC1_SYNC J2.61 J4.47; /ASIC1_READ J2.49 J4.35; /ASIC1_DATA1 J2.21 J4.79; /BOARD1_CLK J1.42 J4.7; /BOARD1_SPI_CLK J2.52 J4.63; /STIM_CHIP1_SPI_DL J2.46 J4.59; /SPI_LATCH_SHARED J2.48 J3.61 J4.61 plus R18.1 (10k 0402 pulldown, bottom side, not a test point). exports/ldo_b_router/nets.csv: the same nets touch only J3/J4/J5. TP lists: ldo_a TP1-TP9 are power or enable only; the router has only TP7 (ASIC_AC_IN); asic has none. ldo_a board_stats: top component density 28.97 %; outline y 110.34-147.1; in Option A the Frontend covers y about 117.65-143.07, leaving a strip about 4 mm deep at the far end. The strip near J3 is likely under the ASIC board above.
source: Engineering judgement.
consequence: Debugging the first ASIC link needs scope access to these lines, and the stacked head does not give it.
suggested_action: Add six to eight small top-side pads on one ASIC's lines in the free strip at y 143-147 on LDO A (and on the router for Option B), or put them on a dummy-ASIC breakout board.

title: STIM_EN, STIM_START, STIM_CLK and STIM_CHB reach all eight ASICs of a stack and the ASIC configuration cannot be read back, so an ASIC not loaded with a safe table can stimulate whenever another ASIC does.
what: Each of the four stimulation control lines (STIM_EN, STIM_START, STIM_CLK, STIM_CHB) is one FPGA net shared by all eight ASICs on a Frontend: both FPGA-LDO ports and both boards of each stack. CHIP_RESET is shared the same way. The only per-chip control is the configuration shifted in over SPI, whose stimulus tables hold a per-stimulator ENABLED field; the ASIC has no SPI output pin, so firmware cannot read back what a chip holds, and no record says what the stimulation registers contain after power-up or after CHIP_RESET. On today's pin-map-V5 hardware (FPGA-LDO A V12, Option B router V2) the far board's SPI clock, latch and data pins (16, 18, 66, 68, 70, 72) are plain lanes to FPGA inputs, so the four far ASICs of each stack are powered and clocked but can never be configured, yet they receive every stimulation pulse with whatever table they powered up with or picked up from their floating SPI lines. Option B's J5 has no spare pin, so there this state would be permanent; pin map V6 makes every chip loadable, but safety then rests entirely on firmware loading a safe table into all eight chips every time.
where: FPGA-LDO A: /STIM_EN_SHARED (J2.63, J3.51, J4.51, R2), /STIM_START_SHARED (J2.67, J3.55, J4.55, R3), /STIM_CLK_SHARED (J2.65, J3.53, J4.53, R5), /STIM_CHB_SHARED (J2.1, J3.49, J4.49, R4), all with 10k pull-downs, and /CHIP_RESET_SHARED (J2.58, J3.71, J4.71, R19). Option B router: J3/J4 pins 49/51/53/55/71 joined to J5.116/115/117/119/69. ASIC boards V4, top and bottom: STIM_CHB (FPGA_CHBL/CHBR) on J3/J4 pin 49, STIM_EN (FPGA_EN) 51, STIM_CLK (FPGA_CLK) 53, STIM_START (FPGA_START) 55, FE_RESET 65 and CHIP_RESET 71 reach both dies on both boards. Far-board SPI: T_SPI_DINR(2)/T_SPI_DINL(2) on pins 16/18, T_SPI_DINR/T_SPI_DINL on 66/68, T_SPI_LATCH on 70, T_SPI_CLK on 72. FPGA-LDO A V12 underside port: J4.70 /ASIC3_CLK32MHz_Out (U1.P4), J4.72 /ASIC3_SYNC (P3), J4.66/68 /ASIC3_DATA6/5 (T7/R5), J4.16/18 /ASIC4_DATA6/5 (C18/D18); top-side port: the same pins of J3 for ASIC7/8, to U1 M2/M4/N3/N4/T15/R13. Frontend U1 J6, B10, B11, V9, C9.
evidence: exports/ldo_a/netlist.xml and nets.csv, exports/ldo_b_router/netlist.xml and exports/ldo_b_ldo/netlist.xml: nets as listed. exports/asic_top/pads.csv: pin 51 -> U01_BCD1/2 FPGA_EN, pin 55 -> FPGA_START, pin 53 -> FPGA_CLK, pin 49 -> FPGA_CHBL/R; T_SPI_LATCH (70) and T_SPI_CLK (72) reach both far dies, while on the near board SPI_LATCH (61) and SPI_CLK (63) serve the near chips only. exports/asic_top/netlist.xml and exports/asic_bottom/netlist.xml: the die symbol has 34 non-supply pads; its only SPI pads are the inputs SPI_CLK, SPI_DINL, SPI_DINR, SPI_LATCH, and there is no SPI output. Trace of 220 chip-pin rows (a review working file (not published)), V4 boards on V5 wiring: no FPGA output meets an ASIC output, and twelve nets meet FPGA inputs. They are the 2-node far-chip SPI lanes, for example /ASIC3_CLK32MHz_Out = J2.35, J4.70 (top latch) to P4, an input in inputs/frontend/V2_review_fixes/Frontend_V46_pins_V2.xdc line 25, and /ASIC7_SYNC = J2.24, J3.72. known/pinmap_v6_trace.csv: these 12 rows become FPGA outputs only in V6 (dir out, 'rename (existing line)'). known/asic_open.json A-P: Option B J5 is 120/120 used. inputs/asic/Pins__Sheet1.csv lists STIM_START, STM_CLK, STIM_EN and STIM_CHB as 'Shared / Control', and 'Chip out' lists only D<1:8>, CLK32MHZ, SYNC, READ (plus DISC_OUT). ASIC_REFERENCE.md: section 4 (per-channel ENABLED bits and amplitudes arrive over SPI), section 9 ('4096-zero SPI default is not an approved ASIC semantic preset'), item U05 (safe stimulus-disable codes unqualified; no safe presets established). rtl_primary_findings.md: the historical SPI engine has no readback. R2 (10k) holds STIM_EN low only while the FPGA is unconfigured. Worst case per ASIC: 128 x 22.5 uA at up to +/-10 V compliance (as recorded in LDOB-07).
source: ASIC designer's pin sheet Pins.xlsx Sheet1 (inputs/asic/Pins__Sheet1.csv); inputs/asic/ASIC_Reference/ASIC_REFERENCE.md sections 4 (stimulus tables, stimulation sequence), 9 and 10 (U05, U07); inputs/asic/ASIC_Reference/rtl_primary_findings.md; original slides 25-28 as extracted in inputs/asic/ASIC_Reference/logic_primary_extraction.json; known/pinmap_v6_trace.csv; known/asic_open.json A-P; known/ldo_b.json LDOB-07; engineering judgement.
consequence: A chip that powers up with stimulators enabled, or whose SPI load is corrupted (for example by the latch glitch in SYS-51 or by the floating top-chip latch in the separate pull-down finding), drives current into tissue whenever stimulation starts for any chip in the stack, and nothing in the system can detect it. A head built from FPGA-LDO A V12 or Option B V2 with far boards fitted can deliver unintended stimulation from up to four unconfigured chips per stack whenever the near chips stimulate, whatever the firmware does.
suggested_action: Record now that far boards are not fitted to pin-map-V5 hardware (FPGA-LDO A V12, Option B V2) with stimulation enabled, and carry this into the Option B decision, because there the far chips can never be configured. Ask the ASIC designer what the stimulation registers hold after power-up and after CHIP_RESET, and whether an all-zero L/R stream disables every stimulator; then make it a firmware rule to load an all-disabled table into all eight chips after every power-up and CHIP_RESET, before STIM_EN is raised. Before freezing V6, decide whether one of the last spare joint contacts should split STIM_EN per port.

title: No bring-up or handling procedure exists, yet 21 open items, four of them major, rely on one as their only protection for the first build.
what: Many open items were accepted for the first build on condition that a rule is followed. Examples: cable last on and first off; orientation and near/far check before mating; rails measured before the first ASIC board; ESD grounding; VIO1 set before any bitstream. Apart from four HDMI-board notes and the VIO1 step, no such procedure exists in the project records. The ASIC boards are now kept as received, and V4 adds neither key nor marking, so for SYS-09 and R2S-04 the procedure is the only defence. This review adds further first-power checks: see the findings on the shared STIM lines, the R700 feedback resistor, the J3 5 V pad beside TCK, the top-chip SPI latch and blank flash, and a bench supply on TP14.
where: HDMI Extension Board: TP700, TP701-TP708, J920, SW601, U505. Frontend: TP14, TP2-TP11, TP12 (DONE), J3. FPGA-LDO A and Option B LDO board: TP1-TP9, J3/J4 pins 1 and 34-56. ASIC V4 boards: bond fingers before bonding (the assembler does not place U01).
evidence: Search of inputs/ for 'bring-up', 'bringup' and 'first power': the only procedure-like notes are inputs/hdmi/V36_prefab_fixes/START_HERE.md lines 69-73 (four notes: cable type, program the FT232H EEPROM, TXPOLARITY, never both 12 V jacks); inputs/hdmi/power_estimate/START_HERE.md line 69 (VIO1 = 1.8 V); inputs/hdmi/V37_record/START_HERE.md line 52 (U700 temperature). The other hits (review text in inputs/hdmi/V35_prefab_review, a hand-over note in inputs/notes and historical XEM8305 notes in inputs/asic/ASIC_Reference) are not procedures. Nothing covers the Frontend, the FPGA-LDO boards or the ASIC boards. Items whose action is a rule or a first-power check: SYS-09, SYS-10, LDOB-04, LDOB-08 (major); SYS-11, SYS-14, SYS-16, SYS-18, SYS-19, SYS-20, SYS-32, SYS-40, SYS-52, LDOB-12, LDOB-24, R2E-03, HDMI-02, HDMI-05, HDMI-25, FE-19, LDOA-15. boards/asic_top and asic_bottom PCB.kicad_pcb: the only text item is the dimension '21.7424'.
source: Project records listed under evidence; known/system.json, ldo_b.json, ldo_a.json, hdmi.json, frontend.json, r2-elec.json; engineering judgement.
consequence: The first power-up of bonded, implanted ASICs depends on each person remembering about two dozen scattered rules. One missed step (a live mate, a turned or mixed stack, an unchecked rail) can destroy all eight ASICs of a head.
suggested_action: Before any board is powered, write a one-page bring-up and handling order. HDMI board alone: FE_5V at TP700, VIO1, EEPROM. Each Frontend alone on a checked port: rails, JTAG, flash. Frontend plus FPGA-LDO without ASIC boards: nine rails, pin-to-pin resistance. Bare ASIC boards: marking, orientation, rails at the fingers. Bonded boards last, cable last on, with ESD grounding. Link each step to the item it closes.

title: Rocking either V4 ASIC board on or off with the cable live leaves +10 V or -10 V and three 1.5 V rails connected after all four ground contacts have opened.
what: On the 80-pin J3/J4 the only grounds (AGND 42/44, DGND 46/48) sit mid-row, with four rails on each side and VDD_CGEN on pin 1. When a board is rocked off from either end, the grounds open while the rail group on the far side is still mated. From the pin-80 end those are DVDD, VDD10, VDD_DRIVER, REF_VCM and VDD_CGEN; from the pin-1 end, VDD_FE, REF_VDD, VSS10 and VDD_ADC. Every joint in the stack has this order, because each board passes pin n to pin n. Nothing on the head can switch the rails off first (SYS-10). This is the J3/J4 counterpart of LDOB-24 on J5.
where: Both V4 boards J3/J4 (pin 1 at x 143.34, pin 80 at x 127.74), plus FPGA-LDO A J3/J4 and Option B router J3/J4, which use the same order. Rails: 1 VDD_CGEN, 34 DVDD, 36 VDD10, 38 VDD_DRIVER, 40 REF_VCM, 50 VDD_FE, 52 REF_VDD, 54 VSS10, 56 VDD_ADC.
evidence: W2/a review working file (not published) on exports/asic_bottom/pads.csv (asic_top gives the same result), output rocking_out.txt. Method as in LDOB-24: rigid tilt about a line 0.5 mm past the end row; a contact opens at 0.45 mm separation. Pin-80 end lifted: the last ground opens at 0.85 mm. REF_VCM, VDD_DRIVER, VDD10 and DVDD stay mated to 0.89/0.94/0.99/1.05 mm, VDD_CGEN to the end, and 35 signal contacts are still mated. Pin-1 end lifted: the last ground opens at 1.05 mm. VDD_FE, REF_VDD, VSS10 and VDD_ADC stay mated to 1.11/1.19/1.27/1.37 mm, and 28 signal contacts are still mated. The rails are on whenever the cable is live (EN_ASIC_RAILS from R1/C3).
source: Hirose DF40 Series catalog 2013.11, p.1 (effective mating length 0.45 mm at 1.5 mm stack height) and p.2 (30 mating cycles), distributor copy https://cdn-shop.adafruit.com/product-files/2227/ed_DF40_20140305-337786.pdf . known/ldo_b.json LDOB-24 (same mechanism on J5); known/system.json SYS-10 and SYS-32 (ASIC boards cannot be pulled straight). Engineering judgement.
consequence: A far-board swap or bench re-stack with the cable connected exposes the chips to a stimulation rail and live signal lines with no ground return. This may damage or latch up the ASICs; their tolerance is unknown.
suggested_action: Add 'HDMI cable unplugged before any DF40 on the head is mated or unmated, including far-board swaps' to the handling procedure now. If the FPGA-switched rails of SYS-10 are added, switch them off before handling.

title: On the Frontend cable connector, the 5 V pad sits 0.15 mm from the FPGA's TCK pad, and neither JTAG line has a series resistor.
what: The cable pin map carries 5 V on pin 19 and reuses the neighbouring HDMI pins 17 and 18 for the FPGA's JTAG clock (TCK) and data out (TDO). On the Frontend, pad 19 is 0.15 mm from pad 17 in the same row, and contact 19 sits next to contact 18 inside the connector. Both JTAG nets go straight to FPGA bank 0, which is powered from VCCAUX_1V8. A solder bridge or bent contact would therefore put the port's 5 V, with up to about 0.7 A behind it, onto an FPGA pin rated for 10 mA of clamp current. At the HDMI board end the same pins have 100 ohm resistors, so only the Frontend end is exposed.
where: Frontend J3: pin 17 FPGA_JTAG_TCK at (113.9, 103.055) and pin 19 VIN_5V at (114.3, 103.055), pads 0.25 x 0.85 mm, 0.15 mm gap. Pin 18 FPGA_JTAG_TDO at (114.1, 101.83), 0.30 mm from pad 19. U1 F8 (TCK) and T8 (TDO); VCCO_0 (E10) is on VCCAUX_1V8. HDMI board J610-J617 pins 17/18 go through R640/R643 (100 ohm).
evidence: exports/frontend/connectors.csv: J3 pad positions and sizes. exports/frontend/nets.csv: FPGA_JTAG_TCK = J3.17, U1.F8; FPGA_JTAG_TDO = J3.18, U1.T8 (2 nodes each); VIN_5V = J3.19, C206, C207, C209, TP14, U16. exports/frontend/netlist.xml: U1.E10 VCCO_0 is on VCCAUX_1V8 (49 nodes). Source current: TPS2553 with R711 = 37.4k gives IOS 637/696/764 mA (min/nominal/max, SLVS841G equations 1-3). exports/hdmi/nets.csv: HDMI1_JTAG_TDO = J610.18, R643.2.
source: AMD DS181 Artix-7 data sheet v1.27.1 (3 July 2024), Table 1 p.1 (I/O input maximum VCCO + 0.55 V; VCCAUX 2.0 V) and Table 2 p.2 (10 mA clamp current), https://docs.amd.com/v/u/en-US/ds181_Artix_7_Data_Sheet (the AMD URL returned 404 to earlier reviewers; read from a saved copy). TI TPS2553 SLVS841G sec. 8.3, equations 1-3, https://www.ti.com/lit/ds/symlink/tps2553.pdf . HDMI Type D pin order (17 SCL, 18 SDA, 19 +5 V) as cited in SYS-20, https://www.electronics-notes.com/articles/audio-video/hdmi/hdmi-pinouts-connections.php (not re-read). Engineering judgement.
consequence: One bridge at assembly, or one damaged plug, can destroy the Frontend FPGA at the first power-up through the cable, and can push VCCAUX_1V8 past its 2.0 V absolute maximum.
suggested_action: Add to the first-power checks of every Frontend and cable: resistance from J3.19 to J3.17 and to J3.18 above 1 MOhm, and a visual check of the contacts. At the next Frontend revision, consider 33-100 ohm series resistors on TCK and TDO next to J3.

title: On ports 1, 2, 7 and 8 the Frontend's dedicated SYNC input floats, and the Frontend cannot tell its port.
what: Cable pins 12/14 carry a separate SYNC pair only on ports 3-6; on ports 1, 2, 7 and 8 the HDMI Extension Board leaves them unconnected. On the Frontend these pins go to an LVDS input that has only a 100 ohm resistor across it and no bias, so with the far end open its output is undefined and can toggle with noise. Nothing on the cable tells the Frontend which port it is on, so firmware must use the SYNC folded into the command pair (pins 9/11) by default. The XEM pin file also still warns that the Frontend routes 12/14 to transceiver input RX0, which is no longer true.
where: HDMI Extension Board J610, J611, J616, J617 pins 12/14 (unconnected-(J61x-SYNC_P/N)), no XEM pin and no ESD part. Frontend J3.12/14 to /CABLE_SYNC_P/N to R64 100R, U18, U1 B9/A9 (LVDS_25, DIFF_TERM FALSE).
evidence: exports/hdmi/pads.csv: J610/J611/J616/J617 pads 12/14 'unconnected-(J61x-SYNC_P/N-Pad12/14)', passive + no_connect; J612-J615 pads 12/14 on B64_L16/L23/L22/L18. exports/frontend/netlist.xml: /CABLE_SYNC_P = J3.12, R64.1, U1.B9, U18.1/10; /CABLE_SYNC_N = J3.14, R64.2, U1.A9, U18.2/9; no bias resistors; U1.E3/E4 (MGTPRXN0/P0_216) on GND. inputs/frontend/V2_review_fixes/Frontend_V46_pins_V2.xdc lines 116-117: B9/A9 LVDS_25 DIFF_TERM FALSE. inputs/hdmi/firmware_V34/fit_pins_V34_sync.xdc lines 2-4: ports 1, 2, 7, 8 not connected, and the stale CAUTION about Frontend V40 GTP RX0 (E4/E3). The Frontend schematic V46 note records the floating input but is itself stale (it names D8/C8 and says ESD only at the XEM).
source: AMD UG471 v1.10 p.92 (external termination, DIFF_TERM FALSE); AMD DS181 v1.27.1 Table 11 (LVDS_25 needs VIDIFF of at least 100 mV for a defined input; not re-read, the DS181 URL returned 404, value taken from the schematic's own citation); engineering judgement.
consequence: If firmware listens to pins 12/14, ports 1, 2, 7 and 8 take spurious SYNC events (misaligned recordings or stimulation), and moving a cable between ports changes behaviour.
suggested_action: Make the SYNC folded into 9/11 the Frontend firmware default and enable the dedicated SYNC only by a host command or a flag in the command stream. Delete the stale CAUTION line in fit_pins_V34_sync.xdc and update the Frontend schematic note.

title: Driving Frontend pin M15 low to switch off the GT rails instead resets and reloads the FPGA, in a loop.
what: FPGA pin M15 drives EN_GTPWR_1V5, which through U15 enables buck U13; U13's power-good (PG, a pin that goes low when a regulator is off or out of regulation) is the only enable of U5, the transceiver supply regulator. U5's PG is tied with U4's into BOOT_RAILS_PG_3V3, the manual-reset input of reset chip U12, which then pulls PROGRAM_B and INIT_B low through U11 and erases the FPGA's configuration. With the FPGA blank, M15 floats, R58 pulls the enable high, the rails return and the FPGA reloads, so any design that drives M15 low repeats this about every 7 s. The 'shutdown function' promised in the U15 field cannot be used.
where: Frontend: U1 M15 (EN_GTPWR_1V5), R58 4.99k to VCCO_1V5, U15, EN_GTPWR_3V3 (U13.4, R57), PG_GTP_1V4 (U13.12, U5.5, R43), BOOT_RAILS_PG_3V3 (R9, TP10, U4.12, U5.3, U6.5, U12.3 MR), BOOT_RESET_N (U12.6 to U11.1/U11.3, U14.2), FPGA_PROGRAM_B (U11.6 to U1 P10), FPGA_INIT_B (U11.4 to U1 T10), C84 1 uF on U12 CT, R25 PUDC_B to VCCO_1V5.
evidence: exports/frontend/netlist.xml: the nets listed under where. TPS748 SBVS074N sec. 6.3.2, p.17: PG goes low when the device is disabled or VOUT falls below about 90 %. TPS3890 SLVSD65A p.3: MR low asserts RESET, which stays low for the delay after MR returns high; tPD = 1.07 s per uF, so about 1.07 s with C84 (more than the '>=215 ms' in the U12 field). U7 field: 17,536,096 bits at 3 MHz SPI x1 = 5.85 s. Cycle about 7 s. PUDC_B strapped high (R25), so M15 has no configuration pull-up. inputs/frontend/V2_review_fixes/Frontend_V46_pins_V2.xdc lines 118-119: M15 constrained LVCMOS15 as an FPGA output.
source: TI TPS748 datasheet SBVS074N (June 2024), sec. 6.3.2, p.17; TI TPS3890 datasheet SLVSD65A, p.3 (pin functions, CT formula) and p.4; MPS MPM3833C Rev 1.0, p.4 (PG, soft-stop). Engineering judgement on the drawn netlist.
consequence: A firmware default of 0 on M15, or a power-saving feature, puts the Frontend into an endless reconfiguration loop of about 7 s per cycle.
suggested_action: Record in the pin file and firmware notes that M15 must be driven high; do not rely on leaving it unconstrained, since Vivado's default pull-down on unused pins (from memory, not checked) would fight R58. Alternatively, take U5 PG out of BOOT_RAILS_PG_3V3 on the next schematic revision.

title: The stimulation rails are set to +/-10.0 V, but no ASIC supply absolute maximum is on record.
what: VDD10 and VSS10 are set to +10.0 V and -10.0 V and reach the ASIC connectors, as the ASIC designer's power-pin sheet asks. The inherited regulator design used 9.0/9.1 V, and the ASIC reference treats the +/-10 V chip figure as a stimulation compliance range (the voltage the outputs can swing to), not a supply rating. The files cannot settle whether 10 V is safe; only the chip's absolute maximum supply rating from the ASIC designer can. The project record shows the newer +/-10 V levels were chosen on purpose.
where: Option A: U9 LT3042 (R901 100k 1 %) and U10 LT3094 (R1001 100k 1 %) to J3/J4 pins 36 (ASIC_VDD10) and 54 (ASIC_VSS10). Option B: the same regulators on the LDO board, through J5 pins 55/73 to router J3/J4 pins 36/54. ASIC board: J3/J4 pin 36 to P10_L/R, pin 54 to M10_L/R on both chips.
evidence: Vout = ISET x RSET = 100 uA x 100 kOhm = 10.0 V. LT3042/LT3094 ISET 98-102 uA over full conditions plus a 1 % resistor gives about +/-3 %, i.e. 9.7-10.3 V. Connections from exports/ldo_a, ldo_b_router, ldo_b_ldo and asic netlist.xml and parts.csv. inputs/asic/J3_pinout__Power_Pins.csv rows 36 (10 V) and 54 (-10 V). inputs/asic/ASIC_Reference/ASIC_Nine_Rail_Design_Intent.csv: 9.0 / 9.1 V, approved window UNKNOWN; ASIC_REFERENCE.md lines 134-137. inputs/notes/fpga-ldo-v14.md line 127 (+/-10 V chosen).
source: ASIC designer's sheet J3_pinout__Power_Pins.csv; inputs/asic/ASIC_Reference/ASIC_REFERENCE.md lines 134-137; Analog Devices LT3042 and LT3094 data sheets (ISET).
consequence: If the chip's supply limit is near 10 V, the +/-3 % regulator setpoint error leaves no margin and could overstress the ASICs.
suggested_action: Get the stimulation supply absolute maximum from the ASIC designer; if it is below about 10.5 V, change R901/R1001 to 91k to restore 9.1 V.

title: All eight ports share one enable from U700 power-good, so one FE_5V fault turns every stack off together.
what: U700's power-good output (PG, a pin that goes low when the output voltage is out of range) drives PORT_ENABLE, which is the enable of all eight port power switches. PG goes low if FE_5V leaves its window for more than 120 us, or during U700 current limit or thermal shutdown. Every port then turns off at once and returns 1.5-2.5 ms after FE_5V recovers. Eight ports at their switch limits do not by themselves trip U700's current limit; realistic triggers are a sag of the +VDCIN input, thermal shutdown, or a load step beyond the regulation window.
where: HDMI Extension Board U700 (TPSM63606) pin 13 PG -> net PORT_ENABLE -> U701-U708 (TPS2553) pin 3 EN; pull-up R703 10k to FE_5V; switch current set by R711 37.4k (ILIM).
evidence: exports/hdmi/netlist.xml: PORT_ENABLE = R703.1, U700.13, U701-U708.3. TPSM63606: PGUV 92/94/96.5 %, PGOV 105/107/110 %, deglitch 120 us falling, 1.5/2.0/2.5 ms rising; IOUT 0-6 A; low-side valley current limit 6.5/7.1/7.7 A. TPS2553 with 37.4k: 636 / 696 / 763 mA (min / nom / max); 8 x 763 mA = 6.1 A, above the 6 A rating but below the 6.5 A minimum current limit; nominal total 5.6 A. TPSM63606 sec. 8.3.9 recommends a 20-100k PG pull-up; R703 is 10k (harmless here).
source: TI TPSM63606 SLVSGB4B (Apr 2022), sec. 7.5 table p.7-8 and sec. 8.3.9, https://www.ti.com/lit/ds/symlink/tpsm63606.pdf; TI TPS2553 SLVS841G eq. 1-3.
consequence: One supply fault resets all eight recordings at once instead of only the affected port.
suggested_action: Accept and record it; on a later spin consider driving PORT_ENABLE from a slower or latched signal.

title: The ASIC rails come up in a fixed order, ±10 V last at about 0.25-0.5 s, and no required order is known.
what: All ASIC regulators share one enable net that rises slowly through a resistor-capacitor (RC) delay, and each low-noise regulator's output follows a second RC on its SET pin, so the rails come up one after another. The 1.5 V TPS7A2015 rails start first (about 15 ms), the ±12 V boost/inverter rails are up by about 30 ms, VDD_FE and REF_VDD reach 90% at about 57 ms, and VDD10/VSS10 reach 90% at about 0.25 s and 99% at about 0.5 s. This low-voltage-first, ±10 V-last order is conventional and nothing in the files says it is wrong. The files cannot settle whether the ASIC accepts it, because no ASIC document states a required power-up order; only the ASIC designer can answer that.
where: FPGA-LDO Option A and Option B LDO board (same parts): net EN_ASIC_RAILS with R1 (10k from VIN_3V3) and C3 (4.7 uF), driving U1 (LT3582-12) SHDN, U3/U4/U5/U7 (TPS7A2015) EN, U2/U6/U8/U9 (LT3042) and U10 (LT3094) EN/UV; SET networks R201/R601 15k, R801 7.5k, R901/R1001 100k, each with 1 uF (C203, C603, C803, C903, C1003); LT3582 ramp capacitors C16/C17 10 nF.
evidence: exports/ldo_a/netlist.xml and exports/ldo_b_ldo/netlist.xml: values and EN_ASIC_RAILS fan-out as above; PGFB tied to IN on U2/U6/U8/U9/U10, so fast start-up is off and the SET RC governs; exports/ldo_a/parts.csv JP1 'Bridged'. With the LT3582 222k SHDN pull-down: Thevenin 3.158 V, 9.57k, tau about 45 ms; EN reaches 0.9 V at 15.1 ms (TPS7A20), 1.1 V at 19.3 ms (LT3582), 1.24 V at 22.4 ms (LT3042). LT3582 ramp 1.5 V/ms with 10 nF. SET: 2.3 x 15 ms = 34.5 ms to 90% (99% by about 95 ms); 2.3 x 100 ms = 230 ms to 90%, 5 x 100 ms = 500 ms. inputs/asic/ASIC_Reference/power_primary_findings.md line 69 lists rail-order limits as missing.
source: TI TPS7A20 SBVS338H p.7 section 5.5 (VEN(HI) 0.9 V), https://www.ti.com/lit/ds/symlink/tps7a20.pdf; Analog Devices LT3042 Rev A (3042fa) EN/UV threshold and p.18 SET-pin soft start; LT3094 EN/UV threshold; LT3582 (3582512fb) SHDN threshold and ramp current, https://www.analog.com; inputs/asic/ASIC_Reference/ASIC_REFERENCE.md U02/U03.
consequence: Probably none, but an ASIC that needs a different order could be stressed or start in a bad state at every power-up.
suggested_action: Ask the ASIC designer whether the ASIC has any required power-up or power-down order before the first ASIC board is attached.

title: The ±12 V soft-start keeps the FPGA-LDO start-up surge near 0.2-0.37 A at 3.3 V, so a stack draws about 0.27-0.48 A at the 5 V pin during start-up, not the port limit that FE-02 states.
what: The LT3582-12 ramps both outputs together at about 1.5 V/ms, set by 1 uA into C16/C17 (10 nF). Its output capacitors therefore charge at roughly 18-35 mA per side, not at the switch current limit. The ramp starts about 19 ms after VIN_3V3 and lasts 5.5-12.6 ms, while the FPGA is still held in reset, so the Frontend draws little at that moment. The port limit is reached only if the 25 V 0805 output capacitors keep almost their full value at 12 V and the ramp runs at its fast corner.
where: FPGA-LDO A and Option B LDO board: U1 LT3582EUD-12; C16/C17 10 nF (RAMPN/RAMPP); C14 22 uF + C901 10 uF (STIM_POS_12V / STIM_PRE_POS via JP1); C21 22 uF + C1001 10 uF (negative side via JP2); C15 1 uF (CAPP); EN_ASIC_RAILS (R1/C3); J2.68-70. HDMI board U701-U708.
evidence: Ramp = (12 V / 0.8 V) x IRAMP / CRAMP = 1.5 V/ms; 0.95-2.2 V/ms with IRAMP 0.7-1.3 uA and C ±10 %. With about 12-16 uF effective per side at 12 V (X5R bias loss, from memory), charging takes 18-35 mA per side, plus 2-4 mA of LT3042/LT3094 ground current. At 75 % efficiency the LT3582 draws 0.20-0.37 A at 3.3 V near the end of the ramp. Total: Frontend in reset 0.10-0.20 A plus 0.06 A for the ASIC rails and LDO quiescent current gives 0.34-0.63 A at 3.3 V, or 0.27-0.48 A at 5 V (x 3.315 / (0.88 x 4.8)), against the 0.637 A minimum limit. Bound case, no derating (33 uF) and 2.2 V/ms: the converter runs at its switch limits (boost about 63 mA out from ILIMIT_P 285 mA min), drawing 0.51-0.61 A at 3.3 V, 0.64-0.71 A at 5 V. Each J2 VIN_3V3 contact carries 0.08-0.14 A (0.3 A rating). Script: W2/a review working file (not published)
source: ADI LT3582/LT3582-5/LT3582-12 data sheet 3582512fb Rev B: p.3 (ILIMIT_P 285/350/430 mA, ILIMIT_N 490/600/720 mA, ILIMIT_DIS 124/155/186 mA, IRAMP 0.7-1.3 uA, VOUTP 11.88-12.1 V), p.10 (the -12 outputs rise together), p.14 (ramp-rate equation and 1.5 V/ms example), https://www.analog.com/media/en/technical-documentation/data-sheets/3582512fb.pdf ; read from the local copy a review working file (not published) because analog.com timed out. TI TPS2553 data sheet SLVS841G eq. 1-3 (637 mA minimum limit), https://www.ti.com/lit/ds/symlink/tps2553.pdf . inputs/hdmi/power_estimate/START_HERE.md; known/frontend.json FE-02; known/system.json SYS-50 (EN timing).
consequence: Read literally, FE-02 could prompt a change to R711-R718 or the start-up circuit that is not needed. The real port-limit risk is still the high operating load (FE-02, SYS-02).
suggested_action: Drop the start-up clause from FE-02, or confirm it on the first stack by scoping TP14 and the port FAULT pin during power-up.

title: The ASIC designer's DVDD figure allows only about 5 pF per output, so the real output-driver current makes DVDD about 1.7-3.5 times the 1.39 mA per board in the budget.
what: The designer's sheet gives DVDD ('IO', 12 % of 17 uW per channel) 1.39 mA per board. With CLK32MHZ at 32 MHz and eight DATA lines at 32 Mb/s per chip, that covers the switching current of only about 5 pF per output. In practice each output drives 28-55 mm of trace across one or two DF40 joints into an FPGA pin, about 8-17 pF. The output drivers alone therefore draw 2.3-4.9 mA per board, 9-20 mA per stack. That is far inside U5's 300 mA and the contact rating. However, it is data-dependent digital current that returns on DGND and crosses NT1, because U5 is grounded to AGND (LDOA-11/16).
where: ASIC boards V4: per chip D<1:8>, CLK32MHZ, READ and SYNC (T_ copies on the far board). FPGA-LDO A: U5 TPS7A2015 (DVDD, GND on AGND) and NT1. Frontend U1 input balls.
evidence: inputs/asic/J3_pinout__Power_Budget.csv: IO 2.04 uW per channel, DVDD 1.39 mA per board. Implied load: 0.696 mA per chip / (1.5 V x (32 MHz + 8 x 8 MHz)) = 4.8 pF. Track lengths (exports/*/nets.csv medians): ASIC board 5.7-8.9 mm, FPGA-LDO A 18.6 mm (max 31.6), Frontend 3.9 mm (max 14.0). At about 0.08-0.12 pF/mm plus contacts and pads, that gives 8-17 pF (assumed). Result: 1.15-2.45 mA per chip, 2.3-4.9 mA per board. At NT1's 14.6 mOhm (LDOA-11), 9-20 mA per stack gives 0.13-0.29 mV of data-correlated drop. Data rate from inputs/hdmi/design_inputs/START_HERE.md (8 lines at 32 MHz). Script: W2/a review working file (not published)
source: ASIC designer's power budget sheet inputs/asic/J3_pinout__Power_Budget.csv; CMOS switching current I = C x V x f (engineering judgement); FPGA pad capacitance assumed (AMD DS181 not re-read); known/ldo_a.json LDOA-11 and LDOA-16.
consequence: Small: about +0.03-0.07 W per stack, and more data-correlated current across NT1 than LDOA-11/16 assumed.
suggested_action: Use about 5-6 mA per board for DVDD in the stack budget and in the LDOA-11/16 ground decision, and ask the ASIC designer whether the 'IO' share includes the board load.

title: V6 puts the far chips' READ strobes on J3/J4 pin 2, 8.0 mm from the nearest ground contact, the worst position on the 80-pin joint.
what: Pins 2, 4, 6 and 8 were open spares in V5. In V6 they carry READ, DATA8, DATA7 and DATA6 of ASIC8 and ASIC4. The only ground contacts are pins 42-48. The worst signal-to-ground distance therefore grows. The earlier fix of grounding the spares is no longer possible, because all six spares now carry signals.
where: FPGA-LDO A V12 J3/J4 (and the router and both ASIC boards): pins 2/4/6/8 at x 91.983-93.183; AGND pins 42/44 at x 99.983/100.383; GND pins 46/48 at x 100.783/101.183.
evidence: From exports/ldo_a/connectors.csv: pin 2 is 8.00 mm from pin 42 and 8.80 mm from pin 46; pin 4 7.60/8.40 mm; pin 6 7.20/8.00 mm; pin 8 6.80/7.60 mm. The maximum signal-to-ground distance rises from 7.32 mm (J3) and 7.47 mm (J4) to 8.00 mm. Signals more than 5 mm from any ground rise by four on each connector: from 21 to 25 on J3 and from 23 to 27 on J4 when counted as in SYS-23 (merge recount on exports/ldo_a/connectors.csv; the first count gave 20 to 24 and 22 to 26).
source: Project files as listed; known/system.json SYS-23 (V5 figures).
consequence: READ marks the data slots. Crosstalk or ground bounce on READ could misalign channel decoding for two chips per port. The size of the effect depends on the unknown ASIC edge rate.
suggested_action: At bring-up, probe ASIC8_READ at its new Frontend J1 contact during full data traffic. Ask the ASIC designer whether a later board revision can place a ground near pins 1-8.

title: Ground stacks fit within 1.1 mm of all eight FE-21 capacitors, but they take about 2.5% of MGTAVCC and 1.5% of MGTAVTT on L4.
what: A full GND stack (2-3, 3-4, 4-11, 11-12, 12-13) fits next to every capacitor FE-21 names. C5 and C18 take it directly on their own GND microvia; the other six sit 0.23-1.09 mm from the ground pad. The stacks stay legal with all 20 V6 nets routed. Each stack punches an anti-pad in the L3/L4 supply planes, so the GTP supply planes lose a little area, but every plane stays one piece.
evidence: Ground-pad distance to the nearest full stack, before -> after: C55 3.86 -> 0.23; C54 3.20 -> 0.55; C56 3.20 -> 0.69; C52 2.97 -> 0.35; C18 2.85 -> 0.00; C51 2.76 -> 1.09; C5 2.52 -> 0.00; C53 1.62 -> 0.60 mm. Plane area lost to the FE-21 stacks alone: MGTAVCC_1V0 L4 -0.73 of 29.18 mm2; MGTAVTT_1V2 L4 -0.53 of 35.72 mm2; VCCINT_1V0 L3 -1.08 of 76.70 mm2. With all V6 changes: MGTAVCC -4.3%, MGTAVTT -4.0%. All fills stay one piece (out/post_fe21_only.json, out/post_v6_esc12_swapsfirst.json).
source: FE-21 in known/frontend.json, which cites AMD UG483, 7 Series FPGAs PCB Design Guide, chapter 2, https://docs.amd.com/v/u/en-US/ug483_7Series_PCB (not re-read here). Placement and refill data: a review working file (not published) and out/post_*.json.
consequence: The FE-21 fix is buildable together with V6. The small loss of GTP plane copper is the price, and C51 stays at about 1.1 mm.
suggested_action: Adopt these eight positions in the V6 layout and re-check the MGTAVCC/MGTAVTT plane necks near C51-C56 after the final fill.

title: The XEM LVDS high level exceeds the Frontend's 1.5 V bank input limit only if VCCO_1V5 sags below 1.452 V.
what: The Frontend receives the XEM's LVDS signals (low-voltage differential pairs) in banks powered at 1.5 V, while the XEM drives them from a 1.8 V bank. AMD allows this only if each input leg stays within the data-sheet recommended range, VCCO + 0.20 V. At the 1.50 V setpoint the highest leg voltage is 1.652 V against a 1.70 V limit, so there is 48 mV of margin and no violation. The limit is crossed only if VCCO_1V5 drops below 1.452 V (3.2 % low) while the XEM sits at both its maximum common-mode voltage and maximum swing.
where: Frontend U1 P14/R15 (CABLE_CLK), M14/N14 (CABLE_CMDSYNC) in bank 14, B9/A9 (CABLE_SYNC) in bank 15, rail VCCO_1V5 from U4 (MPM3833C, R7 150k / R8 100k); driven from HDMI Extension Board XEM8310 bank 64 (HP, VIO1 1.8 V).
evidence: XEM output (DS931 LVDS DC table): VOCM 1.000-1.425 V, VODIFF 247/350/454 mV, so peak leg = 1.425 + 0.454/2 = 1.652 V. Frontend limit (DS181 Table 2): VCCO + 0.20 = 1.70 V at 1.50 V; crossing point 1.452 V. U4 setpoint 0.6 x (1 + 150k/100k) = 1.50 V; with VFB 591-609 mV the DC worst case is about 1.46 V, so a crossing also needs ripple or droop. Pins and standards: exports/frontend/pads.csv; inputs/frontend/V2_review_fixes/Frontend_V46_pins_V2.xdc (LVDS_25, DIFF_TERM FALSE on all six pins); inputs/hdmi/firmware_V34/fit_pins_V34.xdc (LVDS, bank 64, 1.8 V). The DS931 values come from a search summary (direct fetch failed), and the DS181 and MPM3833C values from third-party copies of the data sheets. Absolute rating is VCCO + 0.55 V (DS181 Table 4).
source: AMD UG471 v1.10 p.92 (LVDS_25 inputs in banks at another VCCO need DIFF_TERM FALSE and VIN within the data sheet); AMD DS181 v1.27 Tables 2 and 4; AMD DS931 'LVDS DC Specifications', https://docs.amd.com/r/en-US/ds931-artix-ultrascale-plus/LVDS-DC-Specifications-LVDS; MPS MPM3833C data sheet (VFB).
consequence: None expected in practice. At worst a brief, formal excursion past the recommended input limit at one corner, far below the absolute rating.
suggested_action: No hardware change. Keep VCCO_1V5 at its 1.50 V setpoint with low ripple, and confirm it at bring-up.

title: Returned CLK32MHz lines have no series resistor, so a strong ASIC driver could overshoot the FPGA input limit.
what: Each ASIC drives its 32 MHz recording clock point-to-point to an FPGA clock pin with no series resistor, and the FPGA captures data on the falling edge. Overshoot is the voltage swinging above the supply; AMD limits how far above the 1.5 V bank supply an input may go and for how long. In a linear model of the far-chip (ASIC3) path the edge stays clean, but a strong, fast driver peaks near 2.5 V, about 1 V over the bank, beyond AMD's allowance, while a 30 ohm, 1 ns driver stays under about 1.7 V. The files cannot settle this because the ASIC output drive is unknown; a probe measurement at bring-up or the ASIC designer's driver data would.
where: Far chip: ASIC3_CLK32MHz_Out from the far board (no CAD) through the near ASIC board's T_CLK32MHZ (J3.70/J4.70), FPGA-LDO Option A J4.70 to J2.35, Frontend J2.35 to U1.P4. Near chip: ASIC1 CLK32MHZ (J4.45), Option A J4.45 to J2.59, Frontend J2.59 to U1.R2. The same applies to ASIC2 and ASIC4-8.
evidence: exports/frontend/nets.csv: /ASIC3_CLK32MHz_Out J2.35-U1.P4 10.71 mm; /ASIC1_CLK32MHz_Out J2.59-U1.R2 13.99 mm. exports/ldo_a/nets.csv: ASIC3 J2.35-J4.70 18.51 mm; ASIC1 J2.59-J4.45 30.81 mm; both 2-pin, no series part. exports/asic/nets.csv: /T_CLK32MHZ J3.70-J4.70 0.48 mm; /CLK32MHZ about 4.06 mm. Model (15-60 ohm, 0.3-2 ns, 3-8 pF, far-chip path only): one mid-rail crossing in every case; peak at U1.P4 2.28-2.51 V at 15 ohm/0.3 ns, 1.82-2.05 V at 30 ohm/0.3 ns, 1.90-2.13 V at 15 ohm/1 ns (lower value for 8 pF, higher for 3 pF). Clamp diodes are not modelled; they would limit the peak but conduct current. Falling-edge capture: ASIC_REFERENCE.md line 53, historical_primary_findings.md line 12.
source: AMD DS181 v1.27.1 Table 4 (HR bank overshoot: VCCO + 0.55 V for 100 % of the unit interval, VCCO + 0.95 V for 0.24 %) and Table 8, https://docs.amd.com/api/khub/documents/iAkxxTOk96ANLJqYf2hgrQ/content; inputs/asic/ASIC_Reference/ASIC_REFERENCE.md item U03 (ASIC VOH/VOL and drive strength unknown).
consequence: Probably works. With a strong, fast ASIC driver the FPGA clock inputs would see overshoot beyond AMD's limit on every cycle.
suggested_action: At first power-up, probe one returned CLK32MHz at the Frontend J2 pad; if the peak exceeds about 2.05 V, ask the ASIC designer whether the output drive can be reduced.

title: Three head boards carry DF40s on both faces, so one face's connectors use Hirose's full two-reflow limit.
what: Hirose allows DF40 connectors at most two reflow cycles (passes through the soldering oven) and at most 0.02 mm of board warpage across a connector. FPGA-LDO A, the Option B router and the ASIC board have DF40s on both faces, so the first face's connectors see both assembly reflows and any further reflow or hot-air rework exceeds the rating. The Frontend and the Option B LDO board are also double-sided with DF40s on one face, so their DF40s also use both cycles unless their face is reflowed last.
where: FPGA-LDO A J1/J2/J3 (top), J4 (bottom); Option B router J3 (top), J4/J5 (bottom); ASIC board J4 (top), J3 (bottom); Frontend J1/J2 (bottom, 59 top parts); Option B LDO board J1/J2/J5 (top, 63 bottom parts).
evidence: Hirose DF40 catalog p21: reflow cycles 2 max; warpage 0.02 mm max at the centre relative to both connector ends. Part sides from exports/ldo_a, ldo_b_router, asic, frontend and ldo_b_ldo parts.csv. The ASIC board is 1.6 mm thick (exports/asic/board_stats.txt and inputs/asic/pcbway_fab PCB-job.gbrjob); 0.8 mm appears only as the deck's fit-model profile (inputs/system/README_2026-11-11.md line 51).
source: Hirose DF40 Series catalog, 2024, p21, https://www.hirose.com/en/product/series/DF40 (read from the LCSC copy).
consequence: Within two reflows the assembly is in spec, but any reflow or hot-air rework of these boards is outside the connector rating.
suggested_action: Tell the assembler not to give any board a third reflow and to reflow the DF40 face last on the Frontend and the Option B LDO board; do rework by hand iron only.

title: Nothing on the Frontend blocks the V6 change set: all 20 nets route together with 28 ground stacks and need no layer, outline or ball change.
what: The 12 new spare-contact lines, the 4 returned-clock swaps moved off FPGA-LDO A (8 nets) and the FE-10/FE-21 ground stacks were placed together on a copy of the board, stacks first. All 20 nets then route over the whole board in both orders. This holds whether the outer layers may carry long runs or only escapes of 1.2 mm or less, as the existing lanes do. The copy uses only the board's seven via spans, keeps the Hirose strips clean, and has 0 DRC errors and 0 unconnected items, with every plane still one piece. One ball needs care. K17 has no room for a via under it, because the CABLE_CMDSYNC LVDS pair runs 0.155 mm from its centre on L10. J1.29 therefore reaches K17 with a 1.18 mm top-layer track between BGA balls, which passes the 0.09 mm solder-mask web check.
where: Copy a review working file (not published) (sha256 ea99e3eea5bca6fc...). J1 spare contacts 29-49 to bank 14/15 balls; J2.40/J2.42 to K5/K6; swaps J1.5, J1.13, J1.56, J1.64, J2.25, J2.26, J2.35, J2.36.
source: Board rules boards/frontend/Artix_Frontend_8L_V3.kicad_dru and .kicad_pro, used unchanged. KiCad 10.0.6 'kicad-cli pcb drc --refill-zones --severity-all'. fe_candidate column of a review working file (not published) known/asic_open.json item A-P. Hirose DF40 catalogue p.8 note 3 (insulation area), https://www.hirose.com/product/download?distributor=all&type=catalogue&lang=en&series=DF40 (not re-read; 0.75-1.19 mm strip limits taken as stated in ASIC-14). Results in a review working file (not published) and out/r_esc12_*.json, out/r_all_*.json, out/post_v6_*.json.
consequence: The Frontend side of A-P can be closed in one layout change. What stays open is the FPGA-LDO A routing (no rule-respecting V12 path for most new lines), the V6 pin file, and the bank-34 decision.
suggested_action: Treat the copy as feasibility evidence only (grid-routed, not proposed copper). When the V6 layout is drawn, route by hand on these layers. For ASIC8_DATA8, keep the 1.2 mm top-layer escape at K17, or move it to a free bank-14 ball with via room (U10, U11, V11 or V14). Then run DRC with schematic parity against the V6 schematic.

title: The HDMI Extension Board does not fit a closed PC slot: too tall, no bracket holes, two ports off the bracket.
what: A standard-height PCIe card may be at most 111.15 mm tall; this board is 114.10 mm, a height inherited from BRK8310. It has no screw holes for a metal bracket, port 8 lies wholly outside the bracket opening and port 7 lies about 3.9 mm outside it. With the XEM8310 module fitted on its 5.00 mm connectors, the component side stands about 17.5 mm tall, more than one slot width (14.47 mm). None of this matters on the planned open DFR1169 adapter in enclosure V3, but it does matter in a PC case or in the closed OWC Helios 5S box that the weekly deck still lists as an off-the-shelf alternative.
where: HDMI Extension Board V37: board outline y 47.954 to 162.054 (Edge.Cuts); J616 (port 7, centre y 66.7), J617 (port 8, centre y 53.6), J610-J617 at x 67.08; left (port) edge x 64.7 to about 100 mm; MC1, MC2, MC3.
evidence: exports/hdmi/board_stats.txt: height 114.1000 mm; exports/hdmi/summary.txt: Edge.Cuts y 47.954 to 162.054; 114.10 - 111.15 = 2.95 mm over. exports/hdmi/pads.csv: the only NPTH or mechanical holes are J4 (x 104.6 to 113.6), J500, the MC1-MC3 pegs, MH2 (223.3, 131.2) and MH3 (147.8, 69.2), so none in the bracket region. exports/hdmi/parts.csv: J610-J617 from y 145.3 down to 53.6 in 13.1 mm steps; bracket opening 4.8 to 94.7 mm above the finger tip is y 157.25 to 67.35. MC1/MC2 field 'Mated height: 5.00mm'; stack 5.00 + 1.46 + 11.00 = 17.46 mm against 14.47 mm (inputs/hdmi/V35_prefab_review/ALL_FINDINGS.md lines 750-774; the 1.46 and 11.00 mm module terms were not re-read from the Opal Kelly drawing, whose PDF has no extractable text). inputs/hdmi/enclosure_V3/START_HERE.md: DFR1169 used. inputs/system/weekly_deck/START_HERE.md: Helios 5S entry with height, bracket and double width listed as open.
source: PCI Express CEM r3.0 card dimensions as cited in inputs/hdmi/V35_prefab_review/ALL_FINDINGS.md (the specification itself was not read; it is behind the PCI-SIG paywall; 111.15 mm confirmed by secondary sources). Opal Kelly XEM8310 mechanical drawing, https://docs.opalkelly.com/xem8310/specifications/.
consequence: No effect on the DFR1169 adapter in enclosure V3. In a PC case or the Helios 5S the card would need two free slots and a custom bracket, and may not fit at all.
suggested_action: Keep the 'adapter or enclosure only' use rule in the HDMI board record and name the Helios 5S as excluded until its card height, bracket and double-width limits are checked.

title: The animal's reference electrode is tied to the host PC and 12 V adapter grounds, with no isolation and no leakage rule on record.
what: The ASIC boards' J1 pin (AGND, the reference connection) joins GND at NT1 on the FPGA-LDO board. That ground runs through each HDMI cable shield to the HDMI Extension Board's DGND, which is also the ground of the USB-C/Thunderbolt link, the PCIe edge and the 12 V adapter. No board carries an isolator, so mains leakage from the host, the adapters or another instrument touching the animal can return through the animal's tissue and its reference electrode. Many research rigs accept this, while commercial systems sell isolation for subject safety; the project has no rule either way.
where: ASIC V4 boards J1.1 (/AGND) at (144.875, 68.28); NT1 on FPGA-LDO A (100.58, 121.0) and on the Option B LDO board; Frontend J3 shell and GND pins; HDMI board J610-J617 shells to DGND, J500 (USB-C) A1/A12/B1/B12, J6 PCIe edge, J4.2.
evidence: exports/asic_top/pads.csv and asic_bottom/pads.csv: J1.1 = /AGND. exports/ldo_a/parts.csv: NT1 is the only AGND-GND tie. exports/hdmi/connectors.csv: J500 A1/A12/B1/B12 = DGND; J4.2 = DGND. exports/hdmi/parts.csv: no isolator, optocoupler or transformer. inputs/hdmi/enclosure_V3/START_HERE.md lines 39-49: one USB-C (Thunderbolt) link to the computer and 12 V on J4, with the adapter fed from the board's 12 V. inputs/system/weekly_deck/START_HERE.md line 67: stacks sit on a sheep's skull. A search of inputs/ for 'isolat', 'leakage' and '60601' found no rule.
source: TDT PZ5M documentation, Overview ('full biomedical isolation for subject safety'), https://tdt.com/docs/hardware/pz5m-medically-isolated-neurodigitizer/ . IEC 60601-1 patient-leakage limits for type CF applied parts, 10 uA normal and 50 uA single fault (from memory, not re-read). Engineering judgement.
consequence: Under a fault in the host or a supply, mains-frequency leakage current can flow through the animal and its reference electrode, and nobody is set to check it.
suggested_action: Record a rig rule: either accept non-isolated operation (earthed host, one earth point, no other mains equipment touching the animal), or add isolation (for example an optical Thunderbolt link and an isolated 12 V supply). Measure leakage from J1 to earth once with the full rig.

title: A bench supply hot-connected to the Frontend's TP14 can ring VIN_5V to 7.5-8 V, while cable hot-plug stays below about 5.6 V.
what: FE-19 left the cable hot-plug overshoot to a measurement. A circuit model that includes the port switch shows the overshoot is small. The TPS2553 limits its current within about 2 us, long before the cable inductance and the Frontend's input capacitors can ring, and the cable resistance damps the rest. The real exposure is a stiff bench supply clipped onto TP14 while it is already on, because nothing then limits the current.
where: Frontend VIN_5V: J3.19, C206/C207 (22 uF 10 V 0805), C209 (100 nF), U16 MPM3833C, TP14. HDMI board: U701 TPS2553 (R711 37.4k) and C721 (1 uF) at J610.19.
evidence: Time-step model in a review working file (not published) Inputs: U700 at 5.02 V; TPS2553 at 85-135 mOhm with current held to IOS 0.764 A after 2 us; C721 1 uF; cable loop 0.1-2.5 Ohm and 0.2-4 uH (assumed); Frontend input 8-44 uF after DC-bias loss (assumed). Results: peak VIN_5V 5.02-5.24 V; 5.50 V with a 50 % current-limit overshoot; 5.63 V with a 5 us limit response. Only a 10-20 us response with a 0.1 Ohm loop reaches 7.1-8.0 V. A 1.8 m 34 AWG power wire alone is about 1.5 Ohm (0.86 Ohm/m, V35 review), which is overdamped (5.02 V). Stiff source through 0.05-0.1 Ohm leads, 0.5-1 uH, into 15 uF: 7.5-8.0 V.
source: TI TPS2553 SLVS841G sec. 6.5 p.6-7 (rDS(on) 85/95/135 mOhm; tIOS 2 us typical) and equation 1 p.16 (IOS maximum), https://www.ti.com/lit/ds/symlink/tps2553.pdf . MPS MPM3833C Rev 1.0 p.3 (6.5 V absolute maximum, as recorded in FE-19). Linear Technology AN88, ceramic input capacitor hot-plug overshoot (from memory, not re-read; analog.com timed out), https://www.analog.com/media/en/technical-documentation/application-notes/an88f.pdf .
consequence: The cable case needs no part change. The bench-supply case can damage U16, which feeds every Frontend rail.
suggested_action: Keep FE-19's scope capture only as a confirmation. Add to the bring-up order: connect a bench supply to TP14 before switching it on, with its current limit set to about 0.8 A.

title: With the V4 ASIC boards, firmware must still follow the chip numbering, the reversed DATA order and the shared CLKH and control lines, but SPI data is now one DL/DR pair per chip, the far boards have their own SPI clock, latch and returned clock (pins 72, 70, 62 and 12), and the XDC records none of this and has no clock constraints.
what: Facts the FPGA design needs, read from the files. ASIC numbers: on the FPGA-LDO underside port (J4), ASIC1 = near board U01_BCD1, ASIC2 = near U01_BCD2, ASIC3 = far U01_BCD1, ASIC4 = far U01_BCD2; on the top-side port (J3), ASIC5/6 near and ASIC7/8 far, same order. Within every chip, DATAL<4..1> arrive as DATA1..4 and DATAR<4..1> as DATA5..8. Each chip's returned clock is on the P side of an SRCC/MRCC clock-capable pair in the same bank as its data: R2, D13, P4, E16, R3, R16, N3, P15 for ASIC1..8; ASIC1/3/5/7 in bank 34, ASIC2/4 in bank 15, ASIC6/8 in bank 14. SPI: stream STIM_CHIP1 loads ASIC1 and ASIC3, CHIP2 loads ASIC2 and ASIC4, CHIP3 loads ASIC5 and ASIC7, CHIP4 loads ASIC6 and ASIC8 (stream number and ASIC number differ for 3 and 4); BOARD1_SPI_CLK clocks ASIC1-4, BOARD3_SPI_CLK ASIC5-8, one SPI_LATCH for all eight. CLKH: BOARD1_CLK to ASIC1-4, BOARD3_CLK to ASIC5-8. STIM_EN, STIM_START, STIM_CLK, STIM_CHB (both CHBL and CHBR), CHIP_RESET (RRST_DIGITAL and RST_DRIVER), FE_RESET (RST_FEL and RST_FER) and IMP_TST go to all eight. No FPGA pin sees any DISC_OUT; AC_IN is only a 10k to AGND and TP7. The XDC has pin locations only: no create_clock or input-delay constraints for the eight returned clocks.
where: inputs/frontend/V2_review_fixes/Frontend_V46_pins_V2.xdc; FPGA-LDO A / router J3/J4; V3 boards U01_BCD1/U01_BCD2.
evidence: W/a review working file (not published) output (per-chip pad -> connector pin -> FPGA net -> ball -> bank), package file a review working file (not published) (AMD xc7a35tcsg325, 12/3/2013). Example: ASIC1 DATAL<4> pin 79 -> ASIC1_DATA1 ball U2; DATAR<1> pin 37 -> ASIC1_DATA8 ball L3; CLK32MHZ pin 45 -> R2 IO_L13P_T2_MRCC_34. LDO A R6 10k ASIC_AC_IN to AGND, TP7.
source: AMD 7 Series FPGAs Clocking Resources UG472 (clock-capable inputs; not re-read); ASIC_REFERENCE.md section 3 (capture on each chip's own returned clock).
consequence: A decoder that assumes DATA1 = DATAL<1>, or that STIM_CHIP3 is ASIC3, will scramble channels or configure the wrong chips.
suggested_action: Write this map into the Frontend firmware notes (or as comments in the XDC) and add clock constraints for the eight returned clocks before the first build.
v2note: The claim that R2S-09 is wrong was not upheld in full by the second check: Holds in part. V4 netlists: near chips use SPI pins 57/59 and 23/25, CLK 63, LATCH 61, CLK32 45/19. Far chips use 66/68 and 16/18, CLK 72, LATCH 70, CLK32 62/12. So STIM_CHIP1-4 reach only ASIC1/2/5/6, each BOARD1/3_SPI_CLK reaches two chips and SPI_LATCH_SHARED four. Far clocks land on R7, B17, L4 and U16, none MRCC/SRCC. Still true: chip numbering, reversed DATA, CLKH split, shared controls, no DISC_OUT, no clock constraints. The XDC header still claims CC clocks. See SYS-64.

title: The intended GT pair inversion (Frontend TXPOLARITY = 1) is not noted in either FPGA constraint file.
what: The transceiver (GT) pair is swapped on purpose between the Frontend and the HDMI Extension Board on all eight ports, so with a straight cable the bits arrive inverted. The plan is to undo this by setting TXPOLARITY = 1 (a transmit-side bit inversion) in the Frontend transceiver. This is written in a dated V42 note box on the Frontend schematic with a citation, in the title block and in the HDMI V35/V36 records, but not in Frontend_V46_pins_V2.xdc or fit_pins_V34.xdc, which firmware authors will start from. TXPOLARITY is set in the transceiver wizard or HDL, not in the XDC, so a comment there is only a reminder.
where: Frontend J3.3 = GTP_TX0_N (U1 H1), J3.5 = GTP_TX0_P (U1 H2). HDMI Extension Board: J610-J617 pin 3 through C745/C747/.../C759 to MC3 GTY RXP, pin 5 to RXN.
evidence: exports/frontend/netlist.xml: GTP_TX0_N = J3.3 (pin function TX0_REC_P_3) + U1.H1 (MGTPTXN0_216); GTP_TX0_P = J3.5 + U1.H2. exports/hdmi/netlist.xml: MGT_RXP0_224 = J610.3 + C745.1 + U801; Net-(MC3-MGT_RXP0_224) = C745.2 + MC3.1; same pattern on all 16 capacitors C745-C760 and MC3 pins 1-15 and 41-55. No 'POLARITY' in Frontend_V46_pins_V2.xdc, fit_pins_V34.xdc, fit_pins_V34_sync.xdc or header_pins_V34.xdc; Frontend_V46_pins_V2.xdc line 120 lists 'GTP TX0 H1/H2' as not constrained. The Frontend schematic V42 note flags TXPOLARITY = 1 in every Frontend bitstream, including IBERT, as unverified. inputs/hdmi/V35_prefab_review/ALL_FINDINGS.md lines 248-251; inputs/hdmi/V36_prefab_fixes/START_HERE.md line 72.
source: AMD UG482 7 Series FPGAs GTP Transceivers User Guide, TX polarity control (p.106, as cited on the Frontend schematic), and UG578 UltraScale Architecture GTY Transceivers (RXPOLARITY); not re-read for this review. Engineering judgement.
consequence: If the inversion is missed or applied twice, the link fails comma alignment at bring-up; it shows at once in IBERT and needs no hardware change.
suggested_action: Add one comment line to Frontend_V46_pins_V2.xdc and to the XEM fit_pins file: Frontend TXPOLARITY = 1, XEM RXPOLARITY = 0.

title: Each stack has a one-way transceiver lane and no reset line, so recovery needs firmware or a manual switch.
what: Each cable carries one transceiver pair (a multi-gigabit serial lane), from the Frontend to the XEM only; the Frontend's receive pairs are grounded. The cable also carries JTAG (the programming and debug port) but no reset or PROGRAM line, and JTAG reaches one port at a time, chosen only by hand on rotary switch SW600. All eight port power switches also share one enable. A hung Frontend can therefore be recovered only by a command its firmware still decodes, by turning SW600 and sending a JTAG reprogram, or by a whole-system power cycle, and updating the flash on eight Frontends takes eight switch changes.
where: Frontend U1 MGTPRX0-3 (E4/E3, A4/A3, C4/C3, G4/G3) on GND; Frontend J3 pins 3/5 GTP_TX0, 2/15/17/18 JTAG. HDMI Extension Board MC3 bank 224/226 TX pins unconnected, bank 224 RX0 to J610 pins 3/5 via C745; SW600 (SEL_0..SEL_8, pull-ups R620-R628) to U610-U618 pin 20; PORT_ENABLE = U700.13 to U701-U708 EN.
evidence: exports/frontend/netlist.xml: all four GTP RX pairs on GND; J3 has no reset or PROGRAM pin. exports/hdmi/netlist.xml: MC3 pins 2-16 and 42-56 'unconnected-(MC3-MGT_TX...)'; MC3 pins 22-36 (bank 225 TX) go to the PCIe edge J6 through C13-C20, and bank 225 RX also goes to J6; SEL_0..SEL_8 connect only to SW600, R620-R628 and U610-U618 (no FPGA control). The receiver's lock time must come from the XEM8310's UltraScale+ data sheet (DS931); the DS181 Table 55 figure (2.3 x 10^6 UI, 0.92 ms at 2.5 Gb/s) is for the Artix-7 GTP and does not apply to the receiver.
source: Engineering judgement; AMD DS931 (Artix UltraScale+ transceiver lock time) for bring-up timing.
consequence: Field recovery and flash updates need someone at the switch. Link bring-up must be designed one-way: the Frontend sends idle characters after configuration, the XEM locks, and the XEM reports lock back over the LVDS command pair.
suggested_action: Define a command-channel 'reconfigure' (IPROG) and a link-status reply in firmware before bring-up; accept the manual JTAG switch for now.

title: The Frontend pin file leaves drive strength and slew rate of the shared ASIC outputs on Vivado defaults.
what: The seven FPGA outputs shared by all eight ASICs (latch, stimulation clock, board clocks, SPI clocks, reset) have only a pin and an I/O standard in the pin file, so Vivado uses its defaults: 12 mA drive and SLOW slew (edge speed). Each runs about 117 mm through three boards and three DF40 contacts with no series resistor. In a simple lossless line model the edges are clean at the defaults, and also with a faster 0.6 ns, 20 ohm edge even at 8 nH per DF40 contact. A double crossing of mid-rail on SPI_LATCH_SHARED, which could latch the ASIC shift registers twice, appeared only in the harshest corner (0.3 ns, 15 ohm edge, 8 nH per contact), so nothing is wrong as drawn; writing the setting explicitly guards against a later change.
where: Frontend FPGA Board U1: D11 SPI_LATCH_SHARED, B11 STIM_CLK_SHARED, G16/V17 BOARD1_CLK/BOARD3_CLK, D10/V8 SPI_CLK, C9 CHIP_RESET_SHARED; inputs/frontend/V2_review_fixes/Frontend_V46_pins_V2.xdc lines 91-108; FPGA-LDO Option A J3/J4 pins 7, 53, 61, 63, 71.
evidence: Frontend_V46_pins_V2.xdc: 0 DRIVE or SLEW lines; lines 91 (BOARD1_CLK G16), 98 (SPI_LATCH_SHARED D11), 108 (STIM_CLK_SHARED B11) have only PACKAGE_PIN and IOSTANDARD LVCMOS15. Topology: exports/frontend/nets.csv SPI_LATCH_SHARED 12.23 mm; exports/ldo_a/nets.csv J2.48/J3.61/J4.61/R18.1, 27.40 mm, no series part; exports/asic/nets.csv /SPI_LATCH 20.16 mm, 4 vias. exports/ldo_a/pads.csv: J4 pin 61 is 4.16 mm and pin 7 is 8.2 mm from the nearest GND contact. Re-run of the model with 2 pF loads: SPI_LATCH at 0.3 ns/15 ohm gives a 0.046 V back-step with one crossing at 5 nH and 0.097 V with two crossings at 8 nH; at 0.6 ns/20 ohm and 8 nH, no back-step; STIM_CLK 0.052/0.073 V with one crossing; BOARD1_CLK never stepped back. DS181 Table 17: LVCMOS15 S12 and S16 delays equal, F12 about 0.23 ns faster, so a 0.3 ns FAST edge is likely pessimistic.
source: AMD UG912 v2022.1 (DRIVE pp. 216-217, default 12; SLEW p. 381, default SLOW), https://www.xilinx.com/support/documents/sw_manuals/xilinx2022_1/ug912-vivado-properties.pdf; AMD DS181 v1.27.1 Table 8 note 4 and Table 17, https://docs.amd.com/api/khub/documents/iAkxxTOk96ANLJqYf2hgrQ/content. Not checked against Artix-7 IBIS models or UG471. Model limits: linear source without clamp diodes, same lumped inductance on every DF40 contact, far ASIC board (no CAD) assumed equal to the near board, ASIC latch edge sensitivity unknown (ASIC reference U05).
consequence: Nothing fails as drawn. If firmware later sets SLEW FAST or a higher drive on these pins and the contact inductance is near the pessimistic end, the ASICs could latch configuration twice, which would look like random configuration errors.
suggested_action: Add explicit 'DRIVE 8 SLEW SLOW' (or 12/SLOW) to the seven shared FPGA-to-ASIC outputs in the pin file; an IBIS run on SPI_LATCH_SHARED would confirm the margin if wanted.

title: The relayed start-up order loads SPI before CLKH starts, but the only recorded working firmware ran CLKH continuously and clocked its SPI engine from the returned clock, which exists only while CLKH runs.
what: The relayed designer answer is: send SPI, reset the digital and analog sections, then start the recording clock. The original slides say the FPGA sends CLKH when recording starts. The historical four-lane firmware instead sent CLKH all the time, and ran its SPI engine and its two-cycle reset pulses on the returned clock (CLK32MHZ), which the ASIC produces only while CLKH runs. A Frontend design ported from that firmware would have no SPI clock before CLKH starts. If the relayed order is strict, stimulation tables cannot be reloaded during recording without stopping CLKH.
where: Frontend firmware: the SPI engine for 8 DL/DR pairs, BOARD1/3_SPI_CLK and the V6 top SPI clocks, CHIP_RESET (C9) and FE_RESET (D8). CLKH on BOARD1_CLK (G16) and BOARD3_CLK (V17); the eight returned clocks.
evidence: inputs/asic/ASIC_Reference/ASIC_REFERENCE.md line 67: order is SPI, then resets, then start recording clock. inputs/asic/ASIC_Reference/logic_primary_extraction.json slide 13: the FPGA sends 'CLK32MHz_In' to start the recording. inputs/asic/ASIC_Reference/rtl_primary_findings.md: the four-lane top connects the SPI engine to the returned clock (top_4lane_framed.v:269-277), reset pulses are two returned-clock cycles, and every historical top drives CLKH continuously (16 MHz).
source: inputs/asic/ASIC_Reference/ASIC_REFERENCE.md section 4 and item U05; inputs/asic/ASIC_Reference/rtl_primary_findings.md; inputs/asic/ASIC_Reference/logic_primary_extraction.json (slide 13).
consequence: Either the chips cannot be configured before recording starts, or the relayed order is not followed. Experiments that change tables during recording may need recording gaps.
suggested_action: Clock the Frontend SPI engine and reset pulses from the 32 MHz cable clock or Y2, not from a returned clock. Ask the ASIC designer whether SPI loading and resets need CLKH stopped, and whether tables may be reloaded while recording.

title: None of the 88 ASIC-to-FPGA input lines has a pull resistor on any board or in the pin file, so a missing or unpowered ASIC board leaves its returned clocks and data inputs floating.
what: Each ASIC drives 11 lines to the FPGA: 8 data, READ, SYNC and the returned clock. On the Frontend and FPGA-LDO boards these are bare two-pin nets, and the pin file sets no PULLDOWN. When a board is not fitted (for example during a staged bring-up with one ASIC board per port) or its rails are off, 22 FPGA inputs per missing board float, including two returned clocks. A floating clock input can toggle on noise and run capture logic on garbage, and floating input buffers draw extra current.
where: inputs/frontend/V2_review_fixes/Frontend_V46_pins_V2.xdc lines 3-90 (88 ASIC inputs, LVCMOS15). FPGA-LDO A nets /ASICn_DATA1-8, /ASICn_READ, /ASICn_SYNC and /ASICn_CLK32MHz_Out.
evidence: exports/ldo_a/netlist.xml and exports/frontend/netlist.xml: all 88 ASIC input nets contain only connector and U1 pins. Frontend_V46_pins_V2.xdc: no PULLDOWN, PULLUP or PULLTYPE. DS181 v1.27.1 Table 3: internal pull-down 68-330 uA (stated at VIN = 3.3 V); pad capacitance 8 pF.
source: AMD DS181 v1.27.1 Table 3 p.3, https://docs.amd.com/v/u/en-US/ds181_Artix_7_Data_Sheet; engineering judgement.
consequence: Absent chips produce spurious frames at bring-up, which may be forwarded over the GT lane, and fault finding gets harder.
suggested_action: Add PULLDOWN TRUE to the 88 ASIC inputs in the pin file; an ASIC push-pull output easily overrides a weak pull-down. Have firmware check each returned clock's frequency before using that chip's data.

title: On the FPGA-LDO underside port the near board mates through its J4 plug, not its J3, so the "top" board hangs lowest and its J3 receptacle is the open end.
what: FPGA-LDO A J4 and router J4 are DF40C-80DS receptacles on the bottom face, so the board under them must offer a plug: the near board hangs face up and mates with its J4, and the far board mates its J4 into the near board's J3. This works electrically because both V3 boards pass all 80 pins from J3 to J4. But the round-2 description (near board plugs in with its J3; the far board's J4 has nothing above it) holds only for the top-side port. On the underside port the far ("Top") board is the lowest board in the stack, its J4 must be fitted and its J3 receptacle is the exposed end; on the top-side port its J4 plug is the exposed end. Both free ends carry +10 V and -10 V on pins 36/54.
where: FPGA-LDO A and router: J3 DF40C-80DP top, J4 DF40C-80DS bottom, both at (99.783, 113.51). V3 boards: J3 DS on B.Cu, J4 DP on F.Cu. Option A levels (z = 0 at LDO A bottom): near -3.10 to -1.50, far -6.20 to -4.60 on the underside port.
evidence: exports/ldo_a/parts.csv and exports/ldo_b_router/parts.csv (connector types and sides); V3 dumps; ASIC J4 to LDO A / router J4 fit 180 deg, 0.185 mm, pin n on pin n (W/a review working file (not published)); W/a review working file (not published)
source: Engineering judgement.
consequence: Assembly notes, a cost-down that leaves one connector off the top board, or a cover for the open connector would be wrong for one of the two ports if written from the J3-port picture.
suggested_action: Use near/far, not bottom/top, in assembly and firmware notes; fit both connectors on the far board, or make one variant per port; choose a cover for the exposed plug or receptacle.

title: The only ASIC-board Gerber set in the workspace is an older one-chip design with no pass-through lanes.
what: Gerbers are the files a factory uses to make a board. The only Gerber set for the ASIC board was made on 21 June 2026 from an older design with one chip and connectors J1/J2. The two-chip ASIC board reviewed here (two ASICs, J3/J4, pass-through lanes) has no Gerber set anywhere in the workspace. Boards made from the June set cannot sit in a stacked pair with the pass-through pin map.
where: inputs/asic/pcbway_fab/*.gbr (same files as boards/asic/board/pcbway.zip and inside Board-1024.zip); reviewed design boards/asic PCB.kicad_pcb (U01_BCD1/U01_BCD2, J3/J4).
evidence: pcbway_fab: 17 Gerbers, TF.CreationDate 2026-06-21T18:35, KiCad 9.0.7; component attributes name only J1, J2, U01_BCD1 and capacitors; 45 unique net names, none containing 'T_' or '(2)'. exports/asic/nets.csv: 97 rows (one is the no-net row), 22 containing T_ and 25 containing (2). Board-1024.zip: its PCB.kicad_pcb (26 Jul 2026) has no U01_BCD2 and only J1/J2, and its Gerbers are the same June set. No Gerber containing U01_BCD2 was found in the Desktop workspace.
source: Engineering judgement.
consequence: Any ASIC boards already made or ordered may not match the two-chip pass-through pin map that both FPGA-LDO options assume.
suggested_action: Confirm with the ASIC designer which design files the existing or ordered ASIC boards were made from.
